confirmed.consequence: The keyboard user reverses the product's signature gesture and is dropped at the top of the document; their next Tab restarts the whole surface. Undo is the gesture that makes a person brave enough to try the seam at all, and here it is the gesture that costs them their place.
confirmed.fix: On the seam's undo, restore focus to the control that opened it — `[data-act="send"]` on the peeled sheet if still mounted, otherwise the note body the words were peeled from — the same restore the Tasks tick path already performs.
confirmed.assertion: On notes.seam at 1440x960 and 390x844: press Send, then Ctrl+Z; `document.activeElement` is inside `.desk` and is not `document.body`.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED. Every observable claim reproduces verbatim, and driving it turned up a second broken path the seat missed, which makes it worse rather than weaker.

Driven in chromium at 1440x960 against file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.seam:
- Pressing `[data-act="send"]` lands focus on `BUTTON.deskFactLink[data-act="open-task"]`, aria-label "Open in Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when. Your note stays here." Exactly as stated.
- `Ctrl+Z` announces "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." and `document.activeElement === document.body` — true, measured directly, stable at 600ms.
- Same session, tasks.board: focus the `.tick` ("Mark done"), Enter, `Ctrl+Z` — focus is back on the same `.tick`, aria-label back to "Mark done", announcement "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is back in the to do column." The asymmetry the seat draws is exact.

This is not a re-raise of `undo-drops-focus-on-body` / `undo-drops-focus-to-body` (r1). Those were closed by the narrow guard in `doUndo` at _gate-suite.html:11492-11497, which claims focus ONLY when `document.activeElement.closest(".undo")` — its own comment says it is "deliberately narrow… claims focus only when the control that was pressed is the one about to be removed." On the seam the control about to be removed is `[data-act="open-task"]`, which is not in the strip, so the guard never fires, `paint()` drops the node, and nothing catches the keyboard. The r1 fix is intact; this path was never covered by it.

WHAT THE SEAT MISSED, and it is the more damaging half. The drawn Undo button fails identically. I focused and pressed `.undoAct` ("Undo Ctrl Z") in the strip on notes.seam: focus lands on BODY too. Cause: the inStrip branch sets `refocus = {kind:"field", sel: phone.matches ? ".phoneField" : ".topField"}`, and I measured `.topField` to be ABSENT in seam state at 1440 (present in notes.notebook, absent on the seam). The consumer at 13977-14031 does `const field = mount.querySelector(refocus.sel); if (field) …` and then unconditionally `refocus = null`, so a miss silently consumes the branch and skips the `caret` fallback in the `else if` beneath it — precisely the hazard the r1 comment warned about ("a stored destination breaks the cross-room case… would consume refocus on a null target and skip the caret fallback"). It is not hypothetical; it is live on the seam today, on both undo affordances.

So on the one protected object the whole suite exists to justify, both ways back are dead for the keyboard. Recovery costs a Tab from the top: after undo, the next Tab lands on `.filingBtn` ("This note is about The house. Change it."), nowhere near the sheet the person was working.

Severity: blocking, and I am setting it there deliberately rather than at defect. The undo transaction itself is honest — the card is removed, the announcement is right — but the keyboard model this product advertises and demonstrates one product over is not implemented on the seam, and r1 closed two findings of exactly this class, which is the panel's own precedent that this is must-fix rather than polish.

The fix is directionally right and its targets exist — I verified that after undo `[data-act="send"]` IS remounted at 1440 (the revert sets `peeling = note.id`, `sentTask = null`), and `.readBody` is mounted alongside it. Confirming, with the fix sharpened on three points it leaves under-specified.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Keep the seat's destination — it is right and matches the Tasks tick precedent — but implement it as an ordered fallback, cover the review branch, and cover the strip button too.

1. Give `offerUndo` a fourth argument: an ordered array of selectors to try after the revert. The seam's two call sites (12260 review, 12303 desk) pass their own. Do NOT pass a single `refocus = {kind:"act", sel:'[data-act="send"]'}` — the consumer at 13978-13980 no-ops on a miss and then nulls `refocus`, skipping the caret fallback, which is exactly how the strip path is already broken today.

2. Order matters and must be evaluated in priority order, not as a CSS selector list (a list picks first-in-document-order, not first-in-preference):
   - desk (12303): `['[data-act="send"]', '.readBody']`
   - review (12260): `['.handBody']` — `[data-act="send"]` is NOT remounted there. The revert at 12261-12266 does not restore `peeling`, so `taskWording` is empty and the peel sheet is gone. The file's existing idiom for this is `state === "review" ? ".handBody" : ".readBody"` (see 11981, 12145, 12183); reuse it rather than hardcoding `.readBody`.

3. Make the passed chain take precedence over the existing `inStrip` branch when it is present, so pressing the drawn `.undoAct` button lands in the same place as Ctrl+Z. Leave the `inStrip` → `.topField`/`.phoneField` guess as the fallback only for call sites that pass no chain — and while in there, harden the consumer: after a `kind:"act"` or `kind:"field"` miss, fall through to the `caret` branch instead of nulling `refocus` unconditionally. That one-line change also repairs the strip path on the seam for free.
confirmed.breaks:
Plausibly breaks: (a) the cross-room case r1 explicitly protected — undoing from inside search, where neither `.topField` nor `[data-act="send"]` exists, must still leave the caret in `#q`; a chain that ends without a match must fall through to `caret`, not swallow it. (b) The 30s expiry path at 11456-11473 sets its own focus recovery independently; a chain must not fight it, and the expiry recovery has the same `.topField`-absent-on-the-seam bug, so it is worth fixing in the same pass. REFUTED — the finding is factually wrong about two of the three states it names, and its fix would damage them. The kernel that survives is real but small.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper`, scoped to `[data-app="timeline"]` — note a bare `document.querySelector('.dock')` returns Notes' hidden dock, which is probably how the seat got some of its numbers):

- `.app.sheet` is Timeline's scroller. At 1440x960 owner-flight: scrollHeight 1173, clientHeight **924**, max scrollTop 249 (the seat's "864/1173" is wrong; 864 is not a number this element has at any width I drove). At scrollTop 249 `.word` is at y=-191 and the whole `.b-bar` — Add a moment / Preview / Get the link — is at y=-85. At 768x1024 max scroll is 1581 and the bar sits at -1393. That part is real.

WHY IT IS REFUTED:

1. **"all three Timeline states" is false, and the two it is false about are the two the fix would break.** `desk` and `phone` are not Orla's app. `src/timeline.js` STATES names them "Received · desk" and "Received · phone" — the couple's view of a shared plan link. There is no unpinned head there to scroll away: `src/across.css:422` sets `[data-app="timeline"]:not([data-state^="owner"]) .tlHead { display: none }` under a written decision — "Studio chrome on a page a couple opens from a link is a decision, not a freebie. The wordmark is the OWNER's; a guest gets the artifact and the colophon." Driven: `.tlHead` computes `display:none` and measures 0px in both, and `timeline.phone` has exactly one tabbable in the entire document. The finding read a deliberate, commented exclusion as an omission.

2. **The fix therefore proposes putting Orla's account tile and "Add a moment" on a page Mara and Finn open from a link.** That is not polish; it hands the guest the owner's chrome and a verb that acts on the owner's plan. It also contradicts the fixture's own framing ("on a page a couple opens from a link it is provenance for a stranger, not chrome") and would put a dead search field carrying Tasks' sentence — "Search comes with the other views" — on a surface where "the other views" means nothing to the reader. A fourth honest door in the wrong voice.

3. **The honest-door premise underneath the dock half is false.** Home, Inbox, Help and the account tile are not lost on Timeline: `.rail` carries `data-rail="home|inbox|help|me"`, all `aria-disabled` with their not-here-yet sentences, all arrow-reachable inside the roving group. Nothing is unreachable; the dock is not carrying anything Timeline lacks except a search field that does not exist.

4. **The scroll-boundary half of the fix is unnecessary and the riskiest thing in the finding.** Timeline already sticks content against this exact scroller — `src/timeline.css:1965`, `.b-stick { position: sticky; top: var(--gap-section) }`. refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces verbatim, and must not be discarded. The load-bearing half of the fix, as written, would replace an honest failure with a lying one.

DRIVEN (chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight). Every number and every sentence in the observation is exact.
- Run A: `.b-item:has-text("Menu tasting") .b-grab` → the stepper whose aria-label is literally "Move a week later" → Done. `.b-undo` = 1130x54, data-empty="false", text "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days later.UndoCtrl Z". Ctrl+Z → row back to "16 days away … Sat 1 Aug". Correct.
- Run B: same, then `[data-layout-to="down"]`. `.b-undo` = 0x0, data-empty="true", sentence gone. Ctrl+Z → row still "23 days away … Sat 8 Aug". The only live region in the document holds "The measure runs down the page." and nothing else.
- Rested Ctrl+Z on Timeline: silent. Tasks, driven the same way: `#say` reads "Nothing left to undo." (src/tasks.js:1592). The asymmetry is real.

MECHANISM (src/timeline.js:2937): `render()` opens with `history.length = 0`, and the orientation handler at :2949-2957 calls `C.mount()`, which empties the host (`host.textContent = ""`, :141) and re-runs `render`. So the stack is not merely detached — it is cleared. Worth telling the founder: this is wider than orientation. A spine glance does the same. I marked the live `.b-item` node, pressed `[data-rail="notes"]` then `[data-rail="timeline"]`, and got `same node? false, connected? false` — the Timeline is torn down and rebuilt on a rail trip, the strip empties, and Ctrl+Z is dead. That contradicts the locked architecture's own sentence, "none ever torn down, so nothing a person was doing is lost when they glance at another," more sharply than the orientation case does.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. "Carry the pending undo record across the orientation re-render … and keep the strip's sentence with it" names only the record and the sentence. It does not touch what the record actually holds. Every one of the five `remember()` call sites captures DOM: :1573 `undo: function(){ setAway(root, item, from) }` plus a `focus` closure over `pressed`; :1601 closes over `group` and `item`; :1633 over `event.target`; :1762 over `root` and `item`; :1930/:1966 likewise. After the remount those nodes are detached. `setAway` (:1310-1386) writes `record.date = iso` — the record is shared and persistent — but paints only the passed `item` and queries the passed `root` for `.b-step`, `#b-edit-date`, `.b-ceiling`, then `place(measureEl)` on a detached parent. So preserving `history` verbatim gives you: Ctrl+Z after the switch clears the strip, reports success, silently reverts the underlying record, and leaves the visible measure reading Sat 8 Aug / "23 days away" until some later remount. That is precisely the defect this file's own comment at :1191-1194 records as already paid for once — "a delete left a live offer to restore a row that no longer existed, and pressing it restored nothing and cleared itself as though it had worked." The fix as written re-opens it, and upgrades a defect into a misleading one.

The second half is right in substance and wrong in its address. There is no Timeline-owned `.sr` region: `[data-app="timeline"] .sr` returns 0 nodes, and the document's only `[aria-live]` is `#say.sr`, the suite's polite region, which is what `window.__SUITE.say()` writes and what the r1 fix `orientation-switch-says-nothing-on-desk` deliberately moved this product's announcements onto (see the comment at :2966-2975: `.b-live` belongs to the owner surface and the guest desk has none). Name the suite region, not a Timeline one.

SEVERITY. Defect, not blocking or misleading. Nothing false stands on screen at the moment of failure — the strip withdraws its own offer rather than continuing to advertise a key that is dead, and the move is reversible by hand with −7. But it is a real defect at this bar: a control whose entire job is which way the measure runs destroys the reversal of a change made one second earlier, and the silent Ctrl+Z means a screen-reader owner cannot tell the difference between "undone" and "nothing happened". On the spine-trip evidence it edges toward blocking against the suite's own "none ever torn down" claim; I am holding it at defect because the offer is honestly retracted.

- The Tasks comparison is correct too: ticking a card logs one event only, `sel:"sr"` → "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company done. 1. `aria-hidden="true"` on `.undo` puts a focusable control outside the accessibility tree. `.undoAct` is `<button>`, `tabIndex 0`, no ancestor aria-hidden — I measured it. ARIA forbids this (axe `aria-hidden-focus`, WCAG 4.1.2): the keyboard user still tabs into it and hears nothing. The file itself proves the strip is a designed focus destination — `:11464` reads `if (strip.contains(document.activeElement))` before removing it. The fix would trade a repeated announcement for a silent button, and at ≤720 (`:3948`) that strip is the undo affordance.
2. "let `.sr` carry ... its window" moves the worse half of the bug into the shared region. `#say` is one region for the entire suite (`:7952-7962`, "One region for the suite"). A running number in it either ticks — and then `#say` fires 29 times and clobbers every Tasks/Timeline announcement made in that window — or it freezes, which is the exact lie this file already fixed once (`:11407`: "printed a thirty-second promise in one place and expired the strip silently at ten in another").

It is at the top of that class, though, because Notes is unusable by ear for thirty seconds after the suite's signature gesture.

Verbing only the `crossed` branch leaves one component printing a labelled time in one list and a bare time meaning something different in the other, three rows away. More fundamentally, the fix is structurally void: the origin-to-moment distance is locked, so every pixel lifted off the hero lifts the origin *and* the moment by the same amount — you must delete 178px from everything above the measure at 390 to move the moment one screen's worth. The finding proposes a **96px ::after gradient on opacity gated at > 4** for the same role: a second size, a second mechanism, a second threshold. That is the "N treatments for one role" class this panel has refuted repeatedly here (three-eyebrows-for-one-role, keycap-three-treatments, eyebrow-drawn-three-ways). The 96px is borrowed from Tasks, where the number is justified by card width ("past ~104 it starts eating a legible card"), a reason that does not transfer to a vertical edge.

At most a refinement: the shipped law deliberately reserves the fade for a *pane* that hides something unexpectedly, and at ≤768 the sheet is the page, whose bottom edge is the fold every reader already understands. Linear, Stripe and Vercel do not gradient the bottom of the document on a phone.

REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, reproduces exactly, and must NOT be discarded — do not let this verdict close it.

Driven at file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.voice, 1440x960 and 768/1280/1920, the two caps are the only `kbd` in the suite carrying a second dim: `Esc` computes `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)` with `opacity: 0.55`, `Ctrl Enter` computes `rgb(17,17,17)` with `opacity: 0.55`, both 11px/600, both inside `.darkAct` (notes.css:950). Compositing them gives rgb(98) on #111111 = 3.10:1 and rgb(124) on #ffffff = 4.17:1 — the seat's 3.05 and 4.23 to within rounding. _gate.out prints the same two, by name, in its own words: "contrast · 8 OPEN, named and handed to the panel · kbd \"Esc\" @notes.voice 768x1024 — on screen, rendered 3.05:1, needs 4.5 | kbd \"Ctrl Enter\" ... 4.23:1", and "the residue is OPEN, not passed". Nothing guards them. That is a genuine AA failure on functional text and the panel is the right place to rule on it.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — three errors, one of them load-bearing.

(1) The ink-side number is wrong by 4 points and inverts the hierarchy. `rgba(255,255,255,0.72)` over #111111 composites to rgb(188) and measures 9.94:1, not the claimed 6.0:1. The artifact contradicts the seat ten lines from the site of the change: notes.css:62 declares `--on-ink-2: rgba(255,255,255,0.62)` with the comment "7.7:1 on ink" (I measure 7.67). A cap at 0.72 would therefore paint BRIGHTER than `.darkAct`'s own label colour, which is `--on-ink-2` (notes.css:929). The keycap in "Cancel Esc" would out-shout the verb it annotates, on the one state where the whole room goes to ink and the dictation floor is the entire composition. That is the fix making the work worse.

(2) It writes a new alpha into a locked ladder. The ink ramp on this surface is `--on-ink-1: #ffffff` / `--on-ink-2: 0.62`. `rgba(255,255,255,0.72)` is a hard-coded third step, and hard-coded, at that — the same class the lab already paid to clear.

I typed into `.topField` at notes.notebook to raise the commit button: `.act.commitPart kbd` ("Save it · Ctrl Enter") is `visibility: hidden` in the static frames and paints only after capture. Its ground is `background: rgb(17,17,17)` with `color: #ffffff`; at 0.55 it composites to rgb(148) = 6.23:1 and passes AA comfortably. An already-passing cap on the most prominent commit control in Notes loses all recession for zero contrast gain. `.undoAct kbd` (:844) never painted in any of the eight states or the seam run. The gate's 8 OPEN is exactly 2 caps x 4 viewports — the seat's own evidence says only `.darkAct` fails, then the fix reaches past it anyway.

SEVERITY. The seat left the class implicit; defect is right. Both caps stay legible at 600 weight, nothing is asserted untrue, and no advertised behaviour fails — the keys work, `Esc` and `Ctrl+Enter` both fire. WHAT I MEASURED (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…`, at 390/768/1440/1920, all four of notes.notebook, notes.seam, tasks.board, timeline.desk). Every geometric number the seat gives is exact:

This is not a leftover; it is the decided answer, and the decision is written into the shipped source. `src/notes.js:3062`, in the account handler, carries the comment: "Two slots is correct and Tasks proves it; two promises is not." The r1 record for `two-account-tiles-one-honest` says the same in its verdict — it explicitly examined and DISCARDED "pick one account tile per sheet" ("deleting the rail avatar would strip Timeline of its ONLY account door … deleting the Notes dock avatar leaves Notes at 390 with no account door at all"). PROBLEM 2 — "the two copies carry different accessible names" — REAL IN NOTES ONLY, and the finding generalises it wrongly. Not here yet."` / same desc; **Tasks dock `name="Orla, venue manager"` / same desc — identical to the rail.** The finding says "Same on Tasks at 1440" and then lists all three problems as one object; two of the three do not exist on Tasks. PROBLEM 3 — "the sentence in both name and title, spoken twice" — CONFIRMED, and it is the only real defect here. WHAT I CONFIRMED (Chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=tasks.board, real key events)
The primary observation reproduces verbatim. Focus `demo-t-01`, Space -> "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."; ArrowRight -> "In progress, position 1 of 4." with `.trayCount` going 3,3,2,0,5 -> 2,4,2,0,5; Space -> "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the in progress column."; Ctrl+Z -> "Nothing left to undo." and the card stays at `doing` index 0. The same displacement by the card menu: "…moved to the in progress column." then Ctrl+Z -> "…is back in the to do column." with the card restored to `todo` index 0. The code matches: `src/tasks.js` line 1897 is `say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".")` with no `arm(...)` beside it, while the drop handler arms at 2299 and `moveto` arms at 2104. Escape does correctly push nothing (1836-1842). The Done branch is already whole — carrying into Done calls `completed()` (1893) and undoes cleanly ("…done. Press Ctrl Z to undo." -> "…is no longer done. It is in the to do column."). So the hole is exactly: keyboard carry, non-Done landing lane. That is real, it is the board's primary gesture on its accessible route, and it is the "Nothing reversible" class from the paid-for library alive on one of three doors.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — three holes, two of them regressions of bugs this file records as already fixed

1. It loses the completion and hold dates. `carryMove` calls `moveTo(..., true)` on every arrow press, and `applyLaneFacts` (1118-1123) re-stamps `completedAt`/`heldSince` at that moment — long before Space is pressed. The drag path knows this and captures `heldWas`/`doneWas` BEFORE its `moveTo` (2283-2284), with the comment "undoing a card dragged out of Done used to rewrite 'Completed 15 Jul' to today". The fix says the receipt carries "the card id plus the lane and index it held at pick-up" and nothing else. I drove the reachable case: focus `demo-t-09` in Done ("Completed / 15 Jul"), Space, ArrowLeft -> "Waiting, position 1 of 1.", Space -> "…dropped in the waiting column.", and the card now reads "Held today / … since 16 Jul." A receipt built to this fix's spec would restore the lane and stamp `completedAt = TODAY`, printing "Completed 26 Aug" over "Completed 15 Jul". The fix reintroduces the exact defect the drag path documents.

2. It arms an undo for a non-event. I drove Space, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, Space: the card lands back at `todo` index 0 and announces "…dropped in the to do column." The drag path explicitly refuses this case at 2274-2278 ("Picking a card up and putting it back is a non-event. It was arming an undo and announcing a move."). "Record on drop only" as written arms it, and hands the operator an Undo strip for a move that did not happen.

3. It names the wrong second door, and is factually wrong about the one it names. Enter mid-carry does NOT leave the card committed: I measured `aria-grabbed="true"` still set after Enter, and a further ArrowRight moved the card on to Review ("Review, position 1 of 3."). The card is still in hand; Space still drops it, Escape still cancels it. This is also `enter-during-carry-does-not-drop (r1)`, already refuted, re-filed with no claim of regression — and the refutation's grounds still hold at runtime: the card carries `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` and the foot pill reads "…↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel". Making Enter a fourth commit key while both of those name Space alone re-creates the advertised-vs-implemented gap in reverse. The real second door is `endCarry()` (1677): I pressed Space, ArrowRight, then made a real pointer press on another card — the carry ended, `demo-t-01` stayed committed in `doing`, and Ctrl+Z said "Nothing left to undo." The finding walked past it.

SEVERITY — corrected down to defect, deliberately. The seat's framing reads as blocking. It is not. Nothing on screen promises undo on this path: no Undo strip is drawn, the spoken sentence omits the standard "Press Ctrl Z to undo." tail that every armed act appends, and the foot pill names only the three keys it actually implements. "Nothing left to undo." is true of the stack. The operator's recourse survives — Escape before the drop, or Space and walk it back after — so no capability is lost, only parity and the receipt. It is visibly wrong beside two sibling routes that do it right, on the route a keyboard-only operator is confined to, which is why it is a defect and not a refinement.

refuted.problem: Clicking a moment's grab handle in `timeline.owner-flight` inserts the editor above the measure and scrolls nothing. Measured immediately after the open: `.b-editActs` ("Done") occupies y 942–981 and `.b-editDanger` ("Delete this moment") y 993–1045, identically in `down` and `across`. At 1280×900 both are entirely below the fold; at 1440×960 "Done" is cut in half and "Delete" is fully below; at 1920×1000 "Delete" is 45px below. The sheet grows from 1173 to 1755 and the measure — the seven moments and the horizon, the object the whole product is built around — moves to y≈1235, wholly out of view. The sheet can be scrolled, but nothing scrolls it, and there is no edge cue: at 1280×900 the panel simply ends at the sheet's bottom border with the "Shown / Hidden" row as the last thing visible.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the across half is already-adjudicated, three of the finding's measured claims are wrong, and the fix crashes on the wedding day and breaks the undo bar's reserved band. Driven in chromium against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight` at 1280x900 / 1440x960 / 1920x1000 in both layouts.

WHAT IS TRUE. `.b-edit` is 554px tall and mounts into `.b-editHost` with `position: relative; max-height: none; overflow: visible` (timeline.css:1967-1985, the `min-width:1024px` in-rail override). `.app.sheet` is the only scroller and `scrollTop` stays 0 through the open. In `across` the numbers are exact: `.b-editActs` 942-981, `.b-editDanger` 993-1045, sheet 1173 -> 1755. Against the real fold — the sheet's client bottom at 882/942/982, not the window — Done and Delete are below it at 1280 and 1440, and Delete is 63px below at 1920 (the finding says 45, measured against `innerHeight` rather than the sheet).

WRONG #1 — "identically in `down` and `across`". False. In `down` the editor opens at y=653, not 508; `.b-editActs` is 1087-1126 and `.b-editDanger` 1138-1190 — 145px lower than the finding's figures, at every one of the three widths. The finding's whole numeric case is the `across` case asserted twice.

WRONG #2 — the sentence that carries the severity. "The sheet grows from 1173 to 1755 and the measure ... moves to y≈1235, wholly out of view." In `down` the sheet is 2184 before AND after — it does not grow — and `.b-measure` does not move at all: top 354.39 before the open, 354.39 after. In `across` the measure top goes 571.58 -> 1153, not 1235; the finding is 82px out on the one number it calls the object the product is built around.

WRONG #3 — the edge-cue sentence names the wrong viewport. At 1280x900 `across` the Shown/Hidden row (892-929) is ITSELF below the fold; the last visible things in the panel are `.b-stepRead` (808-853) and an empty `.b-ceiling` (859-879). "The 'Shown / Hidden' row as the last thing visible" is the 1920x1000 case, not the 1280x900 case the finding attaches it to.

ALREADY ADJUDICATED. The `across` displacement is `across-editor-hides-the-measure` (r1), where it was VERIFIED TRUE with the same mechanism (`.b-editHost` inside `.b-stick`, 554px inserted, `keepInBand` a no-op because the panel computes to `relative` and there is no `.b-plan`), classed **defect**, and refuted on its fix. Moving the fold cursor from the measure to the Done row is the same defect re-framed, not a regression, and no regression is claimed.

SEVERITY IS OVERSTATED. Nothing is unreachable. The sheet already overflows before the editor exists (1301 vs 864 at 1280 across; 2184 vs 864 in `down`), so scrolling is the established gesture on this surface. Escape closes the editor and returns focus to the `.b-grab` (verified, both layouts). Tab reaches Done and the browser scrolls it in — sheet `scrollTop` 0 -> 460 in across, verified. The steppers, the `role=status` readout and the undo bar all work. This is a defect, not blocking and not misleading.

THE FIX IS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES.
(a) `document.querySelector('.b-editDanger').scrollIntoView(...)` throws a TypeError on one of the seven moments. `editor()` at timeline.js:1709 is `theDay ? null : h("div.b-editDanger", ...)`, and `.b-item[data-anchor="true"]` — the wedding day — has a `.b-grab`. Verified: opening it yields `danger? false`, `acts? true`. The fix's literal text throws inside the `.b-grab` click handler on the anchor moment, the one object every distance on the plan is measured from.
(b) The fix does not restore the casualty it names. Simulated in `across` at 1280x900: the sheet scrolls to 163, Delete lands flush at 882 — and `.b-measure` goes to 990 and the edited moment's `.b-grab` to 1200. Both still off screen. It buys the commit row and pays for it with the measure, which is the thing the finding says the whole product is built around.
(c) `overflow-y: auto` on `.b-edit` destroys the undo band. `.b-edit .b-undo` is `position: absolute; top:16; left:16; right:16` (timeline.css:1324-1341) with `.b-edit` carrying `padding-top: 88/104/148px` to reserve its band — three rounds of tuned numbers whose comments read "Round 1 paid for those buttons holding still under the pointer" and "an OPAQUE plate did not overlap the first field's label, it deleted it". Make the panel a scroll container and the absolutely-positioned reversibility bar scrolls with the content out of its reserve, leaving 104px of dead white at the top and the one `role=status` surface that reports a move off screen.
(d) `min(content, innerHeight − editorTop − 24)` is stale the instant anything moves. `editorTop` is viewport-relative and the panel rides the sheet's scroll; `reserve()` at timeline.js:1841 already records that a filled undo bar raises the sheet 76px, which is why it re-runs on every settle. A cap computed once at mount is wrong after the first wheel event.
(e) It also adds a second vertical scroller inside `.app.sheet` in a 310px rail column, with no `data-fold` treatment — reproducing the un-cued edge the finding complains about, one level deeper, on a file that already owns `markFold` precisely so "a title or a control could not be sliced mid-glyph at the fold with nothing saying so".

refuted.problem: In `across` below 1024 the measure becomes a horizontal scroll container: `overflow-x: auto` with `scrollWidth − clientWidth` of 310 at 390 and 166 at 768. It carries `role="list"` and a good label ("What is still ahead, nearest first") but `tabindex="-1"`, and in `timeline.desk` it contains zero focusable descendants. At 390 four of seven moments — Choose the evening music, Final guest numbers, Venue walk-through, and the Wedding day itself — sit past its right edge; at 768, two of seven, including the wedding day. There is no fade, no scrollbar affordance and no ::after on the element or its parent, so the last visible moment is cut hard against the sheet edge with nothing to say more exists. `timeline.desk` at 390 offers the ACROSS control in its head, so this configuration is one press away.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the headline is factually false about the code and false when driven. Every geometric number in the finding is right; the accessibility claim that carries the severity is wrong.

DRIVEN: Chromium 149 (Playwright 1.61.1), file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.desk&layout=across, at 390/768/1024/1280.

1. There is no `tabindex="-1"`. The full attribute list on `.b-measure:not(.b-back)` at 390 is: `class role=list aria-label="What is still ahead, nearest first" data-px=14 data-clock=2026-07-16 data-across=true data-scrolls=true style=...`. No tabindex attribute at any width. The finding invented the attribute it built its argument on.

2. "Keyboard inert" is false. Tab reaches the measure as the fourth stop at 390 — railTile → "Across" → "Down" → `DIV.b-measure` — and at 768. It matches `:focus-visible` and paints the app's own ring: `outline: solid 2px rgb(79,70,229)` at `outline-offset: 2px`. Twenty ArrowRight presses drive `scrollLeft` to exactly 310 at 390 and exactly 166 at 768 — the maxima the finding itself quotes. Every hidden moment, wedding day included, arrives under the arrow keys with a visible ring on the region. Chrome has focused childless scrollers since 127; this is 149. So fix-half one is already shipping, for free, on the browser this engagement grades in.

3. It is not even the only route. In `timeline.owner-flight` at 390 across (sw 640, cw 332, data-scrolls=true) the measure holds 7 focusable `.b-grab` buttons — the moments are directly tabbable there, and focusing one scrolls it in. `timeline.desk` is the read-only surface.

4. What the finding got right, and I confirmed: overflow of 310 at 390 and 166 at 768; four of seven hidden at 390 (Choose the evening music 356, Final guest numbers 412, Venue walk-through 524, Wedding day 636, against cw 330) and two of seven at 768; ACROSS present and `aria-pressed="true"` on desk at 390; no `::after`/`::before` on the measure or its wrapper (all `content: none`).

5. "Nothing to say more exists" is overstated. In the plain 390 shot the rule runs off the sheet's right edge — an axis continuing past the frame is the conventional signal — and "Final dress fit" / "Sat 22 Au" are cut mid-word. Separately, `across.css` already sets `scrollbar-width: thin` on `[data-across="true"][data-scrolls="true"]`, so a classic-scrollbar platform draws a scrollbar; headless measured `offsetHeight − clientHeight = 0` because it uses overlay scrollbars, which is why the seat saw none. What remains is a soft-edge refinement, not a blocking or misleading defect.

6. The fix would regress the state that matters most. It conditions only on `scrollWidth > clientWidth`, so it also fires in `owner-flight` at 390 — where Chrome deliberately does NOT focus the scroller because it has focusable children — and inserts a redundant container tab stop in front of all seven `.b-grab` buttons. That is a new defect bought to fix a non-defect.

7. The fade half is also technically shaky as written. An `::after` on `.b-measure` is an absolutely positioned descendant of the scroll container, so `right: 0` resolves against the scrolling padding box and the fade travels away from the visible edge as you scroll — it must live on the non-scrolling wrapper, not the scroller.

refuted.problem: After sending words to Tasks from `notes.seam`, all three routes to taking it back leave `document.activeElement === document.body`: Ctrl+Z, a click on the visible "Undo" button, and Enter on that button. I drove all three at 1440×960 and got BODY every time, while the live region correctly reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." and the peel panel is correctly restored with `.peelField` back at y 400. The equivalent path in Tasks does this right — undoing a tick restores focus to the card's own `.tick` — so the two halves of one suite disagree about what undo owes the keyboard.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces on all three routes verbatim, and must NOT be discarded. Every observation checks out. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 on ?v=paper&state=notes.seam: press [data-act="send"], focus lands on .deskFactLink, then (a) Ctrl+Z, (b) click [data-act="undo"], (c) focus the Undo button and press Enter — document.activeElement is BODY on all three, while the live region reads "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." and .peelField is restored at y 400.125 (identical to pre-send). Same at 768. The Tasks comparison is exact: on tasks.board, focus .tick (demo-t-01) → Enter → Ctrl+Z returns focus to BUTTON.tick on demo-t-01. And the cited precedent is right — notes.js:1042 in beginPeel is `refocus = { kind: "field", sel: ".peelField", end: true }`.

Note for the ledger: this is not a new seat's discovery, it is r1's `undo-drops-focus-to-body` — same seat wording, same state, same route ("Ctrl+Z after a seam send, in Notes (state notes.seam)") — closed as fixed and still failing under measurement today. What landed was doUndo()'s deliberately narrow branch, which never covers this case. Treat it as an unfixed close, not a re-raise.

The fix as written repairs one of the three routes it names, and the finding's own assertion would still fail on the other two. doUndo() runs in this order: `revert(); say(undoneLabel); const inStrip = document.activeElement && document.activeElement.closest(".undo"); if (inStrip) { refocus = { kind: "field", sel: phone.matches ? ".phoneField" : ".topField" }; } paint();`. The only seam-scoped place to put the proposed record is the revert callback at notes.js:1135 — which runs BEFORE the inStrip test. On the click and Enter routes the pressed control IS the Undo button, so inStrip is true and refocus is overwritten with `.topField`; I measured `document.querySelector(".topField") === null` in seam state, so paint() consumes the record on a null target, skips the caret fallback, and lands on BODY. That is precisely the failure the comment above that branch warns about for search, reproduced in the seam. So the two most visible routes — the button a person can actually see — are untouched by the proposed fix.

Second error: the selector is unqualified. At 390 `.peelField` exists in the DOM but sits under `.desk { display: none }` (measured: box 0x0, chain peelField/peelScroll/peel/pile → desk:none). I called .focus() on it directly at 390 and activeElement stayed BODY. Every other field refocus in this file is written `phone.matches ? ".phoneField" : ".topField"` for exactly this reason; the proposed record drops that shape and is a silent no-op on the phone.

refuted.problem: Arriving at `?state=notes.seam` at 390×844 or 768×1024 renders the note and the whole peel panel inside `.desk`, which src/notes.css:1526 sets to `display: none` below 721. Measured: `.peel` 0×0, `.readBody` 0×0, `[data-act="send"]` 0×0 and not hit-testable (`elementFromPoint` at its centre returns `DIV.floor`), and none of the peel's controls appear in the tab order — 13 tab stops at 390, not one of them in the peel. The seam state sets `peeling` without `openId`, so the phone reader never opens and the content falls back to the hidden desk. `pickSurface()` at line 805 already makes exactly this fallback and carries a comment saying why. I confirmed the live gesture is unaffected: peeling from the notebook at 390 renders the panel at 358×308 with Send hittable at 138×44, and a 1440→390 resize mid-peel keeps the panel and the typed wording intact. Round 1's `seam-state-at-390-loses-the-note` was refuted on its fix and on two of its measurements; this is the mechanism that refutation did not name, and it makes the fix a single condition.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — on one of its two headline measurements, on its named mechanism, and on its fix, which is inert. The 390 half of the problem is real and should not be discarded; everything the finding says about WHY is wrong.

1. The 768×1024 claim is false. The breakpoint is `max-width: 720px`; 768 is above it. Driven at file:///.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.seam, 768×1024, chromium: `.desk` is display:flex at 668×455, `.peel` 496×258, `.readBody` 527×55, `[data-act="send"]` 138×36 with `elementFromPoint` at its centre returning `BUTTON.act` — hittable — and 25 rendered focusables. Nothing is hidden at 768. The finding names it in its first sentence and in the same breath cites the ≤720 rule that excludes it.

2. The mechanism is misattributed, and this is fatal to the fix. `?state=notes.seam` sets `state = "seam"` (src/app.js:57 splits the compound), and `paint()` at src/notes.js:2721 dispatches `STATES[state]`. `STATES.seam` is its own function at src/notes.js:2414. It returns `{ desk: readSheet(note), body: …, dock: true }` unconditionally — no `phone.matches` branch and no `over:` key at all. `notebook()` at 2127 is bound only to `STATES.notebook` and `STATES.capture` and is never called in this state. My own measurement proves it: at 390 the seam state leaves a real `.desk` element in the DOM (display:none, `.readBody` inside it), whereas `notebook()`'s phone branch returns `desk: ""`, so `.desk` would not exist. I confirmed that contrast directly — driving the live peel at 390 from notes.notebook gives `.desk` absent, `.phoneSheet` 390×844, `.peel` 358×292, `[data-act="send"]` hittable at `BUTTON.act`.

3. Therefore the proposed fix changes nothing. Editing line 2127 patches a function that `?state=notes.seam` never reaches. Apply it verbatim and the 390 seam room is exactly as dead as before. A correct problem with a fix that cannot fire is refuted.

4. Two smaller errors: the function the finding credits with the precedent is `pickTarget()` at src/notes.js:797, not `pickSurface()` at 805 — the comment it quotes is real and sits at 800-804. And the live peel's Send measures 138×36 at 390, not 138×44.

5. Severity is overstated. The seam gesture — the protected object — works at every width, which the finding itself confirms and I re-confirmed. What is broken is one lab deep-link URL at one viewport. That is `defect`, not blocking: the product does what it says; a capture state does not.

This is also the second filing of the same 390 observation (r1 `seam-state-at-390-loses-the-note`, refuted on its fix). The problem is now twice-confirmed and twice mis-fixed; the sharpened fix below is the one that actually lands.

refuted.problem: The seam's central promise is asserted in three places and is false for every note the fixture says has already crossed. The strapline reads "3 so far, and every note stayed here"; each row's accessible name ends "The note it came from stayed in Notes."; the seam card says "Your note stays here" and the receipt says "still yours to edit". Driven at 1440: the three crossed notes (s1 late-checkout, s2 linen, s3 registrar) are in NO index — `notes.notebook` lists 14 `.idxRow`s and none of them is one of the three; they are not in the search corpus — `Ctrl+K` "linen" announces "No note says “linen”. Nothing in the notebook is close to it either." while `fixture.js:486` holds a note body reading "Linen supplier rang, the order now ships Tuesday…", and "supplier" returns "1 of 14 notes", matching the photographer note and not that one; and `/Linen supplier rang/.test(document.body.innerText)` is false at every state. The cause is structural: `work()` returns `N.notes.slice()` and `N.crossed` is a disjoint array that is rendered only as task wording. Each ledger row is a real `<button class="idxRow" tabindex=0>` with a full accessible name, and pressing any of the three (nth 0, 1, 2) produces no announcement, no state change and no note — a focusable, named control that does nothing. A note sent live in-session behaves correctly (send "Heating" → still among the 14, still searchable, index row gains an "In Tasks" pill), which proves the intended behaviour exists and that only the pre-crossed notes are stranded.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces verbatim, and must NOT be discarded. I confirmed every observable claim in Chromium at 1440x960 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.seam|notes.notebook`: the ledger renders exactly three `<button class="idxRow" data-id="s1|s2|s3">` rows whose accessible names end "The note it came from stayed in Notes."; `notes.notebook` renders 14 `.idxRow`s (n01,n02,n03,n06,n04,n05,n07,n12,n13,n09,n11,n14,n08,n10) and none is s1/s2/s3; the head reads "14 notes"; Ctrl+K "linen" returns "No note says “linen”. Nothing in the notebook is close to it either." while `fixture.js:486` holds "Linen supplier rang, the order now ships Tuesday…"; "supplier" returns "1 of 14 notes" and matches the photographer note; and `/Linen supplier rang/.test(document.body.innerText)` is false. Pressing the first ledger row produced an empty live region and no desk change (readBody unchanged) — only `data-open` moved onto the row itself. The seam's central sentence is asserted three ways and is untrue for the three notes the fixture says already crossed. Severity is correctly misleading, at the top of that class.

THE FIX IS REFUTED, and I refute it by building it and driving it. I patched the built file exactly as written — `seed()`'s `return N.notes.slice()` → `N.notes.concat(N.crossed).sort((a,b)=>a.ms-b.ms)` — and three things went wrong.

(1) IT MOVES THE SEAM'S NOTE. `STATES.seam` falls back to `work()[13]`. Re-sorting `work()` by `ago` changes index 13, so the seam room stopped opening "Heating: orchard room takes ~40 min to warm in October…" and opened "Quote from today that I want to keep: “we don't want a big production…" instead. The seam is a protected object and `shots/paper-notes.seam--1920x1000.png` is drawn on the Heating note. The finding does not mention this and the sort is what causes it.

(2) IT MAKES THE DEAD CONTROL WORSE, NOT BETTER. With the corpus patched, pressing the s1 ledger row announces `Open. Mara asked about a late checkout for the bridal suite, Sunday 11am instead of 9. Said yes in principle, just needs to clear housekeeping. Open on the desk.` — and the desk does not change, because `STATES.seam` recomputes its note from `peeling`, which `openNote` never clears. So the row now (a) reprints the entire private note into the live region, which is precisely what the comment at :1930-1934 forbids and the finding itself says to preserve, and (b) says "Open on the desk" when nothing opened. A silent no-op is better than a control that lies and leaks.

(3) THE FINDING IS WRONG ABOUT WHAT IS STRANDED. "only the pre-crossed notes are stranded" is false for the dead-control half. I sent live in the seam and got a fourth row `data-id="crossed_n14"`; pressing it is equally dead — empty live region, no desk change — because `crossed_<id>` is never in `work()`, and the proposed `data-id → lift` wiring will never find it. The fix leaves the row a person just made — the likeliest one to press — exactly as dead as before.

Minor: it is `seed()` at :203 that returns `N.notes.slice()`, not `work()` at :205.

refuted.problem: `go(state)` calls `C.mount()` — a full repaint that destroys the `.b-live` node — and then does `document.querySelector(".b-live").textContent = SAID[state]` on the freshly created replacement. A region inserted into the document already containing its text is not a mutation of a region assistive technology was watching, so none of it is ever announced. Measured directly: I marked the live nodes at load and watched `document.body` for subtree changes. Pressing Preview logs `REMOVED a .b-live` then `ADDED a .b-live with text: "The plan as guests will see it."` and fires zero mutations on any watched region; pressing "Get the link" logs `ADDED a .b-live with text: "Ready to copy."`, again zero. A second run confirms node identity: `.b-live` goes ny9fux → n80t9e → npgkp9 across three acts while the suite's `p.sr` stays `nk8cdg` throughout. The same acts change the whole surface — Preview replaces the three-button bar with one "Back to the plan" and takes `.b-grab` from 7 to 0, removing every edit control — and Escape does nothing. Tasks and Notes are clean by contrast (`p.sr` alive and mutating on tick, filter, Planning, send). The file knows: the orientation switch at :2959-2969 was moved to `window.__SUITE.say()` with a comment explaining exactly this, and the comment above `go()` at :2166-2169 claims the cure — "three of the owner's five top-level actions were silent screen changes" — while the mechanism leaves them silent.
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX AND THE SEVERITY — the core mechanism is real and reproduces exactly, so do NOT discard it; but the finding is factually wrong about half its own named sites, and wrong about the consequence it hangs its severity on.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`). `mount()` at `src/timeline.js:143` does `host.textContent = ""` — total teardown — so `go()`'s write at :2183-2184 always lands on a node that did not exist a millisecond earlier. Marked every live node at load and watched `document.body`: Preview logs `REMOVED .b-live subtree` then `ADDED .b-live text="The plan as guests will see it."`, Back logs the same with `"Back to the plan."`, Get the link with `"Ready to copy."`. Node identity 8hmung → n9s5w2 → p0rsgd → ot7pnq across three acts; the suite region `#say` stays `egmbx7` and stays empty throughout. Zero MUTATED events on any watched region. The seat's numbers are right and its mechanism is right, and `src/app.js:184-186` states the rule in the file's own words.

WHERE IT IS WRONG ABOUT THE CODE. It names four sites; two of them are not broken.
1. `:2672`, the publish-screen copy receipt. I drove it with clipboard permissions granted on `timeline.publish` and got `MUTATED .b-live#fpur73 -> "Link copied."` — same node before and after (`fpur73` → `fpur73`), an in-place mutation of a `role="status"` region that has been in the tree since the mount. That receipt announces today. The headline "nothing it says is heard" is false for it.
2. `:1979`, the owner-surface copy branch in `wireOwner`. Enumerated `[data-act]` on `timeline.owner-flight`: the timeline offers `add`, `preview`, `publish` and no `copy` at all. That branch is unreachable on the suite's owner states, so it is not evidence of anything.
3. "Keep `p.b-live` as the visible receipt" is wrong on the two sites that carry the actual defect. `:2246` and `:2307` render `p.b-live.b-vh` — visually hidden. Strip `role="status"` from those and they are not visible receipts, they are dead nodes.

WHERE IT IS WRONG ABOUT THE CONSEQUENCE. "The mechanism leaves them silent" is false. `go()` focuses the heading first (`:2175-2178`), and I measured focus landing every time: after Preview `H1.b-who "Mara & Finn"`, after Back `H1.b-who "Mara & Finn"`, after Get the link `H1.b-pressTitle "Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July."`. A screen reader announces the focused H1. The comment at :2166-2169 claims the focus move as the cure, and the focus move works — the seat read the comment as claiming the live line and then convicted it of a promise it did not make. The real damage is narrower and worth stating precisely: Preview and Back to the plan focus headings with the IDENTICAL text, so those two acts are indistinguishable by ear and the one sentence that separates the owner's plan from the guest's view is exactly the sentence that is dropped. That is a defect, not blocking — the surface is announced, ambiguously; "Back to the plan" is still reachable by shift-tab from the heading (forward tab from the H1 gives Across, Down, Behind you, then body). The aggravating detail it stacks on — Preview takes `.b-grab` 7→0 — is what Preview means; the guest's view has no edit controls by design, and dressing that as harm inflates the class.

The gates do not cover this: `interaction-check.mjs` asserts nothing about `.b-live` node identity, and no automated seat can see a region that is replaced rather than mutated. The class is a genuine regression of the same defect closed as `orientation-switch-says-nothing-on-desk` (r1) — which is why the file already carries the correct pattern at :2968 and why the sharpened fix is three lines, not a build.

refuted.problem: This is a re-raise of `waiting-lane-is-keyboard-inert` (r1, CONFIRMED, recorded closed). I re-ran that finding's own recorded assertion and it fails exactly as written. Measured at 1440: `.trayAdd` tabindex map is `To do:0, In progress:-1, Review:-1, Waiting:-1, Done:-1`; a 120-press Tab sweep at each of 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 never reaches "Add a task to Waiting" (14 stops at 390, 17 at every other width, the only Add row visited being "Add a task to To do"); and a breadth-first search over ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown from the roving card, to depth 6, reaches all 13 cards and **zero** `.trayAdd` buttons. ArrowRight from Review lands on Done, skipping the empty lane entirely; ArrowDown past the last card in a lane stays on that card. The rover-follows-the-card mechanism works — moving the rover into Done flips Done's Add to tabindex 0 — which is precisely why a lane with no cards can never hold it. Confirmed as an emptiness defect and not a Waiting defect: at `tasks.dense`, where Waiting holds 2 cards, the same pattern gives `10/0, 7/-1, 4/-1, 2/-1, 9/-1` and Waiting is reachable. Nothing in `interaction-check.mjs` asserts anything about `.trayAdd`, which is why this was recorded closed without being closed (lessons L-05).
refuted.why:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, every number reproduces exactly, and it must NOT be discarded — do not read this verdict as "no hole."

WHAT I VERIFIED, driven in chromium at 1440x960 against file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board:
- `.trayAdd` tabindex map is exactly `todo:3 cards/0, doing:3/-1, review:2/-1, waiting:0/-1, done:5/-1`. All five rows are rendered and hit-target sized (233-234 x 36).
- A 140-press Tab sweep yields 18 stops (railTile, 3 chips, Share, Planning, More, Board, Filter, one card + tick/who/cardDots, "Add a task to To do", dockField, dockPrimary, dockAvatar, body). "Add a task to Waiting" is not among them.
- Exhaustive DFS, all 8 keys (arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown) to depth 3 = 512 replayed sequences from the roving card: 9 distinct focus targets, all `.card`, **zero** `.trayAdd`. Confirmed in source: `walk()` (src/tasks.js:1656-1668) only ever assigns a task id to `focusId`, and its horizontal loop `for (let x = at.x+dx; ...) { if (rows.length) {...} }` skips a lane with no rows outright.
- Control at `tasks.dense` is exact to the finding's digits: `10/0, 7/-1, 4/-1, 2/-1, 9/-1`, and Waiting is reachable there. The rover-follows-the-card mechanism is confirmed live: carry a To do card right x3 and drop it, and Waiting flips to `waiting:1/0` with Tab x4 from the card landing on "Add a task to Waiting".
- The re-raise is legitimate, not a bookkeeping error on the seat's side: the tabindex expression at src/tasks.js:651-653 is byte-identical to what r1 quoted, `walk()` is unchanged, no `focusAdd`-style rover exists, and `panel/STATE.md:70` still lists `waiting-lane-is-keyboard-inert` under "Open from round 1 — ten defects, known and classed". Nothing in `interaction-check.mjs` mentions `.trayAdd`. This is lessons L-05 exactly.

SEVERITY: defect, and the seat's own class is right — I checked the escape hatches before agreeing it is not blocking. There are TWO working keyboard routes into Waiting, not the one r1 named: (a) Space, ArrowRight x3, Space — verified, announces "…dropped in the waiting column."; and (b) `.cardDots` "Move this task" opens a real `role="menu"` whose items are To do / In progress / Review / Waiting / Done. So the product still does what it says end to end; what is broken is that a visible, named, 233x36 button on the one lane that is empty most of the time can be pressed by no key sequence.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — three faults, one of them making the work worse:

1. **It creates a keyboard trap where today there is only an unreachable button.** `onKey` bails at src/tasks.js:1870-1871 — `const card = event.target.closest(".card[data-id]"); if (!card) return;`. Every arrow, and Space, is handled only when the event target is a `.card`. Land the rover on Waiting's `.trayAdd` and the next ArrowRight does nothing: you cannot reach Done, and you cannot get back to Review. Only Tab escapes. A fix whose entire subject is the keyboard model is silent on the return path. r1's refutation named this exact omission and the re-raise did not absorb it.

2. **"so the roving model at `src/tasks.js:651-653` is unchanged" is false against the source.** That expression keys entirely off `focusId`, a task id: `rows.some(t => t.id === focusId) || (!focusId && c.id === B.columns[0].id)`. With the rover at `{lane:"waiting", index:"add"}` there is no task id, so `!focusId` takes the second branch and gives **To do's** Add row `tabindex="0"` while the focused Waiting row sits at `-1` — the board's single tab stop in the wrong lane, and Shift-Tab out of a `-1` element undefined. The fix's own third clause (track `{lane, index|"add"}`) requires rewriting 651-653; the sentence claiming it is unchanged contradicts it.

3. **It ignores the three states where the Add row is not rendered, one of which re-opens a closed finding.** `src/tasks.css:1622` `[data-app="tasks"] .board[data-filtered] .tray[data-empty] .trayAdd { display: none; }`; `:1644` the same under `.board[data-blank]`; `:1290` `.trayAdd[data-under] { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }`, toggled after layout at src/tasks.js:2497-2503 whenever the carry strip overlaps the row. Put the rover on an Add row and turn a filter on and its home vanishes in the same mount — that is `planning-drawer-erases-the-done-lane` / `undo-drops-focus-to-body` again, paid for twice already. Put a card in hand and the rover sits on an invisible, pointer-events-none control — the named invisible-but-focusable class in lessons.md.

Also: the ArrowDown-past-the-last-card half was specifically argued down in r1's verified refutation as unnecessary scope, and that judgement still holds — it doubles the rover's row count in every lane and puts a non-numeric `y` into the `Math.min(at.y, rows.length - 1)` arithmetic that every sideways move runs.

unadjudicated.element: every `[aria-disabled="true"]` in the suite — `.rail` tiles (master.html:364), `.segItem` List/Schedule/Calendar, `.viewTools` Filter/Sort/Display, `Share`, `More`, `.dockField`, `.dockAvatar`
unadjudicated.problem: The artefact has no visual language for a closed door, anywhere, and pressing one produces no visible change anywhere. Driven at 1440x960 on `?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, sixteen chrome controls sit on the Tasks sheet and **ten of them are aria-disabled**: Share, More, List, Schedule, Calendar, Filter, Sort, Display, the dock's search field (`.dockField`, 211x38, "Search The Orchard, events") and the dock's account tile. Measured computed styles: every one of them paints `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)` at weight 400 — which is `--ink-3`, the token the system uses for live micro-labels at 5.3:1, i.e. fully-available secondary text. The live control beside them, `Planning`, paints `rgba(17,17,17,0.72)`. A 0.10 alpha step is the entire difference. Inside the view segment it is worse: `Board` is the current view (ink-1 / 600 / white pill) and List, Schedule and Calendar are 0.62/400 — identical to how a live-but-unselected segment item would look, so "not selected" and "not built" are the same picture. In the spine this is a regression of a finding recorded closed at r1 (`closed-doors-are-indistinguishable`, classed misleading). Its own recorded assertion was "the computed color differs from a live `.railTile`'s and cursor is not pointer". I measured both halves at 1440 and at 390-touch: `home` (closed) and `notes` (live, not current) both compute `color: rgba(255,255,255,0.62)`, `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `cursor: pointer`, `opacity: 1`, `filter: none`. The rule the r1 finding named as dead — `.rail [aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--on-ink-2) }` at master.html:364 — is still in the file, still setting the colour `.railTile` already has at line 321. The third clause fails too: I snapshotted every element's box, opacity, background and transform before and after a real mouse click on `home`, and exactly one node in the document changed — `P.sr` at 1x1 px, off-screen. Same result for Share, Filter, Sort, Display, List, Schedule and Calendar: each writes its sentence into `#say` and nothing else moves. At 390 with a real touch tap there is no cursor and no tooltip, so the entire signal is zero.
unadjudicated.consequence: On the surface Orla runs her season from, ten of the sixteen controls do nothing and nothing on screen says which. The two she reaches for first are among them: Share — on a board whose own card reads "Share with the floor team" — and the search field, which is the largest, most inviting object in the floating dock, sitting beside a live black Add task button. She presses it, the screen does not move, and she cannot tell whether the app is broken, her tap missed, or the feature is absent. On her phone at the marquee that is the only reading available to her. The locked answer was "present, reachable, and say plainly that they are not here yet"; as shipped, the plainness reaches a screen-reader user and nobody else.
unadjudicated.fix: One token pair and one function call. (1) Give closed a real ink step: add `cursor: default` to `.rail [aria-disabled="true"]` and replace the dead rule at master.html:364 with `color: var(--on-ink-3)` (rgba(255,255,255,0.42), already declared); on the white sheet, move every `[aria-disabled="true"]` control from `--ink-3` to `--ink-4` and lift the live secondary controls (`Planning`, `.segItem` not current) to `--ink-2`, so the density step separates closed from live rather than current from not-current. This is ink density only — no new colour, no new weight. Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3, so the contrast pass should exclude `[aria-disabled="true"]` rather than block this. (2) Make the press visible: the suite already renders a bottom-centre strip for undo (`undoStrip()`, master.html:12747). Route the sentence the door already carries into that same strip for one beat when any `[aria-disabled="true"]` control is activated — the rail click interceptor and the sheet's handlers already have the string in hand and already call `say()`.
unadjudicated.assertion: For every `[aria-disabled="true"]` element in every state at 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, its computed `color` differs from that of a live sibling control in the same group and its computed `cursor` is not `pointer`; and after activating it by real pointer click, by Enter, and by real touch tap at 390, the sentence it carries is present in a node whose bounding rect is larger than 1x1 for at least one frame.

rounds.headline: Seven seats, 36 findings, and a round that reported itself clean when it was the heaviest since round 1. tools/round.mjs counted a refutation of the FIX as a refutation of the FINDING: 26 of 34 refutations said in their own first line that the problem is real and must not be discarded, one at severity blocking, and the refuters had kept the severity while rejecting the remedy. Corrected, the round reads 2 confirmed, 27 standing, 19% refuted, 3 blocking, 6 misleading, 18 defect. Almost every one sits in a surface this engagement built after round 3 and then ASSERTED rather than DROVE: a new project threw a TypeError and blanked the Timeline, the project menu would not close and its dismissing press fell through onto the card beneath, and the More menu painted white on white at 1.00:1 — four honest doors, present, focusable, correctly labelled and completely invisible.

confirmed.element: Timeline · `footer.b-foot` third span (`src/timeline.js:1173`), visible on `timeline.desk`, `timeline.phone` and inside Preview
confirmed.problem: The application names itself "Signal Studio" everywhere it speaks: `master.html:1` `<title>`, the rail's `aria-label` in all three products, the four honest-door sentences ("Your account, in Signal Studio…", "Every Signal Studio app in one place…", "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen.", "Also in Signal Studio"), and the dictation disclosure ("Signal Studio does not receive or retain that audio."). The products name themselves `notes.` `tasks.` `timeline.`. Exactly one string in the entire suite breaks that — `h("span", { text: o.link || "Signal Timeline" })` — and it is the last line of the guest page. Driven at 1440: on `timeline.desk` and inside Preview ("The plan as guests will see it.") the `.word` wordmark is not rendered at all, so "Signal Timeline" is the only name of the software present on the surface a guest reads. The comment at `src/across.css:384` shows the team already caught this object once and fixed its *placement* by adding the head wordmark; the words were never touched, so the page now names itself twice, in two voices, in two corners.
confirmed.consequence: The couple who open the link learn what the software is called, and they learn the wrong name. It is also the one string in the product with a growth job to do, and per the suite's own naming contract there is a separate product literally called Signal — so "Signal Timeline" is not merely unused, it is confusable with a real sibling.
confirmed.fix: `src/timeline.js:1173` → `h("span", { text: o.link || "Signal Studio" })`. A credit line credits the maker, and the maker is Signal Studio; the product is already named by the `timeline.` wordmark on the owner's view. Do not substitute "Timeline" alone — a guest needs the company name, not the module.
confirmed.assertion: No rendered string or accessible name anywhere in the suite matches /Signal (Timeline|Tasks|Notes)/; the only application name the suite renders is "Signal Studio", alongside the three lowercase wordmarks.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED. Every claim reproduces exactly, in the source and driven in Chromium at 1440x960 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…`.

SOURCE, verbatim:
- `src/timeline.js:1173` — `h("span", { text: o.link || "Signal Timeline" })`. `grep -n "link:" src/timeline.js` returns **nothing**: not one of the eight `foot(...)` call sites (1165 def; 2287, 2297, 2312, 2410, 2756, 2803, 2839) passes `link`, so the default prints on every timeline surface.
- `grep -rn "Signal Timeline" src/ master.html` returns exactly two live hits: this line and the historical narration at `src/across.css:384`. Every other suite string says Signal Studio — `master.html:1` `<title>Signal Studio</title>`; rail `aria-label` at `src/app.js:159`, `src/tasks.js:510-511`, `src/notes.js:1542`; the four door sentences at `src/app.js:101`, `src/app.js:177` ("Also in Signal Studio"), `src/tasks.js:512`, `src/notes.js:3110/3308`; the dictation line at `src/fixture.js:623`. The seat quoted all of these correctly.

DRIVEN (paper, 1440x960), `.b-foot` spans and `[data-app="timeline"] .word`:
- `timeline.desk` — foot = "Kept by Orla" / "Updated 15 July 2026" / "Signal Timeline", all three visible, 11px/400 Geist Mono rgba(17,17,17,0.62). `.word` computed `display: none` (via `src/across.css:425`, `[data-app="timeline"]:not([data-state^="owner"]) .tlHead { display: none; }`). `document.body.innerText` match on `/Signal [A-Za-z]+/g` → `["Signal Timeline"]`; `innerText.includes("Signal Studio")` → **false**.
- `timeline.phone` — identical, minus the keeper span. Same result.
- Preview (owner-flight → Preview) — strip reads "Preview · The plan as guests will see it. · Back to the plan", `.word` not visible, foot ends "Signal Timeline". Exactly as described.
- `timeline.owner-flight` — `.word` = "timeline" visible AND foot = "Signal Timeline": the page does name itself twice, in two voices, in two corners.

NOT ALREADY HANDLED, AND NOT A RE-FILE. The r1 finding `timeline-has-no-name-on-its-head` was refuted **on its fix** ("put the mark ahead of MARA & FINN, or drop the line"), and its own verdict text says, in as many words: "So the fourth-name charge is correct and independently supported" and "**The name is wrong; the line is load-bearing.**" The confirmed r1 taste finding then fixed only the placement — `panel/round-2-notes.md:32-35`: "Timeline now wears `timeline.` on its own sheet head … the footer colophon **stays**, because on a page a couple opens from a link it is provenance rather than chrome." That decision ratified the LINE, never the WORDS, and the colophon wording is absent from round 2's "Deliberate, argue but do not report as oversights" list. This finding is the unadjudicated residue with the remedy the r1 verdict itself implied, which is why it is not a re-file — refusing it on the strength of a superseded finding's id would leave a known-wrong string shipped permanently.

SEVERITY, corrected: the seat left it unstated; it is **defect**, not misleading. "Signal Timeline" is an invented name, not an untrue claim about the plan's state — the same line the r1 verdict drew, and it should hold. It is the top of the defect pile, not above the line: nothing stops working, and the artifact is unmistakably a timeline whatever the byline says.

THE FIX IS RIGHT AS WRITTEN. `o.link || "Signal Studio"` puts the maker in the credit line and leaves the product named by the `timeline.` wordmark on the owner's own head — which is precisely the division `src/across.css:423-425` already declares ("The wordmark is the OWNER's; a guest gets the artifact and the colophon"). The seat's refusal to substitute bare "Timeline" is correct: a stranger needs the company, and "Timeline" alone as a colophon is worse than what ships. Keeping `o.link` as an override is also right — it is the seam for a future white-labelled guest page.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
Take the fix as written — `src/timeline.js:1173` → `h("span", { text: o.link || "Signal Studio" })` — and add three things it omits:

1. **Record the decision where the last one was recorded.** `src/across.css:381-386` narrates this exact object's history and still quotes the old string as the thing that was moved. Extend that comment (or COMPOSITION §5, beside the two full stops) with one line: the head wordmark names the product, the colophon names the maker, and the maker is Signal Studio. Without it the next round re-files the inverse finding and someone puts "Signal Timeline" back for symmetry with `timeline.`.

2. **Do not touch the line's structure, order, or the `o.link` override.** The three-span `.b-foot` and the `keeper:false` / `stamp:false` branches are load-bearing on the phone and the empty-project states; this is a one-string change and must stay one.

3. **Declare it in the fidelity narration.** `verify.mjs:57` lists what Timeline has deliberately moved past its frozen lab ("a second composition (across) and its own wordmark on the sheet head"); the lab master at `_wt-timeline-redesign/.../master.html` still prints "Signal Timeline", so append the colophon rename to that string. Nothing fails without it — `verify.mjs:180-182` short-circuits Timeline out of the pixel gate — but the declaration is the record of why the frames differ.
confirmed.breaks:
**What it plausibly breaks — little, and I checked each gate rather than assuming.**

- **No gate asserts the string.** `grep -rn "Signal Timeline\|b-foot" verify.mjs gate.mjs interaction-check.mjs tools/*.mjs gates/*.mjs` → zero hits. `verify.mjs` §1b (`timelineArtifact`, lines 260-333) picks `.b-num .b-unit .b-when .b-who .b-todayLabel .b-origin .b-date` — the footer is not among them. §1's pixel diff exempts Timeline outright at `verify.mjs:180-182` (`if (product === "timeline") { check(… true, …); continue; }`). The §5 weight census (`timeline · 600 is exercised`, verify.mjs:402) is unaffected: this span is 400. `audit.mjs` measures palette, weight, family, ramp, leading and contrast — none move on a text swap at the same token.
- **Two characters narrower.** "Signal Studio" is 13 glyphs against 15 at 11px Geist Mono, so the `.b-foot` row gets marginally shorter. It cannot introduce a clip; it can move a wrap point. **Re-measure the foot's line count and box at 390 and 430 in `timeline.phone` and `timeline.desk`**, where the row already drops the keeper span and sits closest to wrapping. Also re-measure it in `across` at 1280 and 1440, where the foot shares a grid row that a prior round twice fought over (`src/across.css:370-380`).
- **Frames go stale.** `shots/paper-timeline.desk--1920x1000.png`, `paper-timeline.phone--1920x1000.png` and `paper-timeline.owner-flight--1920x1000.png` all carry the old byline in the bottom-right and must be re-shot. `tools/moved.mjs` will show the footer box changing width against its own snapshot — that is the expected, declared delta, not a regression, and it is the only place the change should surface.
- **The one thing to look at with human eyes after it lands:** `timeline.owner-flight` at 1440, where `timeline.` at 17/600 top-left and "Signal Studio" at 11/400 mono bottom-right are now co-visible. That pairing is correct (product mark + maker's colophon, the Stripe/Linear pattern) but it is the composition this change actually creates, and it deserves one look rather than a green check.

confirmed.seat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
confirmed.element: `.projItem[data-project="all"]` ("All projects") — `src/tasks.js:2658`
confirmed.problem: Choosing every other project row announces `"<Project name>. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` Choosing "All projects" announces `"the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` The line is `var name = (P.list.find(p => p.id === id) || {}).name || "the project";` — `P.ALL` is not a member of `P.list`, so the internal fallback literal falls straight into the live region. Confirmed by driving: `#say` reads exactly "the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it." while the head correctly repaints to "All projects · 10 of 40 done · 3 projects, day 11 of 356".
confirmed.consequence: The one switch that changes the most — from a single wedding to everything Orla is running at once — is the one the product cannot name aloud. A screen-reader user hears a sentence that begins mid-phrase and identifies nothing, so the largest context change in the application is the least legible one. It is also the studio's private placeholder text arriving in the accessibility tree, a class this library has already paid for three times.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the name before the fallback: `var row = P.list.find(function (p) { return p.id === id; }); var name = id === P.ALL ? "All projects" : (row ? row.name : null);` and if `name` is still null, say nothing rather than say a placeholder.
confirmed.assertion: At 1440x960, open `.projMenu` and activate `.projItem[data-project="all"]`: assert `#say` begins with "All projects." and contains no occurrence of the string "the project.".
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED — every claim reproduces verbatim, the code reads exactly as quoted, and no gate covers it. DRIVEN (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`), reading `#say` after each switch: - `.projItem[data-project="academic"]` → `"Academic Year 2026. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` - `.projItem[data-project="school"]` → `"Secondary School Year 2026. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` - `.projItem[data-project="all"]` → `"the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` MECHANISM, verified in source. `src/tasks.js:2658` is `const name = (P.list.find((p) => p.id === id) || {}).name || "the project";`. `src/projects.js:465-477` exposes `list` as a getter over `var PROJECTS = [ORCHARD, ACADEMIC, SCHOOL]` (line 272) and `ALL: ALL_ID` where `ALL_ID = "all"` (line 339) — a sibling key, never a member of the array. `apply()` branches on the same id (`id === ALL_ID ? applyAll() : applyProject(id)`), so the switch itself is correct; only the sentence falls through to the developer literal. Four of five rows in the menu name themselves; one speaks the fallback. 2. "Project settings come with your account." — `.ghost[aria-label="More"]`.
3. "Setting a milestone comes with the Schedule view." — `.drawerAdd`, `src/tasks.js:1298`. Reached in two clicks: Planning → Milestones tab. I inventoried it visible, `aria-disabled="true"`, label "Add a milestone".

The engagement's own instruction is to grade by driving; a copy-consistency census taken off the initial DOM was always going to miss half of it, and here the missing half reverses the conclusion.

This is a fix that already landed; the seat re-found the closed hole.

The seat's own notation gives away the measurement error. It reports `[polite] ""` — that is `#say`, the suite region built at `:9351-9367`, the only node in the document carrying a literal `aria-live="polite"` attribute. `.b-live` carries `role="status"` and no explicit attribute, so a scan keyed on `[aria-live="polite"]` misses it. Focus does land on the identical `h1`, but the region in the same subtree is not empty, and the desk state additionally draws a **visible** eyebrow: `.b-previewStrip` renders `.b-where` = "Preview" beside a "Back to the plan" button (`:19599-19605`). Driven `strip.textContent` = `"PreviewThe plan as guests will see it.Back to the plan"`. Nothing about this transition is unmarked, by eye or by ear.

Text sitting in `#say` from an earlier press is never re-read; it is inaudible, so it cannot be "the last thing said" to anyone. The one genuine residue is that `.b-live` is a **fresh node** each mount (`window.__L === document.querySelector(".b-live")` -> `false`), which is the known reliability question for freshly-inserted live regions. REFUTED — the headline is false on the seat's own repro, the cross-product comparison it argues from is false, and two of the three states it names have no undo to be mute about.

1. "Changes the data and says nothing" is wrong. I ran the seat's exact repro (chromium, 1440x960, `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`, `.b-grab` then `.b-step[data-delta="7"]` then Ctrl+Z) with a MutationObserver on every `[role="status"],[aria-live]` node. The seat enumerated `#say`, `.b-live` and `.b-undoText` and missed the one region the editor has for exactly this. Silence is not what the product does here.

2. "Notes answers 'Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.'" is false. That is Notes' undo-of-a-send sentence (`notes.js:1136,1179`), not its empty-stack answer. `doUndo()` opens `if (!undone) return false;` (`notes.js:308-309`) — no `say`. Driven on `notes.notebook` with focus on a `.railTile`, Ctrl+Z leaves `#say` at `""`; only `tasks.board` answers "Nothing left to undo." So Timeline already matches Notes, and Tasks is the outlier. The finding's premise — Timeline alone against two answering siblings — is 1-of-2, and its fix, scoped to Timeline only, would make Notes the new odd one out rather than closing an inconsistency.

3. Two of the three named states are the guest. `timeline.desk` and `timeline.phone` are the **Received** states (`STATES`, lines 67-68: "Received · phone", "Received · desk"). Measured: `.b-grab` 0, `.b-edit` absent, `.b-step` 0, `.b-undo` 0 in both. The handler exits at `if (!live) return;` because there is no bar. Making those two say "Nothing left to undo." would assert an editing model the recipient of a shared timeline does not have — the fix is worse than the silence on two of its three surfaces.

4. The fix's mechanism does not exist. It says to reuse "the same parts paintUndo writes into `.b-undoText`, turned round". Those parts are the forward sentence: `["Menu tasting at The Orchard moved ", 7, " days ", "later."]`. The exemplar reversal ("is Saturday 1 August, 16 days away") contains a date and a day count that appear nowhere in them; they come from the record after restore. Turned round mechanically, the array yields "Put back. Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days later." — the opposite of what just happened. Five entry kinds (step, rename, visibility, delete, add) each need their own reversal copy; the finding prices this as a one-line addition.

5.
