refuted.problem: One act, two vocabularies, same board, same width. At 1440x960 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.board: Space, ArrowRight, Space announces "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the in progress column." Dragging the same card with real pointer travel into the same lane announces "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company moved to the in progress column." and prints the strip "…moved to In progress · Undo · Ctrl Z". The strip therefore carries the pointer branch's verb for both routes. That is the exact rule the source states two lines above the strip's own move branch — "The strip printed 'reopened' while the live region said 'is no longer done' — one act in two vocabularies, in the same breath. refuted.why:
REFUTED — the two quoted sentences are verbatim correct, and every claim the finding builds on top of them is false.

DRIVEN, Chromium 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, card `demo-t-01` "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company", both routes into `doing`:

- Space / ArrowRight / Space → `#say` reads, in order: "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." → "In progress, position 1 of 4." → "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the in progress column." `document.querySelector(".carry")` after the drop: **null**.
- Real pointer travel (mouse.down, 20 interpolated moves, mouse.up) → `#say`: "…moved to the in progress column."; `.carry`: "…moved to In progress · Undo · Ctrl Z".

1. **"The strip therefore carries the pointer branch's verb for both routes" is false — the keyboard route has no strip.** The Space drop is `src/tasks.js:2369`, `say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".")`, and it calls no `arm()`. `arm({kind:"move"…})` exists at exactly two sites — `src/tasks.js:2775` (the card menu's "moveto") and `:2992` (`onDrop`) — and `footPill()` renders the move strip only off `undone`. There is no strip standing over the keyboard drop to be in two vocabularies with, and no "same breath" for the cited rule to govern.

2. **The rule the finding says was not carried over to the move IS carried over to the move.** The strip's move branch (`src/tasks.js:1038`) prints "moved to {Lane}"; both branches that can arm it speak "moved " + `toLane()` = "moved to the {lane} column" (`:2776`, `:3003`). Strip verb and spoken verb agree on every route that produces that strip. The rule at `:1032` is satisfied, not violated.

3. **What actually remains is a verb difference between two different gestures, and the current copy is the better of the two.** The keyboard route is a narrated carry — picked up → position → dropped — and while the card is in hand the foot pill prints, on screen, `Space drop` (`footPill()`, `:1008`; driven text "Space · drop"). "Dropped" is the closing half of "picked up" and the exact word the key legend the operator just read promised. The pointer drag narrates no pick-up; "moved to" is the whole event in one sentence. Two coherent families, each internally consistent (`endCarry` "put down in the {lane} column", Esc "Move cancelled. … is back in the {lane} column" — all `inLane`, all carry-vocabulary). This is taste stated as a defect.

4. **The fix would manufacture the defect the finding invokes.** Make the Space drop say "moved to the in progress column" and the spoken confirmation stops matching the `Space drop` keycap drawn on the sheet at the moment of the press — one act, the legend saying drop and the voice saying moved. It also strands "put down in the {lane} column" as the near-synonym for an abandoned carry against "moved to" for a deliberate one.

5. **The fix's printed half is not this finding's to make.** "all three read … 'moved to {Lane}' printed" requires the carry drop to arm an undo, which it does not; printing the strip without arming would put an Undo button over an act it does not undo (it would pop whatever is beneath in `undoHistory`). Arming it is the remedy of `carry-drop-is-not-undoable` (r3), already adjudicated. And there is no "one sentence builder": the strip uses `laneName()` (title case, no noun), the voice uses `laneMid()` + " column" (`:1474`–`:1500`) — the fix's own target strings keep the two renderings it says it is unifying.

Severity: refinement at most, not the class this seat's framing implies. Nothing is untrue on either route and nothing fails to work; two accurate sentences for two distinct gestures is not the product asserting something false.

standing.problem: Measured in chromium at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920: the field's content box is 144px at every one of them, the placeholder "Search The Orchard, events" measures 163px in the field's own computed font, and `text-overflow` computes to `clip`. The behaviour gate cannot see it: its "no silent text clipping" rule iterates elements with text child nodes, and a placeholder is an attribute, not a text node. The string is also assembled from `B.workspace`, which is unbounded operator-entered data, so the overflow grows with the venue's name.
standing.consequence: The venue's own name — the single word on the board that says whose business this is — is guillotined mid-syllable in the most prominent floating control on the sheet, at every desktop width the product ships. Lessons.md names this class twice (mid-word clamps; silent content deletion) and it is the cheapest kind of cheap.
standing.fix: Set the resting placeholder to a fixed string that fits the resting field: `' placeholder="Search tasks"'` at `src/tasks.js:948`, keeping `aria-label="Search " + esc(B.workspace)` exactly as it is so the full sentence stays in the accessible name. The field already expands on focus, which is where the workspace name can appear in full if it is wanted.
standing.assertion: At 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, for every visible `input`/`textarea`, the measured text width of its placeholder in that element's computed font is less than or equal to its content-box width.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces, and must NOT be discarded. Do not throw the observation away; throw away the remedy.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, Geist verified loaded — `document.fonts.check('13px Geist') === true`, both faces `loaded`; if it had fallen back to system-ui the string would measure 152.9px and the seat's numbers would be meaningless):
- `.dockInput` content box is exactly 144px at 768, 900, 901, 1280, 1440 and 1920. Correct, and the mechanism is right: `.dockField` is `width:196px` with `padding:0 14px 0 13px`, gap 9, icon 16 → 144. The `min-width:148px` at ≤900 (`src/tasks.css:1964`) never binds.
- `text-overflow` on `.dockInput` computes to `clip`. Correct.
- The cut is real. I screenshotted the live pill at DPR 3 and it reads "Search The Orchard, ever" with the final r sliced mid-stem, no ellipsis. The seat's visible-prefix claim is exact.
- The gate blind-spot claim is right, and understated — `interaction-check.mjs:143` bails on `if (!el.childNodes.length) continue;` before it reaches anything, `:159` requires a `nodeType === 3` child, and an input's `scrollWidth` (144) equals its `clientWidth` (144) because a placeholder does not extend scroll. Three independent reasons the rule cannot see this. Not a restatement of a gate assertion.
- The unbounded-data half is not hypothetical in this artifact, it is drivable. `[data-act="projects"]` opens a switcher with a `[data-act="rename"]` control per project. I clicked through to `data-project="school"` and the resting placeholder became "Search Secondary School Year 2026" — 213.7px in the same 144px box, rendering "Search Secondary Schoo". The seat found this by reading; it is worse when driven.

WHERE THE SEAT IS WRONG ON NUMBERS (minor, not fatal): the placeholder measures 159.2px, not 163px, so the overflow is 15.2px, not 19px. Both wrong by ~4px in the same direction, which is what you get from measuring a string rather than the rendered box.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED:
1. It breaks the visible name away from the spoken name, and says so deliberately. The seat prescribes `placeholder="Search tasks"` while keeping `aria-label="Search " + esc(B.workspace)` "exactly as it is". Today those two strings are identical. After the fix the only visible label on the control is "Search tasks" and the accessible name is "Search The Orchard, events", which does not contain it. That is a Label-in-Name divergence: a speech-input user saying "click Search tasks" gets no match on a control whose visible label is literally those words. The audit gate checks contrast, not 2.5.3, so nothing would catch it. The finding trades a cosmetic clip for a control that answers to a name it does not wear — a worse defect than the one it closes, in the one seat that should care most about what a control is called.
2. Its own consolation is not in the fix. "The field already expands on focus, which is where the workspace name can appear in full if it is wanted" — nothing in the proposed change makes it appear on focus. The placeholder is one string; setting it to "Search tasks" removes the venue from the visible surface at rest AND at focus. The sentence is doing rhetorical work the patch does not do.
3. It hard-codes a workaround at one call site for what is a containment problem, and the house already has the answer next door. `src/notes.css:802` sets `overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis` on Notes' own `.dockField span`. Tasks' `.dockInput` is the one member of the pair that diverged. The suite-level reading the seat missed is that this is Tasks drifting off a pattern the suite already ships, not Tasks needing new copy.

I applied exactly this at runtime and screenshotted it: the resting field renders "Search The Orchard, ev…". Chromium applies `text-overflow` to an input's placeholder and to its unfocused value, and it correctly does NOT apply while the field is focused and scrolling under a caret, so typing long queries is unaffected. standing.element: `src/app.js:100` — `settings: "Your workspace, your way. Not here yet."`, the Settings tile's title in all three products
standing.problem: Every other honest door says what is behind it: "Your account, in Signal Studio.", "Every project in one list.", "What came in while you were working.", "Guides and support.", "Every Signal Studio app in one place.". This one says nothing about Settings at all — it is an advertising tagline, built on possessive parallelism and an internal rhyme, and it is the only string in the entire product that behaves like marketing. The register the rest of the suite holds is plain, declarative and restrained; a rhyming slogan is the one thing that reads as cheap, and it is doing the job of describing a door.
standing.consequence: On the one occasion the suite has to be honest about something it has not built, it reaches for a slogan instead of a sentence — and the person still does not learn what Settings would contain.
standing.fix: `src/app.js:100` → `settings: "How the workspace behaves. Not here yet."` — same shape as its four siblings: a noun phrase naming what is behind the door, then the standing admission.
standing.assertion: Every honest-door sentence in `src/app.js` is a noun phrase naming the destination followed by "Not here yet."; none contains a rhetorical figure (parallel possessives, rhyme) in place of a description.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX AND ON HALF THE ARGUMENT — the narrow observation is real and should not be discarded, but the case built on it is wrong in three places and the proposed replacement is worse at this product's own stated bar.

WHAT IS TRUE. `src/app.js:100` is verbatim `settings: "Your workspace, your way. Not here yet."`. Driven in chromium against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, it is live copy, not dead: at 1440 the `.railUtil` tile is `display:grid`, `aria-label="Settings"`, `title="Your workspace, your way. Not here yet."`, and pressing it announces that exact sentence into the live region (`src/app.js:487`). At 390 the tile is `display:none` (`src/shell.css:397`) and the door moves into the plus panel (`src/app.js:151`), where it carries the same title and announces the same sentence (`src/app.js:468`). Among the five suite doors it is the only one whose first sentence is not a noun phrase naming content — home, inbox, help and me all name what is behind them. That much reproduces.

WHAT IS FALSE. (1) "an internal rhyme" — there is no rhyme. "workspace"/"way" is alliteration plus anaphora on "your". The seat names a device that is not in the string, and that device is a third of its aesthetic case. (2) "the only string in the entire product that behaves like marketing" — false, and not marginally. `src/fixture.js:617` ships `privacyLong: "Yours until you send something on"`, `:648` ships `stayedPut: "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit."`, `:611` ships `placeholder: "Write the thought before it disappears…"`. Those are possessive, rhythmic, tricolon-shaped copy, and unlike the settings string they are rendered as visible text on the sheet rather than hidden in a tooltip. The suite's register is not uniformly "plain, declarative and restrained"; Notes is deliberately warm, and this string is at worst that warmth leaking one tile too far. (3) The finding lists `"Every Signal Studio app in one place."` as one of the five honest siblings it is out of step with. That string lives at `src/tasks.js:512`, inside `rail()` — a function defined at `src/tasks.js:500` and never called anywhere in the suite, because the suite renders one rail from `src/app.js`. One of its five comparators does not render. (4) The diagnosis blames "possessive parallelism", which is contradicted by the seat's own honest list: `me: "Your account, in Signal Studio."` is possessive and the seat cites it approvingly. Possessive is not the fault; the "X, your way" tagline half is.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. `"How the workspace behaves. Not here yet."` fails the bar the codebase writes down for itself at `src/tasks.js:536-538`: "a venue manager with no project-management background understands it unaided; nothing else on this board speaks that language." Every sibling is a concrete content noun — a list, a thing that came in, guides, an account. "How the workspace behaves" is a nominalised abstraction, and "behaves" appears nowhere else in the product's copy. For Orla it is more software-vendor English than the slogan it replaces, not less. Worse, "workspace" is this codebase's name for the venue project itself: `src/fixture.js:66` sets `workspace: "The Orchard, events"` and `src/notes.js:1609` renders it as the sheet's `h1`. The definite article therefore points the sentence at the wrong object — "how The Orchard, events behaves" — where the current possessive at least reads as the app. The fix trades a tagline for an abstraction that also mis-names its referent.

SEVERITY. The seat did not class it; the correct class is refinement, not defect. Nothing is broken, nothing is asserted untrue — a settings screen genuinely would be the workspace on your terms — and the string never appears as laid-out text, only as a native tooltip and a spoken announcement. It is a one-line register wobble on the fifth-most-important door in the product.
standing.sharpenedFix: `src/app.js:100` → `settings: "Preferences and notifications. Not here yet."` — a bare noun pair, exactly the shape of its nearest sibling `help: "Guides and support."`, in words a venue manager reads unaided, with no new abstraction and no borrowed code-noun. Do NOT mirror the account door as `"Your preferences, in Signal Studio."`: making the settings tooltip a near-twin of the avatar's `"Your account, in Signal Studio."` re-opens the settings-vs-account confusion that r1's `two-account-tiles-one-honest` and r3's partly-real `two-account-tiles-on-one-screen` were narrowing, and these are the two adjacent utility controls on the same capsule.
standing.breaks: Almost nothing, which is also why the finding is not worth more than a refinement. No gate asserts the string: grepping `your way|Your workspace` across every `.mjs`, `.json`, `.md` and `.html` in the lab returns only `src/app.js:100` and the five built copies (`master.html:9215`, `_gate-suite.html:9223`, `_gate-notes.html`, `_gate-tasks.html`, `_gate-timeline.html`), so `audit.mjs` and `interaction-check.mjs` are untouched by a copy swap. Re-measure after it lands: (1) rebuild — the string is inlined into five generated HTML files, so `build.mjs` must run or the shipped gates keep announcing the old sentence while `src/` claims the new one; (2) the live-region announcement on press at both 1440 and 390, since the same string is spoken through `src/app.js:487` (tile) and `src/app.js:468` (plus-panel door) and both paths must read naturally as a spoken sentence, not just as a hover tooltip; (3) nothing reflows — the visible label in the plus panel stays "Settings" plus the `Not here yet`, and the sentence itself is a native `title`, so there is no layout risk at 390 and no need to re-shoot frames.

standing.problem: The venue name is interpolated into a placeholder that does not fit its box. REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, every geometric number reproduces, and it must NOT be discarded — do not close this observation, close it with the corrected remedy below.

WHAT I VERIFIED (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, Geist confirmed loaded via `document.fonts.check('400 13px Geist')` = true, `[...document.fonts]` shows `Geist 100 900: loaded`):

1. `src/tasks.js:948` reads exactly as quoted: `' placeholder="Search ' + esc(B.workspace) + '"'` with `B.workspace` = "The Orchard, events" (`src/fixture.js:66`). Verbatim correct.
2. `.dockInput` content box is **144.0px** at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 — invariant, because `.dockField` is a fixed `width: 196px` (`src/tasks.css:1198`) with `padding: 0 14px 0 12px`, 9px gap and a 16px icon. Exact.
3. The placeholder string measures **159.22px** in the input's own computed face (13px/400 Geist, `letter-spacing: -0.13px`). Seat said 159px. Exact.
4. Computed `text-overflow` on `.dockInput` is **clip**. Confirmed.
5. It paints cut. I cropped the resting dock at 1920 and 768 from live renders AND from the shipped frames `shots/paper-tasks.board--1920x1000.png` (2x DPR, crop at 1632,1812) and `--768x1024.png` (crop at 474,1872). Both show "Search The Orchard, ever" with the r guillotined mid-stem, exactly as claimed. The full string never fits: the field only reaches 392px on `:focus-within`/`.is-live`, by which point the placeholder is gone. At rest — the state of every shipped desktop frame — it is always cut.
6. The methodological aside is right and worth keeping: `inp.scrollWidth` = 144 = `inp.clientWidth`, `overflowX` false, while the glyphs paint cut. A scrollWidth census genuinely returns zero here. That is a real hole in the geometric gate, not an excuse.

This is also new, not a re-file. In r3 `.dockField` was a `<button>` carrying "Search The Orchard, events" in an auto-sized span (see the `search-door-answered-three-ways` adjudication, which quotes that outerHTML) — no clip. The field became a real `<input>` in this round, and the fixed 196px pill is what created the cut. Severity is **defect**: nothing is asserted untruly and nothing fails to work; it is visibly wrong on the most-photographed control on the board.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. It does not merely set the placeholder — it explicitly instructs "leave `aria-label="Search " + esc(B.workspace)` exactly as it is," and defends that as a feature. That instruction is the defect.

(a) It manufactures a WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failure (Level A). The placeholder is this control's only visible label. After the fix the visible label is "Search tasks" and the accessible name is "Search The Orchard, events" — the accessible name would not contain the visible label at all. A speech-input user saying "click Search tasks" loses the control. Trading a clipped glyph for an unreachable control is the wrong direction at this bar, and this panel has already paid for `spine-focus-ring-below-non-text-contrast` and `who-hit-target-clipped`; re-opening an A-level failure by hand is worse than the cut.

(b) It breaks the house pattern one file away. Notes' real search input, `src/notes.js:2533`, sets `aria-label="Search everything you wrote" placeholder="Search everything you wrote"` — identical strings, deliberately. In an engagement whose entire subject is the three products reading as one application, splitting Tasks' two names apart is a divergence introduced for no gain.

(c) The stated justification is measured wrong. "The venue is already stated at 20px in `.headName` 30px above the dock" is false. Driven: `.headName` sits at y=35 and the dock at y=916 at 1920; y=83.4 and y=946 at 768. The head is ~880px away at the opposite end of the sheet, not 30px above it. The venue IS in the head at 20px/600 — that part is true, and it is enough to carry the fix — but the proximity argument the seat leans on to keep the venue in the accessible name does not exist.

(d) A minor number is off: "Search tasks" measures **75.94px**, not 73px. It fits 144px either way, so this is not load-bearing, but it is wrong.

The copy instinct is right — "Search tasks" names the scope the way Notes names its scope, and it beats repeating the board's own h1 at the foot of the sheet. Only the deliberate two-name split has to go.
standing.sharpenedFix: In `src/tasks.js:948` set the placeholder AND the aria-label to the same short string: `placeholder="Search tasks" aria-label="Search tasks"`. Drop the `esc(B.workspace)` interpolation from both. "Search tasks" is 75.94px and clears the 144px content box with 68px to spare, at every width. This matches the house pattern already shipping at `src/notes.js:2533`, where Notes' search input carries the identical string in both attributes, and it keeps the visible label inside the accessible name so WCAG 2.5.3 stays satisfied. The venue is not lost: it is the sheet's own h1 at 20px/600 in `.headName`, in the same document, read by the same screen reader — an accessible name of "Search tasks" is more useful there than a second recitation of the workspace. Do NOT reach for `text-overflow: ellipsis` instead; "Search The Orchard, e…" is still bad copy, and it would only convert a hard cut into a soft one. Do NOT widen `.dockField` past 196px to make the venue fit either: the resting-to-focus growth (196→392px, `src/tasks.css:1215`) is a designed gesture, and shrinking that delta to buy room for a string that duplicates the h1 spends the wrong thing.

standing.element: Running text across the suite — `.readBody` (Notes desk), `.tpNote` (Tasks task panel), `.darkNote` (dictation), `.cardNote` (board card)
standing.problem: `text-wrap: pretty` is declared on the suite's running text (notes.css:551, :923, :1344, tasks.css:677) and is being relied on as the widow control. Driven in Chromium at 1440, lifting each of the 14 fixture notes onto the desk in turn, 5 of 14 set `.readBody` with a final visual line at ≤21% of the widest line: 480/464/**62** ("couples."), 481/489/**39** ("walk."), 418/483/**49** ("it."), 485/447/**102**, 433/431/**86**. The shipped `notes.seam` state is one of them and reproduces identically at 1280, 1440 and 1920 — it is in `shots/paper-notes.seam--1920x1000.png`. The same class is in Tasks: opening a card body gives `.tpNote` lines 513/**62** in a 517px measure at every desk width. And at 390 the dictation privacy note sets `.darkNote` at 298/319/315/287/**50** — "save." alone.
standing.consequence: The largest and most-read type in the product — the note a person opens the Notes desk to read, and the note the seam operates on — ends one paragraph in three on a single orphaned word. It is the one typographic tell that separates typeset from merely set, and it is in the surface the whole suite argument is built around.
standing.fix: Add a widow guard to the renderer for `.readBody`, `.tpNote`, `.darkNote` and `.cardNote`. After layout, build the block's visual line rects from a `Range` over its contents; while the last line is under 25% of the widest line and the last line holds fewer than three words, replace the space before the final word with U+00A0 and re-measure, capped at two joins. It must restore from the untouched source string before each run so it is idempotent, and re-run on `document.fonts.ready`, on resize, and after every repaint — a trim that runs once before the webfont swaps produces complete-looking sentences with the middle missing, which is the more expensive failure.
standing.assertion: For all 14 fixture notes lifted onto the desk at 1280/1440/1920, and for `.tpNote` and `.darkNote` wherever they render at 390/768/1280/1440/1920: the last visual line rect of the block is ≥ 25% of its widest line rect. And for each, the block's `textContent` with U+00A0 normalised back to U+0020 equals the source string character for character, so the guard is proven not to have deleted anything.
standing.verdict: REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation, and do not ship this remedy. Driven in Chromium 149 at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper`. WHAT REPRODUCES, EXACTLY. Every quoted number is verbatim right. `.readBody` across all 14 fixture notes at 1280/1440/1920, identical at all three: 5 of 14 with a last line at ≤21% of the widest — 485/447/**102** (21%), 418/483/**49** (10%), 433/431/**86** (20%), 481/489/**39** (8%), 480/464/**62** (13%). The seam state is one of them: `.readBody` in `notes.seam` measures 480/464/62 in a 496px block, last line "couples." alone. `.darkNote` at 390 measures 298/319/315/287/**50** — "save." alone. And the headline is true on its own terms: forcing `text-wrap-style: auto` on `.readBody` and re-walking all 14 gives the same 5 widows (only note 7 differs, 86 vs 42), so `pretty` is buying essentially nothing here. The artifact's own source already knows this — `src/timeline.css:1388` reads "balance, not pretty: pretty only suppresses a widow and never…". WHERE IT IS FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT THE CODE. (1) `.tpNote` does NOT carry `text-wrap: pretty`. `src/tasks.css:2263-2269` sets margin, size, weight, line-height, tracking, colour and `max-width: 52ch` and nothing else; computed `text-wrap-style` on the open task panel is `auto`. The cited `tasks.css:677` is `.cardNote`, a different class in a different component. So one of the four named elements is misattributed, and its actual condition is the artifact's own named worst case — "Greedy `wrap` was the only text in the file with no widow control at all, which is the real objection" (tasks.css:648) — not the one the finding diagnoses. (2) `.cardNote` is named in the element list and in the fix with zero evidence: I measured every `.cardNote` at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 and got 0 widows under 25% at four of the five widths and 1 of 8 at 1920 (249/60, 24%). WHY THE FIX IS UNSHIPPABLE. 1. **"Restore from the untouched source string before each run" destroys the seam's pick model.** `.readBody` is not plain text. `bodyHtmlOf()` (notes.js:770) renders it as `………` — I read that innerHTML off `notes.seam`. Those `data-i` spans are the units the arrow-key pick walks, and `.pick` is the drawn mark. A guard whose idempotency mechanism is "restore from the source string" flattens all of them on every run. I implemented the fix exactly as specified and it flattened them and changed the wrap in the process: note 10 measures 481/489/39 in the shipped tree and 481/454/76 after the guard's own restore, purely because the `.lede`/`.sent` markup was gone. Its idempotency requirement is the thing that breaks it. 2. **It fails its own acceptance test on the case it measured.** Running the guard as written on `.tpNote` (513/62): after the capped two joins it lands at 467/**109** = 23% of the widest line — still under the 25% rule the fix declares, so it gives up with two U+00A0s inserted for nothing. Two joins is the wrong cap. 3. **It leaves `pretty` in place, so the join does not land where the guard computed it.** Chromium's `pretty` re-optimises a trailing window; changing the token stream makes it re-decide. Proof from this artifact: the same `.readBody` string wraps 433/431/86 under `pretty` and 433/475/42 under `auto`. A guard that assumes joining word N−1 puts word N−1 on the last line is assuming greedy wrapping — which is exactly what `pretty` is not. This is also the file's own stated house rule, verbatim at tasks.css:650: "no text block may have two wrapping laws switched by a sibling." 4. **On `.cardNote` it collides with an existing owner of the same text node.** `trimToWord()` (tasks.js:3028), called from `retrim()` (tasks.js:3186) on layout and resize, already does `node.textContent = node.dataset.full`, binary-searches the word count against the 2-line clamp, and writes `tidy(words) + "…"`. The proposed guard wants the same trigger, the same node and its own "untouched source string". Whichever runs second destroys the first: guard-then-trim wipes the NBSP, trim-then-guard restores the untrimmed string into a clamped box and re-overflows it. The finding never mentions `trimToWord`. It also means the "last visual line" of a closed `.cardNote` ends in "…", so joining words in front of it is meaningless. 5. **"After every repaint" is the wrong hook on the gesture the suite is sold on.** Notes repaints from `selectionchange` on a 120ms debounce (notes.js:3804-3818, `pickTimer = setTimeout(offerPick, 120)`), i.e. mid-drag while a person is picking words for the seam. A separate post-repaint hook doing up to three forced synchronous layouts per block lands squarely inside that. SEVERITY. Left undeclared; it is a **defect**, not more. Nothing asserts anything untrue and nothing fails to work — it is running text that rags badly in 5 of 14 fixture notes and in one shipped frame. It is worth fixing at this bar, with the corrected remedy.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Split it by element; only one of the four needs a renderer.

**`.tpNote` (tasks.css:2263)** — it has no wrap control at all, which is the file's own named objection. It is plain escaped text (tasks.js:1161), no spans, no clamp, so it is the safe one. Add `text-wrap: pretty` there for house consistency, but do not stop: measured, that only moves 513/62 to 494/82 (17%). Include it in the guard below.

**`.readBody` and `.darkNote`** — if a guard ships, it must:
(a) never touch markup. Operate on **text nodes only** — walk the block's text nodes, replace exactly one `U+0020` with `U+00A0` via `node.nodeValue`, and undo by the reverse single-character substitution. Never `textContent = source`. `.sent[data-i]` and `.pick` must survive every run, because the arrow pick, the pointer pick and the drawn mark all address them. Character count is unchanged by the substitution, so `bodyHtmlOf`'s offset mapping and `pickedRange`'s `whole.indexOf(text)` stay aligned, and `pickedRange`'s existing `text.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` already normalises the NBSP back out of anything that crosses the seam — verify that, do not assume it.
(b) set `text-wrap-style: auto` on the guarded block so one law owns the wrap. Leaving `pretty` on means the engine re-optimises against the changed token stream and the join does not land where the guard predicted; measured, `pretty` and `auto` wrap the same `.readBody` string differently (86 vs 42).
(c) raise the cap from two joins to "until the last line is ≥25% of the widest, or four joins, whichever first" — two measurably fails (`.tpNote` 513/62 → 467/109 = 23%).
(d) run inside the existing post-layout pass, not as a new post-repaint hook: `document.fonts.ready`, a `ResizeObserver`, and the tail of the pass that already runs after each paint. Notes repaints on a 120ms `selectionchange` debounce mid-drag, so it must be cheap and it must be in that pass, not after it.

**`.cardNote`** — exclude it. 0 widows at 390/768/1280/1440, 1 of 8 at 1920 (249/60, 24%), it is clamped to two lines, and `trimToWord()` already owns its `textContent` and `dataset.full` on the same triggers. If it is guarded at all, the join belongs *inside* `trimToWord`, applied to the already-trimmed string after the binary search, and only on `[data-open]` cards where nothing is trimmed.

standing.fix: Both levers verified live at 390 with touch. standing.assertion: At 390×844 with `hasTouch`, for each of the three head chips pressed in turn, and for the strip that appears after a tick and after a carry-drop: `.carryName.scrollWidth <= .carryName.clientWidth + 1`, and the `.carry` pill's bounding rect stays fully inside the viewport.

It is also correctly distinguished from the closed undo-strip findings: this is the `filtering()` branch at tasks.js:1056-1057, a different string beside a different button, and it is persistent state rather than a transient strip.

The finding presents both levers as "verified live" and then quotes "238px box, 238px content" — but that 238 content is the wrapped measurement from lever 2, not a fit that lever 1 achieved. Lever 1 contributes nothing to the defect it is offered for.

2. Lever 1 costs the exact defect this branch records having closed. standing.element: .rail button[data-rail="plus"] (accessible name "More") — at 1440 it sits at 28,800; at 390 at 243,783
standing.problem: The rail's live More door is drawn with the SVG path `M12 5.5v13M5.5 12h13` — byte-identical to every create control in the suite: the five `.trayAdd` "Add here" buttons, the dock's `.dockPrimary` "Add task", and the phone capsule's own `.railAdd`. I dumped path data across every visible button on tasks.board at 1440: the plus path appears eight times, seven of them are add, one of them is More. Pressing it opens `.morePop` — All projects, Inbox, Help, all three `aria-disabled` and all three "Not here yet". At 390 the two are adjacent inside one capsule: More at x=243, Add task at x=295, both 44×44, and the only difference is that one is a ghost outline and one a white fill.
standing.consequence: Orla reaches for the plus on the persistent spine to make something — a note, a task, a moment — and gets a menu of three things that do not exist. The suite's most reliable convention (a plus creates) is spent, at every width, on the one object that is supposed to prove the three products are one application. She learns not to trust the spine.
standing.fix: Give the rail's More door its own mark and reserve the plus path for controls that create. Use the three-dot mark the suite already carries for a menu of secondary things — `circle;circle;circle`, the path already on `.headAct` "Notes options" — and while you are there rename `.cardDots`, currently drawn with that same three-dot mark but labelled "Move this task", to "Task menu" so the mark means one thing everywhere.
standing.assertion: On tasks.board at 390 and at 1440, no visible button whose accessible name is not an add action renders an SVG whose concatenated path data equals that of `.dockPrimary`; and inside `.rail` no two visible buttons share identical SVG path data.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation, but do not ship this remedy, because both halves of it make the work worse and the second half makes an honest label dishonest.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven in chromium against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…` across all eight states at 1440 and 390. `util("plus", "More", …)` at line 9294 renders `I[key]`, so the live More door is literally emitted with `I.plus` = `<path d="M12 5.5v13M5.5 12h13"/>`. No CSS rotates or otherwise differentiates it. Geometry exact: 1440 → More at 28,800, 44×44; 390 → More at 243,783 and `.railAdd` "Add task" at 295,783, both 44×44, distinguished only by fill (`rgba(0,0,0,0)` + `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)` vs `rgb(255,255,255)` + `rgb(17,17,17)`). The panel it opens is `.morePop role="menu"` with All projects / Inbox / Help, all three `aria-disabled` and all three "Not here yet". That much is exact and it is a genuine defect.

WHAT IS FACTUALLY WRONG. The headline count is wrong in the finding's own stated evidence. "I dumped path data across every visible button on tasks.board at 1440: the plus path appears eight times, seven of them are add." It appears SEVEN times at 1440 — More, five `.trayAdd`, one `.dockPrimary`. `.railAdd` is a ≤720 object (`display: grid` only inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`), so it is not in a 1440 dump at all; the seat listed a phone control as part of a desk measurement. Six add, one More.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG — HALF ONE. The same 1440 dump the seat says it took already contains a `.ghost` button whose accessible name is "More", at 1357,31, drawn with `circle;circle;circle` — the three-dot mark, `aria-disabled`, title "Project settings come with your account." Give the rail's More the three-dot mark and tasks.board at 1440 carries two controls named "More" wearing an identical glyph, one live and opening a real panel, one a dead door. That trades a mark collision for a full identity collision — same name AND same mark, one working, one not — which is strictly worse than what ships. The fix also defeats its own stated goal: at 1440 tasks.board the dots mark already carries two meanings (the closed "More" door; twelve `.cardDots`) and in Notes a third (`.headAct` "Notes options"). Adding a fourth is not "the mark means one thing everywhere".

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG — HALF TWO. Renaming `.cardDots` from "Move this task" to "Task menu" makes an accurate label inaccurate. `cardMenu()` at line 10796 emits `role="menu" aria-label="Move <title>"` containing exactly one heading, "Move to", and the five lane buttons. Nothing else. "Move this task" is the honest name for that; "Task menu" promises a menu of task actions that does not exist, and would leave the menu's own aria-label and its "Move to" heading contradicting the button that opened it.

SEVERITY, CORRECTED. Defect, not misleading. The glyph asserts create and the control does not create — but only at glyph level: the accessible name is "More", it carries `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and on six of eight states ("More" is the only plus on screen in all three Notes and all three Timeline states at 1440) there is nothing to confuse it with. The collision is live on Tasks only. Visibly wrong, passable.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Use the mark the suite already owns and is not using. `ICON.more` — `rect;rect;rect;circle(fill)`, the 2×2 app grid with a filled dot — is defined on the same 24 grid at 1.6 stroke and is rendered nowhere in the suite: it survives only in the dead standalone `rail()` at line 10241 (`.railMark`), which I confirmed is never in the DOM in any of the eight states at either width. The rail's own build note says of that mark that it "read as a menu and invited a press" — which is precisely what the More door is, and its panel heading is already "Also in Signal Studio", so an app-grid mark is semantically exact.

Smallest correct edit: `util(key, label, extra)` at line 9265 hardcodes `I[key]`. Give it an icon override — `util(key, label, extra, icon)` emitting `(icon || I[key])` — and call `util("plus", "More", …, I.more)`. Keep `data-rail="plus"` as the address so the four sites that resolve it by key are untouched: the outside-click guard (~9585), the toggle (~9604), the arrow-walk guard (~9654), and `paintRail`'s focus restore by `data-rail`. Renaming the key to "more" requires all four plus the focus-restore to change together and buys nothing.

Leave `.cardDots` alone. If the panel wants the dots mark to mean one thing, the control to rename is the head `.ghost` currently named "More" with title "Project settings come with your account." — call it "Project settings", title unchanged. That removes the duplicate "More" name from tasks.board and leaves the dots meaning one thing: an overflow menu for the object it sits on, which `.cardDots` ("Move this task") and `.headAct` ("Notes options") both already satisfy.

If the sharpened fix lands: `I.more` carries a filled `circle r=2.2` at 16.75,16.75, and the rail's own build record says that exact shape "carried a filled dot… that read as a notification badge at 19px" when it sat on the brand. Re-run `audit.mjs --lab=…` and `interaction-check.mjs`, and confirm the `moreOpen` toggle, the outside-click close, and the arrow-walk still resolve the tile — a key rename here silently kills all three and the failure is invisible in a frame. standing.element: `.rail [data-rail="plus"]` at 28,800 and `.ghost` at 1357,31, both `aria-label="More"`, on tasks.board at 1440
standing.problem: Two controls visible at once carry the accessible name exactly "More". One is live and opens the suite doors; the other is a closed door about project settings. They wear different glyphs, and the conventional reading of each glyph is backwards: the head's `···` is the shut one, the rail's `+` is the live menu. Worse, the head control is named "More" in Tasks and "Notes options" in Notes — the same object, the same mark, two names, in one application.

A sighted user learns the word twice and has to learn it a third time when she crosses into Notes. It reads as three teams shipping into one shell, which is the exact impression this artefact exists to defeat.
standing.fix: Name the rail door "Also in Signal Studio" — the sentence its own menu already prints as its heading — and name the sheet-head `···` control "<Product> options" in all three products, matching the string Notes already uses.
standing.assertion: In every state at 1440, no two simultaneously visible controls share an identical accessible name; and the sheet-head `···` control's accessible name is "Tasks options", "Notes options" or "Timeline options" in the respective product.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — the observation is exact and must NOT be discarded; the remedy as written is factually wrong in one half and does not close the hole in the other.

VERIFIED (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…`). Every fact in the PROBLEM reproduces to the pixel:

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, click `[data-rail="plus"]`, then Tab):
tab1 `.moreItem[data-door=home]`, tab2 `inbox`, tab3 `help`, tab4 `.projSwitch` ("The Orchard, events"). At tab4 and every tab after it: `.morePop` present, `visibility:visible / opacity:1 / display:grid`, box exactly x=92 y=729 w=216 h=151, and `[data-rail="plus"]` still `aria-expanded="true"`. The seat also under-reports its own case. `src/tasks.css:1381-1383` hard-codes `.axis i { width: 11.3% }` and `.axis b { left: 11.3% }` — 11/97, The Orchard's day 11. 1. "Drop `period`" ships a crash. `replace()` (`src/projects.js:281-301`) has no guard and does `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(source[k]))` for every key in `BOARD_KEYS`, which includes `"period"`. With the key absent that is `JSON.parse(undefined)` → "SyntaxError: \"undefined\" is not valid JSON" (verified in node). `commitName` calls `P.apply(id)` the instant the name is committed, so the very gesture the finding is about would throw before `mount()`, leaving the switcher open and the board unchanged. `period` must be `null`, not absent — which is why the seat's own sentence nulls the other three and drops only this one.

2. "Render the head's third fact only when a period exists" contradicts the head the seat asks for. `src/tasks.js:784` is `esc(B.season) + ", day " + p.day + " of " + p.of` — one fact. Suppress it and "New project" goes with it, so the head reads "Nora & Cian · Thu 16 Jul" and stops, not "…· New project" as the fix claims. The season word has to survive; only the day clause is conditional. And the condition belongs on `p.day`/`p.of`, not on `period` — the numbers are what would print "day null of null".

3. The fix leaves the path that writes the string back. `renameProject` (`src/projects.js:414`) rebuilds `planning.line = p.kind + " · " + p.board.period` on every rename. Null the period and rename "Nora & Cian", and the drawer prints "New project · null" — worse than what was removed, on the one project the fix exists to protect.

4. `left: 96` is dead. Nothing reads `progress.left` anywhere in `src/` (only `.left` on DOMRects). Nulling it is harmless but is not part of the repair.

REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces almost verbatim, and must NOT be discarded. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 against _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board.

WHAT REPRODUCES EXACTLY

Press Escape -> menu still present and visible, `aria-expanded` still "true", `#say` still "Projects, open." The four `[data-act="tool"]` siblings all behave correctly by contrast: share/filter/sort/display each close on Escape, reset `aria-expanded` to "false", and put focus back on their own trigger. Confirmed in source: `onKey`'s Escape ladder handles `toolOpen`, `dayFor`, `closeMenu()`, `carriedId`, `openTaskId`, `openNoteId`, the filters and the drawer — `projOpen` appears nowhere in it.
- Outside press: with the menu open I clicked (761,264) — `elementFromPoint` is `.cardNote` — and got exactly the seat's result: menu still present, `aria-expanded` "true", `#say` "Approve the final seating plan. Task open.", `.taskPanel` in the DOM. On an inert spot (the tray at 1277,850) the share pop closes (1 -> 0 `.toolPop`) and the project menu does not. Confirmed in source: the light-dismiss block at the head of `onClick` tests `toolOpen` only.
- Arrows: focus `.projItem` #1, then ArrowDown / ArrowUp / ArrowRight / Home / End / typeahead "a" — focus never moves off row one.
- Tab: from `.projSwitch`, five presses land on the "1 today" chip with the menu still open. "Walks straight out of it" is loose (it passes item 1 and three `.projEdit` rename buttons first) but the count and the destination are exact.

The severity is in fact UNDERSTATED, and I am correcting it up to blocking on a ground the finding only brushes. Measured focusables inside `.projMenu`: `projItem|ti=0`, `projEdit|ti=0`, `projItem|ti=-1`, `projEdit|ti=0`, `projItem|ti=-1`, `projEdit|ti=0`, `projItem projAll|ti=-1`, `projItem projNew|ti=-1`. Only the CURRENT project is reachable. With no roving and no `aria-activedescendant`, a keyboard operator cannot select Academic Year 2026, Secondary School Year or All projects, and cannot press New project — at all. A `role="listbox"` where four of five options are unreachable is the product not doing what it says.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED

1. It contradicts itself and re-opens a paid-for defect. It says "route `.projMenu` through the same dismissal model as `toolOpen`" and then specifies a DIFFERENT model: `pointerdown`, and "the outside press consumed rather than passed through." The `toolOpen` model is `click`, and it deliberately does not consume — it closes and lets the press continue. This file already paid for the seat's version: the comment at ~13246 records "The light-dismiss handler is gone. One panel was running two contradictory input models... a real press on a card's tick with the drawer open closed the drawer and did not complete the task." Consuming the dismissing press would put that back, and would make the project menu the one surface in the head that answers a press differently from its four siblings — the exact inconsistency the finding was filed about.

2. `pointerdown` is wrong for the same documented reason. The comment at ~13253 records "The repaint waits for the click. Repainting here destroys the control the press landed on before its click can fire." A `pointerdown` handler that calls `mount()` destroys the element under the pointer before its click lands.

3. The product-switch clause chases a non-defect. After clicking `[data-rail="notes"]` I measured the Tasks app: `hidden` present and `inert === true`, and `.projSwitch` rect is 0x0. The "stranded" `aria-expanded="true"` is outside the accessibility tree and outside the tab order — nothing is stranded. Clearing it also cuts against the locked architecture's "none ever torn down, so nothing a person was doing is lost."

4. The roving clause is wrong on its own stated premise and on its selector. "The five `.projItem` rows... they already carry `role='option'`" is false for one of the five: `.projNew` is `<button class="projItem projNew" data-act="project-new" tabindex="-1">` with NO role (measured: option/option/option/option/**null**). Worse, `.projItem` also matches the inline rename and new-project rows, which render as `<div class="projItem" data-editing>` wrapping the `.projField` input (source ~10332 and ~10366) — a roving model keyed on `.projItem` would try to focus a non-focusable div and would yank focus out of the field mid-rename.

Four changes, three of them different from the finding's.

1. ESCAPE (keep, as written, with one siting constraint). Add a `projOpen` branch to the Tasks Escape ladder in `onKey`, sited immediately after the `toolOpen` branch and before `dayFor`, mirroring `toolOpen` exactly: `event.preventDefault(); projOpen = false; projEdit = null; projNew = false; mount(); const back = document.querySelector('[data-act="projects"]'); if (back) back.focus(); say("Projects, closed."); return;`. The existing `.projField` keydown listener (~13194) already calls `stopPropagation()` on Escape, so a rename in progress keeps its own meaning — verify that still holds after the branch lands.

2. OUTSIDE PRESS (rewrite). Extend the EXISTING click-time light-dismiss block at the head of `onClick` (~12139) — not a new `pointerdown` listener, and NOT consuming: `if (projOpen) { const inside = event.target.closest && (event.target.closest(".projMenu") || event.target.closest('[data-act="projects"]')); if (!inside) { projOpen = false; mount(); } }`. This is literally the same model as the four tool pops, which is what the finding asked for. Note the card case is a shared bug, not a project-menu bug: with the SHARE pop open I clicked the same (761,264) and it also survived while the panel opened, because the card's own open path repaints before `onClick`'s dismiss block sees the press. If that matters, fix it once in the card path for all five surfaces — do not give the project menu a private model to paper over it.

3. PRODUCT SWITCH (drop). Measured `hidden` + `inert` + 0x0 on the whole Tasks app after switching to Notes. There is nothing to fix.

4. KEYBOARD (widen and re-key). Rove over `.projItem[role="option"]:not([data-editing])` — never bare `.projItem` — with ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home/End, and Enter/Space to select, moving real focus and keeping `tabindex="0"` on exactly one row. Give `.projNew` its own explicit tab stop rather than sweeping it into the option ring, since it carries no `role` and is not an option. While there, decide what the three `tabindex="0"` `.projEdit` rename buttons are doing as non-option children of a `role="listbox"` — they are why Tab currently reaches three rename controls before leaving the menu, and they are invalid listbox content.

REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, every measurement reproduces exactly, and it must NOT be discarded. The remedy as written recreates the collision it was raised to remove.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…`)

- `railHtml()` at `_gate-suite.html:9295` renders `util("plus", "More", …)`, and `util` emits `I[key]` — so the More tile draws `I.plus`. `_gate-suite.html:9302` renders `.railAdd` with `I.plus`. `I.plus` is defined once at `_gate-suite.html:9068` as `s('<path d="M12 5.5v13M5.5 12h13"/>')`. Byte-for-byte identical, exactly as claimed.
- 390x844, `tasks.board`, driven: `[data-rail="plus"]` at x=243 y=783, 44x44, aria "More"; `[data-rail="add"]` at x=295 y=783, 44x44, aria "Add task". 52px apart, same capsule, same single path. Exact.
- 768/1280/1440/1920: `[data-rail="add"]` computes `display:none` (`.railAdd { display: none; }`, `_gate-suite.html:411`); `.dockPrimary` is visible carrying `I.plus` + the word "Add task". So at desk the rail-foot plus IS "More" and a second plus sits below it spelling itself out. Exact.
- Neither rail utility carries a word — `util()`'s own comment says so deliberately ("a utility is not a destination").
- `.morePop` copy is verbatim as quoted.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED

1. It moves the collision, it does not remove it. At 1440x960 on `tasks.board` I measured TWO buttons on screen at once whose accessible name is the string "More": the rail tile (x=28 y=800, 19x19 svg, `I.plus`, on ink) and the Tasks head's ghost (x=1357 y=31, 15x15 svg, `I.dots`, title "Project settings come with your account."). Today they differ in glyph. Give the rail tile `I.dots` and they become identical in glyph AND identical in accessible name, on the same screen, going to two different places — one opens the suite door bank, the other is a closed door. That is strictly worse than what is there now, and it is the finding's own charge ("the same glyph means two different things on the same screen") reproduced with the one disambiguator left removed.

2. `I.dots` is already a load-bearing word in this product and it is not "the rest of the suite". It is used at `_gate-suite.html:10117` (card menu, "Move this task"), `:10529` (Tasks head "More"), `:14965` ("Notes options"), `:15283` and `:15517` ("More actions for this note"). Everywhere, dots means *an overflow menu for the object you are looking at*. The suite door bank is not an overflow menu for the current sheet; it is a cross-application switcher. The fix would make dots carry a third, categorically different sense, which is the same class of defect one level up.

3. There is already a correct asset in the set and the finding missed it. `window.ICON.more` is live at runtime (I checked: true on every state) and is `s('<rect x="4" y="4" …/><rect x="13.5" y="4" …/><rect x="4" y="13.5" …/><circle cx="16.75" cy="16.75" r="2.2" …/>')` — the 2x2 app grid with a dot. It is rendered nowhere in the suite (`.railMark` is absent at every width/state I drove); its only consumer is the dead standalone Tasks `rail()` at `_gate-suite.html:10241`, where its authored caption is literally "Every Signal Studio app in one place." That is the exact meaning the finding asks for, at the same zero-new-asset cost it claims for dots. The suite's `railBrand` comment rejects this glyph as a *brand* because it "read as a menu and invited a press that went nowhere" — which is an argument FOR it here, where it is a menu and the press goes somewhere.

4. Craft detail both fixes must respect and the finding does not mention: `data-rail="plus"` is hardcoded three times — the outside-click close (`:9585`), the Escape-refocus (`:9646`), and the panel-open lookup (`:9604`) — and the roving-tabindex state `railCurrent` is keyed off it. The key must stay `"plus"`; only the glyph moves. `util()` currently derives its icon as `I[key]`, so it needs an explicit icon argument. Renaming the key to match the new glyph silently kills Escape-to-close and outside-click-to-close, both of which I drove working today.

SEVERITY: defect, not blocking or misleading. Both controls have correct accessible names, both carry correct `title` at desk, and both do what their names say — the product is not lying and it is not failing to do what it says. The damage is a glance-level ambiguity, worst on a phone where no tooltip ever appears. Visibly wrong, passable.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, ?v=paper&state=notes.notebook). The duplication is exact, not merely similar.
