WHERE IT IS WRONG.

1. The responsive carve-out is inverted, and both halves are false. "Below 721 the desk sheet's pair stays" — it does not exist below 721: `topSheet()` returns "" when `phone.matches` (src/notes.js:1752-1753), and I measured `.verb` = [] at 390x844 and 720x900. "That is where the dock's glyphs give way to the phone capsule" — they do not give way: the phone dock carries the same two glyphs (src/notes.js:1655-1656), measured at 390 as Dictate@55,787 and Read a photo@93,787, and at 720 as @55,843 / @93,843. So the dock pair is present at every width and the desk pair only ≥721. The seat's stated reason for the split is the exact opposite of the code, which means the ≥721 condition was never checked.

2. The 1440 row is a hybrid. At 1440x960 the dock glyphs measure 838,883 and 877,883 — not y=923. 923 is the 1920x1000 value (there the verbs are at 887,193 / 978,193, not 706/797). "730px below" is likewise the 1920 delta; at 1440 the gap is 690px. The x values are 1440's and the y values are 1920's.

3. It deletes the wrong copy, and does not name what that costs. The `.verb` pair is the only worded exposure of these two actions on a desk. After the fix, at ≥721 they exist only as two 17px unlabelled glyphs. `I.photo` (src/icons.js:66) is a generic landscape/image mark — rect, sun, mountain — which in a note dock reads "attach an image", not "read the words off a printed run-sheet". For the named persona that is the difference between finding the feature and never finding it. The fix also leaves `.deskAside` — a ruled margin measured at 684x119 at 1440 built to carry two 53px facts — holding one, and at ≤1280 that margin flips to a full-width bordered row (notes.css:1481-1482) with a single "FILING UNDER" chip stranded in it. Neither consequence is mentioned.

4. The seat's implied argument for the dock — that it is the persistent one — does not hold in the state where the collision occurs. Only `.index` scrolls (measured scrollers at 721/1280/1440: `index` only); after a 900px wheel the `.verb` pair is still at y=193. In the resting state the desk pair is exactly as persistent as the dock's.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT AND SHOULD NOT BE TOUCHED: the dock is already sole owner wherever the desk pair is absent — `.verb` = [] in notes.seam, in the opened-note read view, and at every width ≤720, and in all of those the dock keeps voice and photo.

SEVERITY: defect, not more. Nothing on screen is wrong and nothing untrue is asserted; the cost is four tab stops for two actions and one statement made twice.
standing.sharpenedFix: Invert the owner. Keep the worded desk pair as the single owner in the one state where it exists, and stand the dock's voice/photo glyph pair down there: suppress `.dock .dockGlyph[data-act="voice"|"photo"]` when `!phone.matches && !openId` — i.e. exactly when `topSheet()` renders `.top`. Leave the `.verb` pair and the "Other ways in" label alone; leave the dock pair untouched everywhere else. The dock already restructures on open (it gains `backToWriting`'s `write` glyph plus a rule at src/notes.js:1642-1646), so this uses machinery that ships. Result: exactly one owner per action in every state — desk words while composing, dock glyphs while reading, searching, in the seam, and at every width ≤720 — with the worded form shown wherever a worded form can exist, and the `.deskAside` keeps both of its facts. Notes' resting loop drops from 16 stops to 14 and the dock's run becomes search → account. If the founder instead wants the dock to survive, it is only shippable with words attached, and there is no `.dockField`-style worded slot for two more controls inside a 413px capsule — which is itself the argument for the desk owning them.
standing.breaks:
The finding's fix as written: at ≥721 it is a plain deletion (the condition it names is inert, since the desk sheet does not render below 721), so it would break discoverability of "Read a photo" — the action survives only as a generic image glyph — and it would leave `.deskAside` half-empty. Re-measure after it: the aside at 1440/1920 (today 684x119 and 802x119 with two 53px facts) and its ≤1280 horizontal form, plus the `.top[data-two]` grid balance once column 2 carries one fact against a full-height writing column.

My sharpened fix: the capsule pulses wider on open. Measured today, the dock is centred at ~761.5 and runs 413px@x555 at rest, 464px@x529 with a note open — a 51px swing, 25px per edge. With the pair stood down at rest it measures 335px@x594, so the swing grows to 129px, 64px per edge. Re-measure that at 721 (narrowest desk, where a 413px dock already sits in a 721px viewport) and at 1920, and confirm on the open/close transition that it reads as the capsule following the sheet it opened rather than as a jump — if it does not, hold the resting dock's width with a spacer rather than restoring the duplicate. Also re-run the focus-order and hit-target gates (`audit.mjs`, `interaction-check.mjs`) for Notes: the resting tab loop changes from 16 stops to 14, and any assertion that walks the dock's glyph run past `search` must be re-read.

standing.element: `.morePop`, opened from the rail tile labelled "More" — every state, both variants, 390 through 1920
standing.problem: The menu is painted for the ink floor — panel `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)`, item colour `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)` — but it opens at x=92 with a 216px width against a white sheet whose left edge is x=100. Driven at 1440: 208 of its 216px land on white. At 768 it is 214 of 216; at 390 the pop is at 157..373 inside a sheet spanning 9..381, so all of it lands on the sheet, over the board. I pixel-scanned the shipped 390 render: the four rows (All projects, Inbox, Help, Settings) sample 255,255,255 with the darkest pixel in row 1 at 229 — that is the card border behind it, not the label. Contrast ≈ 1.02. Identical at v=ink, because the sheet is `rgb(255,255,255)` in both variants. The only thing that reads is the ink-coloured eyebrow "ALSO IN SIGNAL STUDIO". The audit's contrast check cannot see this because the menu does not exist until it is pressed.
standing.consequence: Orla presses the one door in the spine that leads to All projects, Inbox, Help and Settings and the application appears to do nothing at all. On the phone a stray line of type lands on top of a task card and nothing else appears. The brief's protected object — honest doors that "say plainly that they are not here yet" — is defeated, because all four sentences are unreadable.
standing.fix: Give `.morePop` the paint `.cardMenu` already uses correctly on the sheet: `background:#ffffff`, item colour `#111111`, the sheet's elevation shadow and radius, and the second line of each disabled item at the same ink alpha Tasks uses on `[aria-disabled="true"]` in the head. Keep the eyebrow as it is; it is the only part currently legible and it is already ink.
standing.assertion: With the More menu open, at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 in both `v=paper` and `v=ink`, every `.moreItem` label has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 measured against the composited pixels actually painted behind it in a rendered screenshot — sampled from the PNG, not from computed style.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, blocking, and must NOT be discarded. Every observation reproduces, and the fix as written changes nothing about it.

WHAT I CONFIRMED, driven in chromium against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, pressing `[data-rail="plus"]` and pixel-scanning the resulting frame:
- Geometry, exact. 1440: `.morePop` at x=92, w=216, right=308; the ink column left of the sheet is 8px wide (1197 dark pixels over 151 rows), so the sheet edge is x=100 and 208 of 216px land on white. 768: pop 86..302, ink column 2px, 214 of 216 on white. 390: pop 157..373, rail/dock 9..381, zero ink pixels — all of it on the sheet. Seat's numbers are right to the pixel.
- Paint, exact. `background-color` computes `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)`; `.moreItem` computes `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)`. Identical at `v=ink`.
- The consequence is worse than "≈1.02". At 1440 the three item rows (110..300 × each 36px band) sample **one unique colour, 255,255,255, across all 6840 pixels of every row**. Not low contrast — zero. Contrast 1.00. At 390 all four rows are the same, the only non-white pixels being board content bleeding through the 7% panel. The eyebrow is the only legible element, exactly as claimed.
- Neither gate can see it: `audit.mjs` and `interaction-check.mjs` contain no reference to `morePop` or `data-rail="plus"`, so the menu is never opened for either.

Two mechanisms the seat did not find, and they are why the fix fails:
1. `--float`, `--ring`, `--ink-3`, `--wash`, `--r-ctl` are declared only inside `[data-app="tasks"]` (line 801 etc.). `.rail`/`.morePop` live in the deck shell, outside it. So `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--chrome-line), var(--float)` at line 593 is invalid-at-computed-value-time and computes to **`none`** today — the panel has neither ring nor elevation right now. `--on-ink-3` is likewise absent from `:root`, so `.morePop p { color: var(--on-ink-3) }` is invalid and the eyebrow's ink is inherited by accident, not designed. The file's own `:root` comment documents this exact hazard ("a rail rule reaching for `--t-11` resolved to nothing").
2. `.rail [aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--on-ink-2) }` (line 442, specificity 0,2,0) outranks `.moreItem` (0,1,0), and every door carries `aria-disabled="true"`.

I APPLIED THE PROPOSED FIX VERBATIM, injected last in the cascade, and re-scanned:
`.morePop{background:#ffffff;box-shadow:var(--ring),var(--float);border-radius:var(--r-sheet)} .moreItem{color:#111111} .moreItem em{color:var(--ink-3)}`
Result: panel → `rgb(255,255,255)`; **box-shadow → `none`**; **item colour → still `rgba(255,255,255,0.62)`**; em → still white. Rows 1–3 re-scan to **min 255, max 255, one unique colour** — pixel-for-pixel unchanged. The fix trades a faint 7% tint for a pure-white slab with no ring and no shadow on a white sheet, and leaves all four doors invisible. It is strictly worse than what ships.

Severity, corrected upward if the seat classed it below blocking: the honest doors are a protected object whose entire justification is that they are "present, reachable, and say plainly that they are not here yet". Four of them render at contrast 1.00. The product does not do what it says.

Direction is also wrong. `.cardMenu` is white because it is the sheet's object; `.morePop` is the rail's drawer, and the source says so at line 585 ("The panel is chrome, not sheet: it is the rail's own object and it wears the rail's ink"). The cheap correct move is to make that ground opaque so it carries its own ink wherever it lands — not to convert a chrome object into a sheet object anchored to and 8px overlapping a dark capsule.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Keep the panel the rail's object; give it an opaque ground and fix the two dead-token bugs underneath. Driven and pixel-verified at 1440:

1. `:root` — declare what the shell actually reaches for: `--on-ink-3: rgba(255,255,255,0.42)` and an on-ink elevation token, e.g. `--float-ink: 0 2px 6px rgba(17,17,17,.30), 0 16px 36px rgba(17,17,17,.36)`. Without this every remedy here silently no-ops the same way the current declaration does.
2. `.morePop` — `background: var(--ink-1)` (opaque #111111, in palette; if you want it to match the capsule's exact value use `background: linear-gradient(var(--chrome), var(--chrome)), var(--ink-1)`, both stated colours at stated alpha — check it against the palette lock either way), and `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--chrome-line), var(--float-ink)`. Keep radius 16px.
3. Beat the `.rail [aria-disabled="true"]` rule at 0,2,0 or higher — `.moreItem { color: … }` alone is dead: `.rail .moreItem[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--on-ink-1) }`, `.rail .moreItem[aria-disabled="true"] em { color: var(--on-ink-2) }`, `.rail .moreItem[aria-disabled="true"] svg { color: var(--on-ink-2) }`.
4. Eyebrow to `var(--on-ink-2)`, not `--on-ink-3`: it is 11px uppercase, and 0.42 white on ink is ~2.9:1 and fails AA at that size. Do not "keep it as it is" — its ink today is an inherited accident of an undeclared token and it inverts to ink-on-ink the moment the ground goes dark.

Measured result of the above, same scan windows: panel ground rgb(34,34,34); door name white on it ≈14.9:1; "Not here yet" and the eyebrow at 0.62 white ≈6.9:1; rows re-scan to 141–167 unique colours instead of 1. Three legible tiers, all above AA, and the panel keeps the identity the source argues for.
standing.breaks:
What it would plausibly break, and what to re-measure:

- Palette lock. `linear-gradient(var(--chrome), var(--chrome)), var(--ink-1)` introduces no hue but may trip a literal-value scan in `audit.mjs`. Re-run the palette gate; if it objects, ship plain `var(--ink-1)` — the panel is a detached floating object with its own shadow, so the small tonal step off the capsule reads as separation, not error.
- Hoisting `--on-ink-3` to `:root` changes any shell-scope rule currently relying on it being invalid-and-inherited. The only two consumers outside `[data-app]` are `.morePop p` and `.moreItem em`, and step 4 reassigns both — but grep the shell block again after the change and re-shoot all eight states at 1440 to confirm nothing else in the rail or dock shifts colour.
- The shadow becomes real for the first time. At 1440/1920 the panel's lower-left corner and its 8px overlap of the ink column now cast onto the sheet edge; at 390 it casts onto the board. Re-shoot `tasks.board` at 390/768/1440/1920 with the menu open and check the shadow does not muddy the card row behind it or the dock's top edge.
- `.moreItem:hover { background: var(--chrome-active) }` was designed for an ink ground and now finally sits on one — verify hover still reads and that `.railTile[data-open]` and the panel do not fight at the seam where the pop meets the capsule.
- Most important: this whole class is invisible to automation because neither gate ever presses `[data-rail="plus"]`. Add a step to `interaction-check.mjs` that opens the More menu and a contrast assertion in `audit.mjs` that composites `.morePop` against its real backdrop in both variants at 390/768/1440/1920. Without that, the next repaint of the rail can re-open this defect and both gates will still be green.

standing.element: Tasks keyboard carry model against `.taskPanel` (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`) — reproduced at 1440x960, present at every width
standing.problem: Driven, in order, on the first card. Space: "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." ArrowRight: lane counts go 3,3,2,0,5 → 2,4,2,0,5 and it announces "In progress, position 1 of 4." Enter: the modal task panel opens and announces "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company. Task open." — the carry is never ended, `carriedId` is still set, and nothing spoken or drawn says the card is still in the air. Escape: the keydown handler takes the carry-cancel branch before the open-panel branch, so it reverts the move (counts back to 3,3,2,0,5), leaves the dialog open, and lands focus on the card behind the modal scrim — I confirmed `document.elementFromPoint` at the focused element's centre returns the scrim, not the card. A second Escape finally closes the dialog.
standing.consequence: Orla walks a card into a new lane, presses Enter to read it, presses Escape to get out of the panel — and her move is silently undone while she is still looking at the panel that opened. There is no receipt, no undo strip, and Ctrl+Z at that moment reports "Nothing left to undo." The focus trap on an `aria-modal` dialog is also broken on this route: focus is placed outside the dialog while the dialog is still up.
standing.fix: In the `Enter` branch of the card keydown handler in `src/tasks.js` (the branch commented "Enter opens the task, the same surface a press opens"), end the carry before opening the panel: run the same commit Space runs — clear `carriedId` and `carriedFrom`, fire `completed()` if the destination lane is `done` — and prepend the drop sentence to the "Task open." announcement. Escape then has exactly one meaning while the panel is up.
standing.assertion: Space, ArrowRight, Enter, Escape on the first card of tasks.board leaves that card in In progress, closes the dialog, and returns focus to the card; the carried state is false immediately after the Enter; and `document.activeElement` is inside `.taskPanel` at every moment `.taskPanel` is in the DOM.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX AND ON ONE LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE — the Escape half of the problem is real, new, and must NOT be discarded.

DRIVEN, chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, first card `demo-t-01`. Every number reproduces: Space → "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company.", `aria-grabbed="true"`; ArrowRight → tray card counts 3,3,2,0,5 → 2,4,2,0,5 and "In progress, position 1 of 4."; Enter → `.taskPanel` renders, `document.activeElement` is the ASIDE, `carriedId` still set (`aria-grabbed="true"` on the card), live region reads only "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company. Task open."; Escape → counts revert to 3,3,2,0,5, "Move cancelled. … is back in the to do column.", `.taskPanel` still in the DOM, focus on `.card[data-id="demo-t-01"]` at (128, 196.8, 234x135.75), and `document.elementFromPoint` at its centre returns `div.tpScrim`. Second Escape → "Task closed." The seat's repro is exact.

WHAT IS FACTUALLY WRONG. "nothing spoken or drawn says the card is still in the air" is false on the drawn half, and that half is precisely what killed this finding's r1 ancestor (`enter-during-carry-does-not-drop`, refuted: "the HUD still names the drop key"). `footPill()` in `src/tasks.js` renders inside `.sheet` and is unconditional on the panel: with the modal open I measured `.carry` at (496, 826, 529.9x36), computed opacity 1, reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company · ↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel". `.tpScrim` is `rgba(17,17,17,0.32)` with no backdrop-filter, so the strip is dimmed and fully legible — I clipped a screenshot of it and read every word. The card also still carries `data-force="moving"`. So the surface does keep saying the card is in the air, in the one place it has always said it, and it keeps naming Space and Esc there. Only the spoken sentence omits it — the r1-adjudicated refinement.

That also caps the class. Not blocking and not misleading: the panel prints no Esc keycap at all (`taskPanel()` offers a `.tpClose` button and `data-act="task-close"` on the scrim, no shortcut text), and the only Escape the product advertises anywhere on this screen is the carry strip's "Esc cancel" — which is exactly what Escape does. Nothing the product says fails, and nothing untrue is asserted. It is a defect: focus genuinely leaves an `aria-modal="true"` dialog onto scrimmed content, and a board move silently reverts where the operator cannot see it. It is recoverable — Tab pulls focus back to `.tpClose` via the existing trap, and a second Escape closes the panel — which is why it is not more.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. It repeats, verbatim, the second half of the r1 refutation: making Enter commit adds a drop key that neither `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` (Enter deliberately absent) nor the carry strip ("Space drop · Esc cancel") names, and the fix names neither. It is worse than a naming gap. Enter's one documented meaning on a card is open-the-note; under this fix, asking to read a card irreversibly commits a move — and if the operator had walked it into Done, fires `completed()` and its receipt — as a side effect of reading. Today Escape restores the pre-carry position; after the fix that recovery path is gone. It also does not repair the real severity in the general case: any other way of opening the panel mid-carry, and the pointer route through `data-act="task-close"`, are untouched.
standing.sharpenedFix: Fix the Escape ladder, not Enter. In `onKey` in `src/tasks.js`, the branch already states its own rule — "Innermost first … an open panel is the innermost thing on the sheet" — and then sites `if (carriedId)` above `if (openTaskId)`, contradicting it. Move the `if (openTaskId)` block above the `if (carriedId)` block, so a live modal owns the first Escape. When it closes with a carry still live, restate the carry rather than dropping it silently: `say("Task closed. " + taskById(carriedId).title + " is still in hand, " + inLane(laneIds()[place(carriedId).x]) + ". Space drops it, Esc cancels.")`, and let `refocus` land on the carried card, not the previously-open one. The second Escape then cancels the move exactly as the strip advertises. Enter, the Space commit path, `completed()`, `aria-keyshortcuts` and the carry strip all stay untouched. Separately, and as a sentence change only with no state change, append the carry clause to the Enter announcement: `say(title + ". Task open. " + title + " is still in hand.")` — that is the one part of the seat's proposal worth keeping, in words instead of in state. Apply the same restatement to the pointer close (`data-act="task-close"` on `.tpScrim` and `.tpClose`) so both routes out of the panel resolve the carry identically.
standing.breaks: The reorder makes cancelling a carry cost two Escapes whenever a panel is open over it, which is correct but is a change to a gesture the strip advertises as one key — re-measure that the strip is still drawn and still reads "Esc cancel" at the moment the second press is expected. Re-measure after it lands: that `refocus` puts focus on the still-carried card and not the just-closed task when the two differ; that the card survives the repaint with `aria-grabbed="true"` and `data-force="moving"` intact (the panel close calls `mount()`, and `mount()` clears `carriedId` on some paths — line 3014 and line 461 both null it, so confirm neither fires here); that `document.elementFromPoint` at the focused card's centre now returns the card, not `div.tpScrim`; that the Tab trap has nothing left to catch, i.e. focus is never outside `.taskPanel` while `.taskPanel` exists; that the pointer route through the scrim and `.tpClose` produces the same sentence and the same focus as Escape; and that the carry strip does not flash the `undone` variant during the close repaint. Also re-check the Escape ladder below the moved block — `openNoteId`, the three filters, and the planning drawer must still fire in the same order — and re-run both gates (`audit.mjs` and `interaction-check.mjs`; I grepped the behaviour gate and it asserts nothing about the Escape ladder, so it will not catch a regression here — add an assertion for the ordering while you are in it).

standing.element: Notes controls routed through the `ELSEWHERE` table: `[data-act="more"]` ("More actions for this note"), `[data-act="options"]` ("Notes options"), `[data-act="privacy"]`, `[data-act="photo"]` ("Read a photo")
standing.problem: Measured at 1440 in notes.notebook, with and without a note lifted. Pressing each of the four changes nothing on screen: the app's `innerText` is byte-identical before and after, the node count is unchanged, `title` is `null`, `aria-disabled` is `null`, and no popover, strip or tooltip appears. The only answer is a live-region string. "Read a photo" sits beside "Dictate" with an identical computed treatment — background `rgba(0,0,0,0)`, colour `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)`, same border colour, opacity 1, `aria-disabled=null`, `title=null` — and Dictate works, taking the floor to ink. Tasks marks nine equivalent controls `aria-disabled="true"` with a title (List/Schedule/Calendar, Search, More, Settings, both avatars); Notes marks exactly one, the shared dock avatar. Separately, `more`'s sentence — "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen." — answers a different question than its label asks: the button says "More actions for this note".
standing.consequence: A sighted person presses a live-looking button in the product's own capture row and gets nothing whatsoever. The product reads as broken rather than honest — which is the exact opposite of what the honest-doors decision was for. A screen-reader user is told the control is available, presses it, and is told it lives somewhere else.
standing.fix: Route all four through the treatment Tasks already ships: set `aria-disabled="true"` and the sentence as `title`, and render the sentence in the receipt strip Notes already owns (`.carry`, the one the undo strip uses) so the press produces a visible on-screen answer that decays the same way. Change `more`'s string to name the note's own actions rather than the suite, e.g. "Duplicating, sharing and deleting a note are on another screen. This note is unchanged."
standing.assertion: In every Notes state, every control whose press routes to the `ELSEWHERE` table carries `aria-disabled="true"` and a non-empty `title`, and pressing it makes an element containing that same sentence visible with a non-zero painted box.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do NOT discard the observation, it reproduces exactly, but this remedy is inert on the very control the finding leads with, names an object Notes does not own, and damages a fifth of its own scope.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, `src/notes.js:3306` ELSEWHERE):
Every observable claim is exact. With a note lifted onto the desk, pressing each of the four leaves `[data-app="notes"]`.innerText byte-identical and the node count at 254→254; a full-page screenshot before/after pressing `photo` is `Buffer.compare === 0`. `title` is `null` and `aria-disabled` is `null` on all four. `.verb[data-act="photo"]` and `.verb[data-act="voice"]` compute identically — `cursor: pointer`, `color: rgba(17,17,17,0.62)`, `opacity: 1` — and so do their `.dockGlyph` twins; Dictate works, photo does not. `#say` is `class="sr"`, `1x1`, `clip-path: inset(50%)`. And `more`'s mismatch is verbatim: `aria-label="More actions for this note"` answered with "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen." — the same string `suite-more` uses at `src/notes.js:3110`. That last one alone is misleading.

WHY THE FIX FAILS.

(1) Half (a) is a NO-OP on the control the finding leads with. Notes' only disabled rule is `src/notes.css:1433` — `[data-app="notes"] [aria-disabled="true"] { cursor: default; }`. Tasks' equivalent (`src/tasks.css:1091`) adds `color: var(--ink-3)`. But `--ink-3` is `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)` (`src/notes.css:45`, `src/tasks.css:41`) — which is EXACTLY what `.verb` and `.dockGlyph` already compute. So even porting Tasks' full rule, `photo` next to `voice` would be pixel-identical at rest; the only change is the mouse cursor. Tasks' treatment reads because a disabled `.segItem` (0.62, transparent) sits beside a live one at full ink on a white pill — I measured `segLive` at `rgb(17,17,17)` / `rgb(255,255,255)`. Notes has no such contrast to borrow. The fix does not fix "identical computed treatment", which is the finding's own headline evidence.

(2) `.carry` is not Notes'. It is scoped `[data-app="tasks"] .carry` (`src/tasks.css:1498`, `tasks.js:1002/1018/1040/1055`); `grep carry src/notes.css` returns six prose comments and zero selectors. Notes' strip is `.undo` (`notes.js:1687`, `notes.css:833`) and it is not a receipt strip — `undoStrip()` unconditionally renders an Undo button with a `⌘Z` keycap and a live `for N seconds` countdown driven by `undoTick`. Putting "Reading a photo happens on another screen. Nothing here changes." in it offers to undo a thing that did not happen and starts a 30-second window that does not exist, and it collides with a genuinely pending undo, since `undone` is one slot.

(3) It marks a privacy guarantee as unavailable. `[data-act="privacy"]` (`notes.js:1613`) is not a door — it is the assurance chip, `aria-label="Private to you. Yours until you send something on."` Setting `aria-disabled="true"` on it announces the product's privacy promise as not here yet. That is worse than the defect.

(4) It would open a fourth grammar. I force-pressed the rail's own closed doors on this build: `settings` and Notes' `.dockAvatar` both leave the screenshot byte-identical and answer only in `#say`. The suite's single answer everywhere is aria-disabled + `cursor: default` + `title` + live region. A visible press-receipt in Notes alone re-opens r1's `three-unavailability-grammars`.

TWO EVIDENCE ERRORS. "Tasks marks nine equivalent controls" is inflated. Scoped to `[data-app="tasks"]` at 1440 on tasks.board there are FIVE visible: More, List, Schedule, Calendar, dockAvatar. `.ghost.headSearch` has no box at that width. `Settings` and `.railAvatar` are the SUITE RAIL's — Notes carries both identically; I dumped the document-wide list on notes.notebook and got the same nine, because no product is ever torn down. The real asymmetry is 5 vs 1, not 9 vs 1.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Split the four; they are not one class.

1. `more` — fix the string, which is the misleading half and costs nothing. Give `ELSEWHERE` its own entry instead of borrowing `suite-more`'s: "Duplicating, sharing and deleting a note are on another screen. This note is unchanged." The seat's wording is right; only its delivery was wrong.

2. `photo` and `options` — these are genuinely unavailable. Mark them `aria-disabled="true"` with the sentence as `title` (matching `src/app.js:126` / `src/tasks.js:531`), and add the ONE rule Notes is missing so the mark is visible: `[data-app="notes"] .verb[aria-disabled="true"], [data-app="notes"] .dockGlyph[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--ink-4) }` — ink-4 is `rgba(17,17,17,0.30)` and is decorative-only by Notes' own comment at `notes.css:50`, so use `opacity` on the glyph or a dedicated 0.44 step instead if the audit's AA check touches these; that is what must be re-measured. Without a density step the attribute changes nothing but the cursor.

3. `privacy` — leave it live. It is an assurance, not a door. Fix its string only: `fixture.js:617` sets `privacyLong: "Yours until you send something on"` with no terminal stop, so the announcement currently reads "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — a run-on. Add the stop at the template, not at the fixture, since the aria-label at `notes.js:1613` already appends its own.

4. If a visible press-receipt is wanted, do it ONCE at suite level, not in Notes. `say()` in `src/app.js` is the single carrier; give it an optional visible twin beside the spine so the rail's `settings`/`me`, Tasks' segItems and Notes' doors all answer the same way. Anything less than that adds a grammar rather than removing one.
standing.breaks:
If shipped as written: adding `aria-disabled="true"` to `photo`/`more`/`options` in Notes produces no visual change (only `cursor: default`), so the panel would read the finding as closed while the defect it names — photo indistinguishable from Dictate — is untouched. Notes' click handler (`notes.js:3090`) has no `[aria-disabled="true"]` guard the way Tasks does (`tasks.js:2415`), so the ELSEWHERE announcement still fires; no functional break there, but the two products would then disagree on whether a disabled control's press is intercepted or handled.

Routing the sentence into the undo strip is the real hazard: `undone` is a single slot and `undoStrip()` always paints Undo + a ticking countdown, so pressing `photo` while a save or a seam-send undo is pending either destroys the pending undo or paints a second strip; `undoTimer`'s expiry path (`notes.js:288`) also moves focus out of the strip if focus is inside it, which would now fire after a press that changed nothing.

Marking `privacy` disabled changes the accessible name of the product's privacy assurance to a dimmed, unavailable control.

RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS: (a) `audit.mjs` AA contrast for any new ink step on `.verb`/`.dockGlyph` against the composited white sheet — 0.30 is well under AA for type and Notes' own comment forbids it as type colour; (b) hit targets on `.dockGlyph` if `cursor`/pointer-events change; (c) `interaction-check.mjs`, specifically the undo assertions, if `.undo` is touched at all; (d) the tab order and focus ring on the four controls, since `aria-disabled` must NOT remove them from the tab order — the whole doctrine at `tasks.js:529` is that a control nobody can reach never gets to say why it is missing; (e) a before/after screenshot diff of `photo` beside `voice` at 1440 and 390 to prove the mark is actually visible, which is the only test that would have caught this fix being inert.

standing.element: `.morePop` (`role="menu"`) and the rail rover — driven at 1440x960
standing.problem: Three separate contract failures on one object. (a) The container is `role="menu"` but its three children are plain `<button aria-disabled="true">` with `role=null` — a menu that reports no menu items. (b) With the menu open and `aria-expanded="true"` on the More tile, ArrowDown/ArrowUp keep walking the rail rover — More → Settings → Avatar — instead of entering the menu; the arrows never reach it. (c) It has no light dismissal: I clicked a card with the menu open and it stayed open; I tabbed through all 20 focus stops of the whole application and it was still open at the end. Only Escape or a second press of More closes it. Tasks' own `.cardMenu` and the Filter/Sort/Display popovers both dismiss correctly on an outside press, via the `toolOpen` branch at the head of `onClick`.
standing.consequence: After one press the menu is stranded open for the rest of the session — three extra focus stops that a keyboard user hits on every pass through the app, invisible to the eye (finding 1), and announced by a screen reader as a menu containing nothing. The contract keys the role advertises do not work.
standing.fix: Give the `.moreItem` buttons `role="menuitem"`; make the rail's arrow rover yield while `[data-rail="plus"]` has `aria-expanded="true"` and route ArrowUp/ArrowDown into `.morePop` instead, wrapping at its ends; and add `.morePop` to the same outside-press dismissal branch the `toolOpen` popovers already use in `onClick`, restoring focus to the More tile when it closes.
standing.assertion: With the More menu open: ArrowDown moves focus to the first `.moreItem`; a press on any element outside `.morePop` and outside the More tile removes `.morePop` from the DOM and returns focus to the More tile; and every element child of `[role="menu"]` has `role="menuitem"`.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON PART (c) AND ON THE WHOLE FIX. Parts (a) and (b) are real and reproduce exactly — do NOT discard them — but (c) is the part carrying the severity and the framing ("three separate contract failures", "no light dismissal"), and it is factually wrong about the code, as is every load-bearing premise the proposed fix rests on.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven at file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board, 1440x960.
(a) Exact. `.morePop` is `role="menu"` (line 9300) and its three children are `class="moreItem" aria-disabled="true"` with `role` = null (line 9277). I read it back at runtime: `[{role:null,dis:"true",ti:0}, x3]`. And the suite has its own counter-example 1,500 lines away: `.cardMenu` (line 10802) emits `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` on every child and a roving tabindex, and moves focus into the menu on open (line 12452). The rail menu does none of it. That inconsistency is genuine.
(b) Exact. With `aria-expanded="true"` on the More tile, ArrowDown walked plus → settings → me. The rover at line 9666 filters `.rail [data-rail]` by `offsetParent` and never tests `moreOpen`; nothing routes arrows into the panel, and focus is left on the plus tile after open (line 9605).

WHAT DOES NOT. (c) is false as a general claim. The suite ALREADY has the outside-press branch the finding says is missing, and it is sited exactly where the finding asks for one — at the head of `deck`'s click listener, lines 9581-9586: `var insideMore = ...closest(".morePop") || ...closest('[data-rail="plus"]'); if (moreOpen && !insideMore) { moreOpen = false; paintRail(); }`. Driven, it fires and closes the menu on: the ink floor (1430,950), the sheet head (900,40), a `.tick`, any of the four `[data-act="tool"]` buttons, a Notes `.idxRow`, and a Timeline `.b-grab`. One gesture out of seven fails — the Tasks card body, which is the one the seat used — and it fails for a reason the finding never names. The card opens on **pointerup** (line 13271), which calls `mount()` and re-renders the board before the click is dispatched; the click target is detached, so no click event reaches `deck` at all. I instrumented both `deck` and `document` in the bubble phase and the log after a card press was empty: `[]`. This is a propagation hole in one control, not a missing dismissal model.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG — three ways, and the first two are checkable facts.
1. "Tasks' own `.cardMenu` ... dismiss[es] correctly ... via the `toolOpen` branch at the head of `onClick`" is false. `.cardMenu` does not touch `toolOpen`. It ships a dedicated full-screen overlay, `<div class="menuVeil" data-act="closemenu">` (line 10801, CSS line 1780, handled at 12514), which is why Playwright reported "menuVeil intercepts pointer events" when I tried to click past it.
2. "the Filter/Sort/Display popovers ... dismiss correctly on an outside press" is false on the seat's own repro. I opened Filter and clicked a card: `{tool:true}` — still open. The `toolOpen` branch at line 12139 has the identical hole for the identical reason. So the proposed remedy is "copy the branch that fails on exactly the gesture you used to prove the bug." It would not close `.morePop` on a card press.
3. Wrong layer. `onClick` is bound to Tasks' `host` (line 13314). The rail is the shell's, rendered once by `railHtml`/`paintRail` for all three products. Wiring rail dismissal into Tasks' handler duplicates a shell branch that already exists and silently drops it in Notes and Timeline — where it currently works.

SEVERITY. The seat's class rested on (c). What survives is a defect, not blocking or misleading: every door in the panel is reachable by Tab (I walked it: plus → All projects → Inbox → Help → the sheet), named, and speaks its "Not here yet" sentence; Escape closes and restores focus (line 9648); six of seven outside presses close it. Nothing the product says to a person is untrue. It sits at the defect/misleading line only because `role="menu"` with zero menuitems is a false assertion to AT — I do not class it misleading because that is the half of the finding the seat argued least. Nothing here is asserted by `interaction-check.mjs`; I checked — it has no `morePop`/`moreOpen` assertion.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Fix the two real halves, in the shell, and fix the propagation hole once for all four surfaces instead of copying a broken branch.

1. ARIA and keyboard, together — they are one change, not two. At line 9277 add `role="menuitem"` and `tabindex="-1"` to each `.moreItem`; keep `aria-disabled="true"` and the title. In the `plus` branch at line 9604, focus the first `.moreItem` instead of the plus tile on open (mirroring `.cardMenu` at line 12452), and keep focusing the plus tile on close. In the keydown handler at line 9666, before the `var tile = ...` test, add a branch: if `moreOpen` and `event.target.closest(".morePop")`, ArrowDown/ArrowUp (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft at <=720, matching the `horizontal` predicate already computed at line 9679) move the roving stop within `[].slice.call(deck.querySelectorAll(".moreItem"))` with wrap, Home/End go to the ends, and `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` as the rover already does. The rail rover then needs no "yield" clause — focus is inside `.morePop`, not on a `[data-rail]`, so it never matches. Once items are roving `tabindex="-1"`, add focusout dismissal: on `deck` focusout, if `moreOpen` and neither `event.target` nor `relatedTarget` is inside `.morePop` or on the plus tile, close and repaint — that is what makes the seat's "still open after 20 tab stops" observation correct behaviour rather than a bug, and it is only correct once the panel is a single tab stop.
2. Light dismissal — move the existing branch, do not duplicate it. Change lines 9581-9586 from a `click` listener to a `pointerdown` listener on `deck` (keep the `insideMore` test verbatim; add `.railAdd`? no — leave the predicate alone). I verified this works: with More open, a card press produced `["deck-pd:cardNote"]` on `deck`, i.e. pointerdown reaches the shell before `mount()` at line 13271 detaches the target. That is the only gesture currently failing, and this closes it without touching Tasks.
3. Optional, separately scoped: the same pointerdown move fixes `toolOpen` at line 12139, which I measured failing on the same gesture. File it as its own finding — do not bundle it here.

RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS. (i) `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs` both green — the focus audit at interaction-check.mjs:80 counts focus stops, and roving `tabindex="-1"` removes three; confirm it still passes (it should: the invisible-focusable test only trips on focusable AND invisible, and these are visible). (ii) The honest-doors constraint says All projects, Inbox and Help are "in the tab order". Under a roving menu they are reachable through the More tile, which is itself a tab stop, but they are no longer three independent Tab stops — get the founder's read on that before shipping, because it is the one place this fix touches a non-negotiable. (iii) At <=720 the panel carries a fourth item (Settings joins it, line 9573) and the arrows lie down; re-drive at 390. (iv) Moving dismissal to pointerdown means a press that BEGINS on the floor and ends on the plus tile now closes then reopens — check the plus tile's own toggle at line 9600 does not double-fire, and re-drive "press plus, press plus again" and "press plus, drag a card". (v) Escape from inside the panel (line 9648) and `paintRail`'s focus restore (line 9614) both still land on the plus tile.
standing.breaks: The roving-tabindex change removes three independent Tab stops (All projects, Inbox, Help), which brushes the "honest doors are in the tab order" constraint — that is the one thing here needing a founder decision rather than an engineering call, and it is why this fix cannot be shipped blind. Moving the shell's dismissal from `click` to `pointerdown` changes when the panel closes relative to a drag: a press that begins on the floor now closes the panel before any drag starts, which is correct but changes the plus tile's toggle timing, so "press plus twice" and "press plus then drag a card" both need re-driving. Focusing the first `.moreItem` on open changes what a screen reader announces at open — re-listen to the `say("More, open.")` line at 9607, which currently speaks while focus is still on the tile. Re-measure: both gates green; the focus-stop count in interaction-check.mjs:80; the panel at 390x844 where it carries a fourth item and horizontal arrows; Escape and `paintRail` focus restore; and the `.morePop` dismissal on all seven gestures I drove (floor, sheet head, tick, tool button, card body, Notes `.idxRow`, Timeline `.b-grab`).

standing.element: `.viewTools .ghost` ("Filter") and its `.toolDot` badge, with any filter active
standing.problem: Pressing "1 overdue" raises a count badge on the Filter button. Measured at 1280: the badge box is x 1058–1072, y 184–198; the label span is x 1034–1063, y 189–206. They intersect by 5px horizontally and 9px vertically, so the badge sits on the final "r" and the control reads "Filte¹". Identical 5x9 overlap at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, and in both variants — the button is a fixed 73px wide, so the badge has nowhere to go. The badge also carries `aria-hidden="true"` and the button has no `aria-label`, so the count exists only in paint.
standing.consequence: The one control that explains why the board just went from thirteen cards to one renders with its last letter obscured, in a screenshot-quality surface. A screen-reader user hears "Filter" whether one filter is applied or none, and has nothing in the accessible name to tell them the board is being filtered.
standing.fix: Inset `.toolDot` into the button's padding box so its left edge begins at least 4px after the label span's right edge, letting the button grow rather than overlap — the same relationship the head's `1 today` / `1 overdue` chips already hold between number and word. Set the button's `aria-label` from the same accessor that renders the dot: "Filter, 1 applied" when the count is non-zero, "Filter" otherwise.
standing.assertion: At 768/1280/1440/1920 in both variants, with a filter active, the `.toolDot` and label-span bounding boxes do not intersect, and the Filter button's accessible name contains the active-filter count.
standing.verdict: REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — the occlusion is real, reproduces to the tenth of a pixel, and must NOT be discarded. But the remedy as written cannot produce the effect it claims, one of its structural facts is false, and the accessibility half rests on a claim that driving disproves. WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, pressing the "1 overdue" chip) The geometry is exact. At 1280: badge x 1058.4–1072.4, y 183.8–197.8; label span x 1034.0–1063.4, y 189.3–206.3. Overlap 5.0px horizontal, 8.5px vertical. Identical at 768, 1440, 1920, and byte-identical in `v=ink`. It is worse than the seat says: I took per-character Range rects and the final "r" advance box is 1058.6–1063.4 — the badge's left edge lands 0.2px BEFORE the "r" begins and covers its entire advance. At deviceScaleFactor 10 the r's shoulder and terminal are gone and only a bare stem survives, so the control reads "Filte|". On the flagship view's primary control, that is a real defect. WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED 1. Mechanically inert as written. `em.toolDot` is `position: absolute; top: 3px; right: 2px` inside `.viewTools .ghost { position: relative }` (line 3117 / `src/tasks.css:2420`). Repositioning an out-of-flow child never grows its containing block, so "letting the button grow" cannot follow from insetting the dot. Executed literally — move the dot's left edge 4px past the span's right edge without touching the button — you set `right: -7px`, the badge hangs 7px outside the button into a 2px flex gap (measured: Filter ends 1074.4, Sort begins 1076.4) and lands on Sort's left edge. The growth has to come from padding on the BUTTON, which the fix never says. 2. "The button is a fixed 73px wide" is false about the code. `.ghost` is `display: inline-flex; height: 34px; padding: 0 11px` with no `width` and no `min-width` anywhere in the cascade. 73.5px is shrink-to-fit, not declared. The badge's "nowhere to go" comes from 14px of badge sitting inside 11px of padding at `right: 2px`, eating 5px of content box — a different mechanism, and the one the fix has to address. 3. Its number is 9px too generous and it spends them on a toggle. The overlap is exactly 5.0px; "at least 4px after the span's right edge" demands 9px of clearance minimum, and since the badge's right edge is pinned 2px inside the button, all of it comes out of button width — +18px if the 11px right padding is kept. Growing only when the count appears means the row moves under the operator's hand at the instant they press the chip. Measured at 768 with `padding-right: 29px` injected: the tools row's right edge goes 728.0 → 740.6 and its headroom against the measured fold threshold (`tools.right > sheet.right - 8`, line ~12858) falls 20.0px → 7.4px — 63% of the slack at the tightest width where the words are still drawn, spent on a state change. A constant reserve costs none of it. 4. The accessibility justification is factually wrong. "The count exists only in paint" — driven at 1280, pressing the chip writes into `.sr[aria-live="polite"]`: "Showing 1 overdue task. 12 others are hidden.", and the Filter pop's footer reads "Clear 1 filter". The count reaches a screen reader twice already. The residual gap is narrower than claimed — a user who tabs to Filter later hears "Filter, menu, collapsed" with no state — and `aria-label` is the wrong instrument: it REPLACES the name computed from the visible `Filter`, creating a second string that must be kept in sync and a WCAG 2.5.3 exposure the moment the wording drifts. The product already ships `b-vh` for exactly this. SEVERITY: defect, and I would cap it there. The filter works, the count is legible as "1", and nothing false is asserted — a decapitated glyph is visibly wrong but passable.
standing.sharpenedFix: Reserve the badge's lane in the button's own padding, permanently and only on the Filter tool, so the corner-badge idiom survives and nothing moves when the filter toggles: `[data-app="tasks"] .viewTools .ghost[data-tool="filter"] { padding-right: 19px; }` Arithmetic against the real source: the badge's left edge sits at `buttonRight − 2 − 14 = buttonRight − 16`; the content box ends at `buttonRight − paddingRight`. Overlap is zero when `paddingRight ≥ 16`; 19px leaves 3px of air between the "r" and the pill. Button goes 73.5 → 81.5px, constant in both states, so pressing a chip changes no geometry at all — the +8px is spent once, at rest, on the leftmost of three tools where it reads as ordinary trailing space. Leave `em.toolDot`'s `top: 3px; right: 2px` alone: it stays a corner badge, the same object as the 6px `:empty` dot on Sort and Display, so the three tools keep one treatment. No rule for the `:empty` case is needed — `filterCount()` is falsy at zero and the `em` is not rendered at all, so `[data-tool="filter"]` never draws the 6px variant. For the accessible name, append rather than override, from the same accessor that renders the dot: emit `', ' + live + ' filter' + (live === 1 ? "" : "s") + ' applied'` inside the button alongside the existing `Filter` (tasks.js:834 / line 10555). The name computes to "Filter, 1 filter applied", the visible word is contained in it (WCAG 2.5.3 holds), and it cannot drift from the label because one accessor feeds both. `.views[data-fold] .viewTools .ghost > span` already clips direct-child spans, so the fold state is unaffected. Do not set `aria-label`.
standing.breaks:
What the sharpened fix plausibly touches, and what to re-measure after it lands:

1. The measured fold. `.viewTools` widens 233 → 241px and the head-fit pass folds on `tools.getBoundingClientRect().right > sheet.right − 8`. Re-measure that headroom at 768, 820, 900, 1024 and 1280, both with the Planning drawer shut and open. Current readings for the baseline: slack is a flat 20.0px at 820–1920 (the row is right-pinned by `margin-left: auto`, so its right edge does not move) and 20.0px at 768 where the seg pushes it; +8px leaves 17.4px at 768 and 20.0px elsewhere, and 1024-with-drawer is already `data-fold="gone"` before and after. No fold state changes in my simulation, but it is the one threshold this touches and it must be read again, not assumed.
2. The glyph itself. Re-crop the Filter button at deviceScaleFactor 10 in both `v=paper` and `v=ink` with "1 overdue" pressed, and confirm the "r" advance box (1058.6–1063.4 at 1280) no longer intersects the badge. Also check a two-digit count — apply "1 overdue" plus a tag filter so `filterCount()` reaches 2, then force a 10+ case if the fixture allows: at two digits the pill grows leftward from `min-width: 14px` on `padding: 0 3px`, so 19px of reserve buys ~3px of air at one digit and goes negative past two. If double digits are reachable in this fixture, raise the reserve to 25px or cap the printed count.
3. The accessible name. Re-run the name computation on the Filter button in all four states (no filter / 1 filter / filter open / `data-fold="words"`) and confirm it reads "Filter" at rest and "Filter, 1 filter applied" when live, with the visible word still contained in it. Confirm the `.sr` announcement is not duplicated into a double-speak on press.
4. Both gates. `audit.mjs` for hit target (34px height is untouched) and for the white-on-indigo badge contrast, which this does not move; `interaction-check.mjs` for the tools row's single tab stop and roving `tabindex`, which the extra span must not disturb.

standing.element: Rail tile "More" (`data-rail="plus"`) and `.railAdd` ("Add task") — desk and phone
standing.problem: Both draw the identical SVG path `M12 5.5v13M5.5 12h13`. At ≤720 both are rendered at 44x44 and land adjacent in the phone dock, so the shipped 390 frame shows two plus signs side by side, distinguishable only by fill — and fill is what this system uses for "primary", so the *thin* one reads as the secondary add. At the desk `.railAdd` is `display:none`, which leaves the rail's only plus sign being the tile that means "More": the door to All projects, Inbox, Help and Settings. It is also the only rail tile with no word beneath it while Notes, Tasks and Timeline all carry one.
standing.consequence: The universally understood create glyph is wired to a menu of doors that are not here yet. Orla taps the plus in the dock expecting to add a task and gets the wrong object — and, per finding 1, an object she cannot read.
standing.fix: Give the More tile the three-dot "…" mark Tasks already uses for its own More control in the sheet head, and reserve the plus exclusively for `.railAdd`. That also makes the desk rail's util group read as two doors rather than one add and one gear.
standing.assertion: No two simultaneously visible controls in the rail or the phone dock render the same SVG path data, at 390 and at 1440.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces exactly, and must NOT be discarded. The fix would put the artifact's most over-used mark on its most important door, and it is the wrong mark for the job.

WHAT REPRODUCES (Chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper`, measured live):
- Both controls draw the identical path. `src/icons.js:29` defines `plus: 'M12 5.5v13M5.5 12h13'`. `src/app.js:172` renders the More tile as `util("plus","More",…)` and `util` emits `I[key]` — so the tile keyed "plus" gets the plus glyph. `app.js:179` renders `.railAdd` with `I.plus`. Verified in the DOM: both `<svg>` innerHTML are byte-identical.
- 390x844, `state=tasks.board`: `[data-rail="plus"]` at x=243 w=44 h=44; `.railAdd` at x=295 w=44 h=44. **8px apart, both 44x44, same path.** Glyphs 19px vs 20px. The only real separator is fill: ghost `rgba(255,255,255,.62)` on transparent vs `#111` on `#fff`, radius 12 vs 14. I cropped the shipped dock and looked at it — it reads as two add buttons, one of them greyed out.
- Desk (1440 and 768): `.railAdd` is `display:none` (shell.css:250), so the rail's **only** plus is the More tile — a control that creates nothing.
- Worse than the seat states, and it is what pushes this to *misleading*: the More tile is the **only visible rail control with no `title`**. Driven at 1440 across all five states, `allRailTitles` = notes:"Notes", tasks:"Tasks", timeline:"Timeline", **plus:NONE**, settings:"Your workspace, your way. Not here yet.", me:"Your account…". `util("plus", …)` is passed `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` and no title (app.js:172-173). So a sighted mouse user gets a bare plus and no hover text anywhere on the desk. The product draws "create" and does "navigate".

TWO FACTUAL ERRORS IN THE FINDING (neither load-bearing, both worth correcting):
1. "the only rail tile with no word beneath it" is **false**. `util("settings",…)` (app.js:174) is also a `.railTile` with no `.railName`, and at desk it sits directly under the More tile — I measured both at 1440: plus y=800, settings y=848, `railName` absent on both. Two of five tiles are wordless, under a rule the source states explicitly ("a utility is not a destination and giving it one would flatten the hierarchy", app.js:141-142). The orphan-label half of the argument is void; the glyph half survives on its own.
2. "desk and phone" overstates the adjacency. At ≤720 the two pluses only ever co-exist on **Tasks**: Notes sets `.rail { display:none }` and Timeline sets `.railAdd { display:none }` (shell.css:410, 417). I confirmed all three at 390. The shipped 390 frame is tasks.board, so the seat's evidence holds — the scope claim does not.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — the dots mark is the most collided glyph in the document:
I counted `I.dots` instances painted per frame at 1440. tasks.board: **15**. tasks.dense: **34**. Their owners: "Notes options" (live), "**More**" (aria-disabled="true" — the Tasks sheet-head control the seat wants to copy, whose sentence is "Project settings come with your account"), and 13–32 × "Move this task" on card feet. Handing the rail's More the same mark would:
- Put **two controls named "More" on one screen, in one frame, drawing the identical glyph, meaning two unrelated things** — one a live door to All projects/Inbox/Help, one a dead door to project settings. That is a strictly worse collision than the one being fixed, because it is simultaneous at every desk width, whereas the plus/plus collision exists only on Tasks at ≤720.
- Make the app's live navigation menu look like the closed doors. The finding's own stated goal is "two doors rather than one add and one gear"; copying a mark that is `aria-disabled` two feet away achieves the opposite.
- Say the wrong word. "…" is an overflow of actions on the object in front of you. The rail's More opens *places* — All projects, Inbox, Help, and on a phone Settings. Linear, Stripe and Vercel all keep those grammars apart; none opens a nav menu from an ellipsis.

WHAT IT PLAUSIBLY BREAKS
