standing.element: Notes pick band vs. the live region, after selecting words in `.readBody`
standing.problem: Driven: a real pointer drag across the note body paints the band "5 words picked. Send to Tasks will use exactly these." while the live region announces "5 words picked. Use these words to make them a task." The spoken half is not a grammatical sentence — "these words" has no way to become "them a task" — and it names no control, so the listener is told to use the words without being told what to press. The string is built at three sites in `src/notes.js` as `${wordsPicked(text)} ${N.copy.begin} to make them a task.`; the code comment two thousand lines away quotes this exact sentence as a defect that was fixed by making Enter work, but the sentence itself was left standing.
standing.consequence: At the single most important moment in the suite — the seam — the screen-reader user gets a different and broken sentence for the same fact than the one on screen, and no route forward.
standing.fix: Announce the band's own rendered string, from the same accessor: `${wordsPicked(text)} Send to Tasks will use exactly these.` Where the pick has a standing target — the condition `startPeel` already tests — append "Press Enter to peel them." so the spoken channel names the key the code now implements.
standing.assertion: After a pick in `.readBody`, the live-region string is exactly the rendered text content of the pick band, plus at most the Enter clause when a standing pick target exists.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX AND ON THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — but the divergence itself is real, so do not throw the observation away.

DRIVEN, chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, index row 1 opened, real pointer drag across `.readBody`. Live DOM after the drag:
- `.pickBar` — role="status" — "6 words picked. Send to Tasks will use exactly these."
- `.sr` — role="status" aria-live="polite" — "6 words picked. Use these words to make them a task."
- `[data-act="peel"]` — "Send to Tasks"; activeElement `.readBody`.
So the two strings diverge exactly as described, the three build sites are `src/notes.js:880, 902, 1035`, `N.copy.begin` is `"Use these words"` at `src/fixture.js:625`, and the comment at `src/notes.js:3700` does quote this sentence verbatim as the defect Enter was made to answer. That much is exact.

Why it is refuted:

1. THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS FALSE. "Use these words to make them a task" is not ungrammatical. `make X a Y` is a standard construction ("make it a rule"); "them" corefers with "these words" and the purpose clause parses cleanly. It is redundant and limp, not broken. The finding's severity rests on "not a grammatical sentence", and that is a taste judgement stated as a syntax fact.

2. "IT NAMES NO CONTROL" IS WRONG ABOUT THE SAME FRAME. `.pickBar` is itself `role="status"` (`src/notes.js:1921, 2156, 2291`) and is inserted in the same repaint carrying "Send to Tasks will use exactly these." — the exact control name. The file's own model says such a node speaks: the comment at `src/notes.js:~248` reasons about "both nodes are role=status and a screen reader heard two near-identical sentences for one press". By the artifact's own premise the listener already hears the control named.

3. FIX HALF ONE MAKES IT WORSE. Putting the band's rendered string into `.sr` gives two `role="status"` nodes byte-identical text on one press — the literal double-speak that comment says it removed. It also misdescribes the code: there is no "same accessor". `wordsPicked()` is shared; the tail "Send to Tasks will use exactly these." is an inline literal duplicated at three template sites. And the band has a second branch (`pickRestored` → "Picked before, and still here. Press space to let it go.") that the fix does not account for.

4. FIX HALF TWO SHIPS A WORD THE PRODUCT DOES NOT USE. "peel" appears nowhere in user-facing copy — grep of `src/fixture.js` returns no string containing it; the visible words are "Send to Tasks" and "Turn this into a task". "Press Enter to peel them." would speak internal jargon to screen-reader users only, which is the inverse of the standard the seat is invoking. It also names a key unconditionally: the band branches on `phone.matches` for precisely this reason, and `NUDGE_PICK`'s comment records the paid-for lesson that keyboard-only instructions were "false on a phone". Measured at 390x844: the drag pick updates `.pickBar` (3 → 4 words) and never touches `.sr` at all, so the phone route is silent in the live region — the fix's Enter sentence would either never fire there or fire wrongly.

5. SEVERITY. Nothing untrue is asserted and nothing fails to work — Enter does peel from `.readBody`/`.handBody` (`src/notes.js:3692`), and the correct sentence is on screen and in a status node. This is a copy refinement, not blocking, misleading, or a defect.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Fix the drift, not the grammar, and do not duplicate a live region.

1. Hoist the band's tail into one constant beside the other Notes copy — `const PICK_STANDS = "Send to Tasks will use exactly these.";` — and read it at all three band sites (`src/notes.js:1921, 2156, 2291`) AND at the three say() sites (880, 902, 1035), so the seen and spoken halves cannot drift again. Retire the `to make them a task` tail; `N.copy.begin` (`src/fixture.js:625`) has no other consumer, so delete the key rather than leave a dangling string.

2. Do not put identical text in two `role="status"` nodes. Pick one owner: either drop the pick sentence from `.sr` while `.pickBar` is rendered (desk and hand rooms both render it), or keep `.sr` as the only spoken channel and make `.pickBar` visible-only. If you take the second route you must first give the phone pick route a say() — measured at 390, `.sr` is never written by that route, so removing role="status" from `.pickBar` makes the phone pick completely silent.

3. If the Enter route is worth speaking, speak it in the product's own words and only where it exists: gate on the same `!phone.matches` test `.pickBar` already uses and append "Press Enter to send it." — never "peel". Better still, draw the keycap on the `[data-act="peel"]` primary the way `save-edit` already carries `<kbd>Enter</kbd>`, so the sighted reader learns the same fact and the two channels agree by construction rather than by string.
standing.breaks: Hoisting the tail into one constant touches three render templates and three announcement sites; the `pickRestored` branch of the band must keep its own phone/desk split or the restored-pick sentence regresses. Suppressing one of the two `role="status"` nodes changes what is heard on every pick route, so re-drive all of them: pointer drag, tap-a-sentence, arrow-walk, and re-pick with the peel open (the `wordingEdited` branch at 874/896/1029 must still announce the edited wording). Re-measure at 390x844 specifically — the phone pick currently updates only `.pickBar`, so any change that makes the band non-live must add a say() there first. Neither gate reads these strings (no match for "words picked", "exactly these" or "pickBar" in `interaction-check.mjs`, `gate.mjs` or `verify.mjs`), so both stay green either way, and any assertion written for this should be added to the behaviour gate rather than assumed. Drawing a `<kbd>Enter</kbd>` on the desk primary is a visual change: re-run `audit.mjs` for hit target and type-ramp on that button, and re-check the 768 and 390 widths where the primary's label already switches between "Send to Tasks" and "Pick the words, then send".

standing.element: notes.voice — `.darkFoot`, and the two `.darkAct` buttons inside it
standing.problem: The dictation takeover's action pair breaks apart, and it does so non-monotonically. Driven in Chromium at ?v=paper&state=notes.voice, height 900 except where noted, measuring the two `.darkAct` boxes: PAIRED at 1920/1280/1024/1000, SPLIT at 900/860/840/820/800/768/700, PAIRED at 600, SPLIT at 500, PAIRED at 430, SPLIT at 390. Two of the split widths are declared, shot viewports. At 768x1024: Cancel sits at x=605..736, y=882 — right-aligned on row one beside the privacy paragraph — while the primary 'Stop and read it back' drops to x=32..322, y=946, the opposite corner. At 390x844: Cancel x=272..358, y=702; primary x=32..247, y=766. `.darkFoot` is `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:20px; align-items:flex-end` (src/notes.css:910) with four children — `.darkNote`, `.spacer{flex:1}`, Cancel, primary. The spacer expands to fill row one, so only the last button ever wraps, and the footer grows 112 → 176 → 259px as it does. Every other action row in the suite holds together at every width I drove: Timeline's `.b-bar` (Add a moment / Preview / Get the link) stays one row from 390 to 1920, and the seam's peel footer (To / Never mind / Send to Tasks) stays one row wherever the desk exists.
standing.consequence: On a phone and a tablet — the two widths where dictating is the main way a note gets made — the takeover's bottom band reads as a mistake rather than a composition. The two actions stop being a pair: the dismissive one is above and to the right, the primary is below and to the left, so the eye lands on Cancel first and has to travel diagonally across an otherwise empty ink field to find the white pill that ends the recording. It also reverses the left-to-right order the suite uses everywhere else, at the one moment the person is mid-sentence and looking for the fastest way out.
standing.fix: Group the two buttons so they cannot separate, and delete the spacer. Wrap them in one element where the footer is built in `notes.js`, and add: `[data-app="notes"] .darkActs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-end; align-items: flex-end; gap: 20px; flex: none; margin-left: auto; }`, then remove `[data-app="notes"] .darkFoot .spacer` (src/notes.css:924) and its node. I applied exactly this live and re-drove 360/390/430/500/600/768/900/1024/1280/1920: the pair holds one row at every width, its right edge lands on the takeover's own 32px margin, `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` stays 0, and `.darkFoot` at 390 falls from 259px to 195px — 64px of a phone screen returned to the transcript. Do NOT instead try `flex: 1 0 100%` on `.darkNote` to push it onto its own row: `max-width: var(--measure)` clamps the hypothetical main size so the flex line never breaks — I tested it and 768 and 900 were unchanged.
standing.assertion: In notes.voice at 390x844 (touch), 768x1024 and 900x900: the two `.darkAct` elements report the same `getBoundingClientRect().top` to within 1px; the one carrying `[data-primary]` has a greater `left` than the other; and the greater of the two `right` values is within 1px of `innerWidth - 32`.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation, and do not ship this remedy. Driven in chromium at file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.voice, height 900 except 768x1024 and 390x844.

THE PROBLEM REPRODUCES. Measuring the two `.darkAct` boxes: PAIRED at 1920/1440/1280/1024/1000, SPLIT at 900/860/840/820/800/768/700, PAIRED at 600, SPLIT at 500/430/390/360. At 768x1024, Cancel x=605..736 y=882 and the primary x=32..322 y=946 — opposite corners, exactly as stated. The mechanism is right: `.darkFoot` (src/notes.css:910) wraps, `.spacer{flex:1}` (src/notes.css:924) eats row one, so only the last child ever wraps, and the footer grows 112 → 176 → 240 → 259px. Two of the seat's numbers are wrong and neither is load-bearing: 430x900 is SPLIT, not PAIRED (Cancel y=758, primary y=822), and Cancel at 390 is x=227..358, not x=272..358 (the button is 131px wide, as the seat's own 768 figure shows). Severity is defect, not more: both buttons stay on screen, both keep their 44px target, both keep their advertised Esc/Enter keycaps. Nothing is asserted untrue.

THE FIX IS FALSE ON ITS OWN CENTRAL CLAIM AND MAKES THE WORK WORSE. I applied exactly the proposed markup and CSS live, re-injecting after every resize (the ≤720 breakpoint re-renders the state and would otherwise discard the patch — which is very likely how the seat came to measure zero overflow). `flex: none` sets flex-shrink to 0, so `.darkActs` is pinned at its max-content 441px (131 + 20 + 290) and its own `flex-wrap` can never fire, because the container is already as wide as its content. Below 505px there is no room for 441 + 64 of padding, and it simply overhangs:

  width  primary right edge  documentElement.scrollWidth − clientWidth
  600    568                 0
  500    473                 0
  430    473                 43
  390    473                 83
  360    473                 113
  320    473                 153

At 390x844 — a declared shot viewport — "Stop and read it back" ends at x=473 on a 390px screen: 83px of the primary action, the only way out of a live dictation takeover, is off the right edge, and `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` is 83, not the 0 the finding claims. The seat's other two claims do reproduce — the pair holds one row at every width, and `.darkFoot` at 390 falls 259 → 195px — but that 64px is bought by pushing the button off the screen it was meant to give back to. It is a symptom of the bug, not a benefit.

Second breakage the fix does not mention: `[data-app="notes"] .darkFoot .spacer` is shared. The phone read-back footer (src/notes.js:2417) is a second `.darkFoot` with the same pattern — `Add another`, `.spacer`, `Discard`, `Keep …`. Deleting the rule "and its node" as written strips the separation there and bunches all three buttons left, in the one state where a person is checking that the product heard them correctly.

The finding's own warning about `flex: 1 0 100%` on `.darkNote` is correct — `max-width: var(--measure)` clamps the hypothetical main size and the line never breaks; I confirmed 768 and 900 unchanged.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Keep the grouping; drop `flex: none`. Wrap the two buttons in one `.darkActs` element at src/notes.js:2387-2388 and delete the `<span class="spacer">` node at 2386, then:

[data-app="notes"] .darkActs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-end; align-items: flex-end; gap: 20px; flex: 0 1 auto; margin-left: auto; }

`flex: 0 1 auto` is the whole difference. Where the pair fits it behaves identically to `flex: none`; where it does not, the wrapper shrinks to the line and its own `flex-wrap` breaks the two buttons onto two right-aligned rows — still one group, still on screen. Driven at 320/360/390/430/500/505/600/700/768/800/900/1024/1280/1920: the pair holds one row from 600 to 1920 (and at 768x1024 it now sits at x=295..736, y=946, one row, on the takeover's own 32px margin); below 505 it stacks right-aligned with both buttons flush to the same right edge — 358 at 390, i.e. 390−32; `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` is 0 at every width including 320. The non-monotonic 600/500 flip-flop is gone in both variants.

Do the same at src/notes.js:2417-2421 in the same commit — wrap `Discard` and `Keep …` in `.darkActs`, leave `Add another` as the first child, delete that spacer node too — otherwise removing the shared `.spacer` rule collapses the phone read-back footer.

Be honest about the trade the correct fix makes: `.darkFoot` at 390 stays at 259px. The 195px the finding advertises is not available without pushing the primary off-screen; if 64px of transcript on a phone is worth buying, buy it somewhere real — the `margin: 40px 0 0` on `.darkWave` (src/notes.css:908) is the candidate.

Re-measure after it lands: `.darkFoot` height and both `.darkAct` rects at 320/360/390/430/500/600/768/900/1024/1280/1920; `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` at each; the same set for `?state=notes.readback` at ≤720; `.darkAct` scrollHeight = 44 at every width (the labels must not wrap inside the fixed-height pill); and re-run audit.mjs for the 44px hit-target pass plus interaction-check.mjs for the Esc/Enter routes off the takeover.
standing.breaks: As proposed: 83px of horizontal overflow at 390x844 and 153px at 320, with the primary "Stop and read it back" partly off-screen at every width below 505 — a regression from the current split, where both buttons are at least fully visible. It also breaks the phone read-back footer (src/notes.js:2417), which shares the `.spacer` rule the fix deletes. After the sharpened version lands, re-measure both `.darkAct` rects and `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` at 320/360/390/430/500/600/768/900/1024/1280/1920, the same for `?state=notes.readback` at ≤720, confirm `.darkAct` scrollHeight stays 44 (no label wrap inside the fixed-height pill), and re-run audit.mjs (hit targets) and interaction-check.mjs (Esc/Enter exits from the takeover).

standing.element: aside.taskPanel[role=dialog][aria-modal="true"], div.carry, and the Tasks Escape branch — tasks.board and tasks.dense
standing.problem: With a card picked up (Space), pressing Enter opens the task dialog and leaves the carry live: .carry still reads "↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel" beneath the scrim while the dialog is open. Escape is then consumed by the carry rather than by the dialog. Driven at 1440x960 and again at 390x844 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.board, Space → ArrowRight → Enter → Escape gives, in order: panelOpen=true, panelModal="true", carry still live; then after Escape — panelOpen STILL true, carry gone, #say reads "Move cancelled. Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is back in the to do column.", and document.activeElement is article.card, which document.elementFromPoint reports as covered by .tpScrim at 1440 and .tpFact at 390. A second Escape is needed to close the dialog. Tab from that point bounces back inside the panel, confirming the trap is live while focus sits outside it. I am not re-filing the closed question of whether Enter ought to drop; this is the layering of Escape and of focus, which is separately and independently broken.
standing.consequence: The person carries a card two lanes across, presses Enter believing they have committed it, and the first press of the only key a modal advertises silently returns the card to where it started — no strip, no visible statement, and Ctrl+Z afterwards says "Nothing left to undo." They are simultaneously left focused on something they cannot see, outside a dialog that declares itself modal. This is the one place on the surface where a dismiss key destroys work.
standing.fix: Resolve the carry at the moment a task panel opens: in the Tasks key handler, before openTaskId is set, commit the carried card and announce it with the same sentence the Space-drop branch uses, then tear down .carry. Make the Escape branch test for an open panel FIRST — close it and return focus to the card that opened it — and only fall through to "cancel the carry" when no panel is open. Assert that .carry and openTaskId can never both be truthy.
standing.assertion: On ?v=paper&state=tasks.board at 1440x960 and at 390x844: after Space, ArrowRight, Enter on the first To do card, document.querySelector('.carry') is null and the card's [data-lane] is "doing"; then one press of Escape leaves document.querySelector('.taskPanel') null, document.activeElement equal to the card that opened it, and the card's lane still "doing".
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces verbatim on two routes rather than the one the seat found, and must NOT be discarded. Do not ship half A of this fix; it fabricates completions.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (Chromium, real key events, ?v=paper&state=tasks.board, at 1440x960 and 390x844)
Every observation reproduces. Space -> "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company.", aria-grabbed="true"; ArrowRight -> "In progress, position 1 of 4."; Enter -> panelOpen=true, aria-modal="true", activeElement=ASIDE.taskPanel, and `.carry` still in the DOM reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company ↑↓←→ move Space drop Esc cancel" with aria-grabbed still set. Escape -> panel STILL open, carry gone, #say = "Move cancelled. Confirm marquee sides with the hire company is back in the to do column.", activeElement = ARTICLE.card, and document.elementFromPoint over that card returns .tpScrim at 1440 and .tpBody at 390 (the seat said .tpFact; trivially wrong, same conclusion). Tab from there hits BUTTON.ghost.tpClose — the trap at _gate-suite.html:13215-13228 pulls focus back inside while the app itself put focus outside. A second Escape closes the panel.

The code matches: the Escape ladder tests `carriedId` (12027-12033) BEFORE `openTaskId` (12035-12043), and the Enter branch (12111-12126) sets openTaskId without touching carriedId. Layering measured: `.carry` is z-index 6 (2195-2200), `.tpScrim` is z-index 40 at rgba(17,17,17,0.32), `.taskPanel` z-index 41 — so the pill is legible, dimmed, under the scrim. Screenshot confirms it reading "Esc cancel" while a modal sits above it.

TWO THINGS THE SEAT MISSED, both of which make it worse
1. It is not the key handler. The pointer route is identically broken: `pointerdown` at 13261 ends the carry only when the press lands off the carried card (`!card || card.dataset.id !== carriedId`), so a real mouse click on the carried card's own body opens the panel with the carry live — I drove it and got the same Escape theft. A fix "in the Tasks key handler" leaves half the defect standing and its own assertion (".carry and openTaskId can never both be truthy") false on delivery.
2. While the panel is open the pill prints three keys and two are dead. I pressed Space and ArrowRight with the panel open and carry live: nothing moved, nothing was said, lane stayed `doing`. The DIR and Space branches both require `event.target.closest(".card[data-id]")` and focus is on the aside. Escape is the only one of the three that fires, and it does the opposite of what a modal's Escape does. That is what earns the class.

SEVERITY — misleading, corrected up from the seat's unstated framing. Nothing is lost: the second Escape closes the panel, the revert is announced, the card can be picked up again. So not blocking. But in this state the surface asserts two things that are false — printed keycaps naming keys that do nothing, and `aria-modal="true"` on a dialog the application itself moves focus out of and onto a scrim-covered element. Both are assertions, both untrue.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — half A is a regression, half B is the whole repair
1. Half A fabricates completions. It says commit the carry "with the same sentence the Space-drop branch uses". That branch is 12093-12100: `if (lane === "done" && carriedFrom.lane !== "done") completed(task, …)`. I drove Space then four ArrowRights: the card sits over Done ("Done, position 1 of 6."), still in hand. Today Enter there just opens the panel. Under this fix, Enter over Done marks the task done — completedAt stamped, ledger receipt, undo armed — because the operator pressed the key whose only stated job is "open the task". That is far worse than the bug it repairs.
2. Half A's announcement is dead on arrival. `say()` (11193-11198) overwrites textContent; the Enter branch's own `say(title + ". Task open.")` fires immediately after. The drop sentence is replaced before any AT reads it. This is the live-region-overwritten class from the paid-for library, reintroduced.
3. Half A is the closed question the seat disclaims. Committing on Enter is `enter-during-carry-does-not-drop` (r1, refuted) and was refuted again inside `carry-drop-is-not-undoable` (r3) on grounds that still hold at runtime: the card carries `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` (10094) and the pill names Space alone. Making Enter a fourth commit key re-opens the advertised-vs-implemented gap in reverse. Disclaiming the question and then proposing the refuted answer does not make it a new question.
4. Half A is also unnecessary. Half B alone fixes both routes, because the Escape ladder is global and route-agnostic.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Keep half B, drop half A entirely, and add the one thing neither half covers.

1. Reorder the Escape ladder only. In `onKey` (_gate-suite.html:12011-12043), move the `if (openTaskId) { … }` block ABOVE the `if (carriedId) { … }` block. The code needed already exists verbatim — it closes the panel, calls `mount()`, focuses `.card[data-id="<was>"]` and says "Task closed." No new code, no new key contract. Because Escape is handled globally, this repairs the Enter route and the pointer route in one edit, and it satisfies the seat's own invariant in spirit: a modal is the innermost thing on the sheet, so it resolves first. Second Escape then cancels the carry exactly as the pill promises, with focus already back on the card and nothing covering it.

2. Do not resolve the carry when a panel opens. The carry surviving Enter is adjudicated behaviour (r1, r3) and it is coherent once Escape is layered right: read the task, close it, keep moving the card.

3. Stop printing dead keycaps under the scrim. `.carry` already ships a suppression state — `[data-app="tasks"] .carry[data-waiting]` at 2218 sets opacity 0 and pointer-events none. Emit `data-waiting` on the carry strip whenever `openTaskId` is truthy, in the same place the strip is built (10731), so nothing under a modal advertises Space and the arrows while both are inert. The carry's live state is still carried honestly by `aria-grabbed="true"` and `data-force="moving"` on the card, and the strip returns intact the moment the panel closes. If the founder prefers the reminder visible, replace the `kbd` row with the single sentence "Still in hand" for the duration — one string, no false keys — but the suppression is the smaller change and reuses a mechanism already on the surface.
standing.breaks:
What edit 1 plausibly breaks, and what to re-measure.

The Escape ladder is shared by eight surfaces and reordering two rungs is the whole risk. Re-drive the ladder end to end and confirm each still answers on the first press: tool popover open (toolOpen, 12013-12021, returns focus to `[data-tool]`); day picker (dayFor); card menu (closeMenu — must still sit ABOVE the panel, since `.cardDots` can be pressed on a card while a panel is closed, and the r3-closed `card-menu-renders-off-screen` lives here); panel with NO carry (unchanged code, must still say "Task closed." and land focus on the card, uncovered); carry with NO panel (unchanged, must still say "Move cancelled. … is back in the to do column."); note open (openNoteId — verify Enter's `openNoteId = null` still guarantees the two cannot coexist, or the reorder puts a rung above an unreachable one); the three filters; the planning drawer and `returnFromDrawer()`. Then drive the new two-press sequence at 1440 and 390: Space, ArrowRight, Enter, Escape must give panelOpen=false, activeElement = the card that opened it, elementFromPoint over that card = the card itself and not `.tpScrim`, carry still live with aria-grabbed="true"; second Escape must revert and announce. Repeat the whole sequence on the pointer route (click the carried card's own body) — that is the route the seat did not test and the one that proves the fix is route-agnostic.

What edit 3 plausibly breaks. `data-waiting` currently means one thing (the strip waiting to appear); giving it a second meaning risks the strip staying hidden after the panel closes. Assert on close that `.carry` has no `data-waiting` while `carriedId` is set. Also re-measure the strip's animation — `carryIn` (2248) runs on mount, so a strip that is re-shown on panel close must not replay the entrance every time a person opens and closes a task mid-carry; if it does, gate the animation on the pick-up mount only.

Gates. Re-run `interaction-check.mjs` (it asserts the carry and Escape model) and `audit.mjs`. Neither should move — no colour, weight, type, geometry or motion token is touched by any of the three edits — but the behaviour gate should gain an assertion that `.carry:not([data-waiting])` and `.taskPanel` are never in the DOM together, which is the seat's invariant expressed where it can actually be enforced.

standing.element: span.grow[title="Came from a note"] inside .cardFoot — tasks.board and tasks.dense
standing.problem: On the board the only sign that a task came through the seam is ``. Queried through CDP, Accessibility.getPartialAXTree returns role "generic", name "" — the title is not exposed as a name on a generic span. It has no role, no aria-label, no .sr text, no tabindex, and measures 13x13. Its sibling one element to the left does the same job correctly: `High priority`. A sweep of every visible [title] element across all eight states at 1440 finds exactly one title-only, textless, non-interactive mark on the whole surface, and this is it. The fact exists in words only one level down, inside the task panel, which prints "Activity · Came from a note in Notes".
standing.consequence: The seam is the argument for the suite existing, and on the board it is a tooltip. A screen-reader user reading the To do column is told nothing about which tasks came out of Notes; a touch user, who cannot hover, is told nothing at all. The one visible proof that the three products are one world is the only mark on the surface that does not speak, and its own neighbour shows the pattern that would fix it.
standing.fix: Add the spoken half the neighbouring mark already carries: `Came from a note.`, so the fact joins the card's text at the point the eye already sees it. No visual change.
standing.assertion: On ?v=paper&state=tasks.board at 1440x960, every article.card that contains a .grow must have "Came from a note" in its rendered textContent, and Accessibility.getPartialAXTree for the first .grow must return a non-empty name.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation, and do not ship this remedy as written. It fixes one of the two routes and leaves the one that matters most on this board untouched, and it is built on a misreading of what its own cited neighbour does. WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven in Chromium against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board` at 1440x960, and again at `tasks.dense` 1440, 768x1024 and 390x844. Six `.grow` spans per state, every one `13x13`, `textContent === ""`, markup verbatim as quoted (`src/tasks.js:385`). The `[title]` sweep is right: of 34 visible titled elements at 1440, `.grow` is the only textless, non-interactive one — the other two textless ones (`.railTile` Settings, `.ghost` More) are buttons carrying `aria-label`. `src/tasks.js:1128` confirms the fact exists in words only in the panel one level down. All of that is accurate. WHERE THE EVIDENCE IS INCOMPLETE, AND IT MATTERS. `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree` on `.cardFoot .grow` returns `{role:"generic", name:"", description:"Came from a note", ignored:false}`. The seat reported role and name and stopped. Chrome DOES expose the title — as the accessible **description** on a non-ignored node, not as a name. NVDA browse mode skips it because the node has no text, so "unspoken in practice" survives; "not exposed" does not. For a seat whose entire warrant is measured evidence, dropping the field that carries the string is not a rounding error. WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. The claim "its sibling one element to the left does the same job correctly" is false about the code. `.hi` does the job **twice**, and the seat copied the half that does not reach the ear on this board. I walked the card's full AX subtree via `getFullAXTree` with `childIds`: `.hi`'s ` priority` produces `StaticText "priority"` deep inside the card — browse-mode text only. The reason a keyboard user hears "High priority" is the OTHER half: `src/tasks.js:379-382` puts `task.priority + " priority"` into the `cd-` string, and the card is `
`. Measured on a fromNote card: name = "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company", description = "Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not, they need the call by Thursday. Mara & Finn. High priority." — aria-label overrides contents, so on focus the foot's inner text is never read. I injected the proposed fix and re-measured. Geometry: identical to the pixel (`.grow` 13x13 at x=280.453, `.cardDots` at x=326, `.cardFoot` 181x24, card 234x135.75) — the "no visual change" claim holds, because `.sr` is `position:absolute` (`src/shell.css:78`) and out of flow inside `.grow`'s `inline-flex`. Accessibility: the card's computed description was **byte-identical before and after**. The new text appears only as trailing `StaticText "Came from a note."` in the browse-mode subtree. So on a board whose cards are tabbable and arrow-carryable — the route the product advertises with `aria-keyshortcuts` — the seam fact is still absent after the fix, while every other card fact is present. The seat's own stated goal, "the fact joins the card's text at the point the eye already sees it," is not met on the primary route. It also lands badly where it does land: browse mode would read the full `cd-` sentence, then the foot again, then a disconnected trailing "Came from a note." after "High priority" — a fifth fragment on a card that already reads its summary twice. SEVERITY. Correcting the seat's implied class downward. The product asserts nothing untrue and does nothing it says it will not: the fact is on the card as a description on a non-ignored AX node, in the tooltip, and in words in the panel `open-task` reveals. This is a fact that is thinner in one channel than its neighbours, on the suite's own load-bearing gesture — visibly wrong but passable. Defect, not misleading, not blocking.
standing.sharpenedFix: Do not add an `.sr` span inside `.grow`. Put the fact where the card's spoken summary already lives — one line, `src/tasks.js:379-382`, appended to the `cd-` array after `comments`: ```js '' + esc([ said[0], task.note, task.tag, task.priority ? task.priority + " priority" : "", task.comments ? task.comments + (task.comments === 1 ? " comment" : " comments") : "", task.fromNote ? "Came from a note" : "", ].filter(Boolean).map((p) => String(p).replace(/\.$/, "")).join(". ")) + "." ``` This is strictly better than the proposed fix on every count and covers both routes with one change, because `cd-` is itself an `.sr` span sitting in the DOM: its `StaticText` is in the card's browse-mode subtree (I confirmed it in the walked AX tree), so browse mode gains the fact too, inside the card's one summary sentence rather than as a fifth trailing fragment. It adds no DOM node, so the `.grow` box and the `.grow + .cardDots { margin-left: auto }` rule (`src/tasks.css:739-746`) cannot be touched. Last position is right: provenance is the least urgent fact on the card and the `.grow` glyph sits last in the visible foot, so ear order matches eye order. Keep the `title` — it is the sighted user's answer to a 13x13 ink-4 glyph, and this engagement's palette and weight locks leave no other way to label it. If a seat later wants the browse-mode foot to echo it the way `.hi` does, that is a second, separate change and must not be made instead of this one.
standing.breaks:
WHAT IT PLAUSIBLY BREAKS. Very little, and all of it measurable. (1) The card's accessible description grows by ~19 characters on six of the fixture's tasks. Nothing clamps or truncates `cd-` — it is `.sr`, `clip-path: inset(50%)`, `white-space: nowrap`, `line-height: 1` — so there is no mid-word-clamp exposure from the lessons library here, but the `.sr` line-height rule exists precisely because leading on hidden strings kept landing on the audit's list, so re-run the type/leading gate rather than assuming. (2) The `.replace(/\.$/, "")` + `.join(". ")` chain means the appended string must NOT carry its own full stop, or the card reads "…note.." — write `"Came from a note"`, not `"Came from a note."` (the seat's own fix string carries a stop; that is a second reason not to copy it verbatim). (3) The description is now longer on the exact six cards that also carry priority and comments, which is the worst case for announcement length on a board a person arrows through card by card; listen to one lane end to end before shipping. (4) `src/app.js:395` sets `fromNote: true` on the card the seam creates at runtime, so a task that crosses from Notes during the session gains the sentence too — verify the seam route, not just the fixture.

WHAT TO RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS. Both gates: `audit.mjs --lab=…master-suite-2026-08` (the `.sr` leading rule has regressed on this class before) and `interaction-check.mjs`. Then, driven: the computed `description` on a fromNote card and on a non-fromNote card at 1440 via `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree`, to confirm the string appears exactly once and only where `fromNote` is true; `.grow` / `.cardDots` / `.cardFoot` / `.card` bounding rects at 390, 768, 1280, 1440, 1920 in both `tasks.board` and `tasks.dense`, to confirm the zero-pixel claim (my injection test showed identical rects, but that test added a node and this fix does not, so it should be even safer); the seam end to end — peel, send, `open-task`, `Ctrl/⌘Z` — confirming the new card announces the sentence and that undo removes it from both sides; and the panel, to confirm "Came from a note in Notes" (`src/tasks.js:1128`) still reads as the fuller statement one level down rather than as a duplicate of the card's.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .cardDots { visibility: hidden } and its .card:hover / .card[data-force="hover"] / .card:focus-within reveals; button.cardDots[tabindex="0"][aria-label="Move this task"]
standing.problem: The card's move menu is a tab stop going forward and not going back. .cardDots is rendered with tabindex="0" but painted visibility:hidden at rest, becoming visible only via .card:hover or .card:focus-within (the coarse-pointer block overrides it to visibility:visible). Forward this works, because the card takes focus first and reveals it. Backward it does not: at 1440x960 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.board, focusing button.trayAdd ("Add a task to To do") and pressing Shift+Tab lands on button.who — cardDots is skipped entirely. The identical sequence at 390x844 lands on button.cardDots, because there the control is visible at rest. Programmatic .focus() on it at 1440 also fails (activeElement stays BODY) until the card is focused first. The rule's own comment reads "`visibility` rather than `opacity`, so a hidden control is genuinely out of the tab order rather than an invisible tab stop" — it is neither out of the order nor reliably in it; and the menu's own comment elsewhere calls it "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take."
standing.consequence: At every desk width a keyboard user who tabs one stop past the move menu cannot get back to it — Shift+Tab walks over it into the card, and the only way back is to tab forward through the remaining seventeen stops of the document. The board's forward and reverse tab orders are not the same list, which is the one property a keyboard user assumes without ever checking, and the control it costs them is the only pointer-free route to moving a card.
standing.fix: Let paint, not focusability, do the hiding. On [data-app="tasks"] .cardDots replace `visibility: hidden` with `opacity: 0`, and add `[data-app="tasks"] .cardDots:focus-visible { opacity: 1 }` declared after the existing hover/focus-within reveals so the interaction rules still win. Leave the coarse-pointer override as it is. Correct the rule's comment, which currently states the opposite of what ships.
standing.assertion: On ?v=paper&state=tasks.board at 1440x960, the sequence of document.activeElement produced by tabbing forward from document.body to the end must be the exact reverse of the sequence produced by shift-tabbing back from the last stop, and Shift+Tab from .tray[data-lane="todo"] .trayAdd must land on a button.cardDots.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, every measurement reproduces, and it must NOT be discarded. The fix as written makes the move menu invisible on every phone and invisible on mouse hover on the desk, which is strictly worse than the defect it repairs.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, file:///.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board)
- 1440x960: the roving stop is the card "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company"; its `.cardDots[tabindex="0"]` computes `visibility: hidden` at rest. Focus `button.trayAdd` ("Add a task to To do"), Shift+Tab → `button.who` ("Mara & Finn"), then `button.tick`, then `article.card`. cardDots is skipped entirely. Forward from the card: tick → who → cardDots → trayAdd. Exactly the asymmetry claimed.
- Programmatic `.focus()` on it at 1440 leaves `document.activeElement === BODY`. Confirmed.
- 390x844 with touch emulated (pointer: coarse), the same Shift+Tab lands on `button.cardDots`. The seat's 390 claim is right — note it only holds with `hasTouch`, since a bare 390 viewport in desktop chromium does not match `@media (pointer: coarse)` and behaves like 1440.
- The quoted comment at src/tasks.css:749-750 does state the opposite of what ships.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. Applied literally — base `opacity: 0` in place of `visibility: hidden`, one added `:focus-visible` rule, "leave the coarse-pointer override as it is" — and driven:
1. The three reveal rules at src/tasks.css:763-765 declare `visibility: visible`, not `opacity: 1`. Once the base is opacity, they are no-ops. Measured at 1440 with the fix injected: hovering the card gives `opacity: 0`. The menu no longer appears for a mouse at all. On a sheet whose own comment (src/tasks.js:1064) calls it "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take", the fix deletes the mouse route.
2. The coarse-pointer override at src/tasks.css:1704 also only sets `visibility: visible`. The fix instructs leaving it alone, so at 390 with touch the measured result is `visibility: visible, opacity: 0` — the permanently-present phone menu becomes an invisible 44px button on every card. That is a catastrophic regression, not a repair.
3. The added `.cardDots:focus-visible` rule is dead weight either way: focusing the dots puts focus inside the card, so `.card:focus-within` already covers it.

SEVERITY. Defect, not blocking or misleading. The untrue sentence is a source comment Orla never sees; the menu is reachable forward from the card, and the board's advertised keyboard move route is carry (Space, arrows, Enter), not the menu. What is genuinely wrong is a control reachable in one direction only.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Move the hiding to paint, but move ALL of it, and keep nothing invisible clickable.

In src/tasks.css:751-765, on `[data-app="tasks"] .cardDots` replace `visibility: hidden` with `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none;`. Leave the `transition` list alone (color and background-color only) so the reveal stays instant, as it is today, and no new motion enters the audit's surface. Then rewrite the reveal block so it drives the property that now does the hiding:

[data-app="tasks"] .card:hover .cardDots,
[data-app="tasks"] .card[data-force="hover"] .cardDots,
[data-app="tasks"] .card:focus-within .cardDots,
[data-app="tasks"] .cardDots:focus-visible { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; }

And in the coarse-pointer block, src/tasks.css:1704, change `visibility: visible` to `opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto;` — it cannot be left as it is, which is the fix's fatal error. Then correct the comment at src/tasks.css:748-750: it should say the slot is reserved so revealing it moves nothing, and that the control is painted out rather than removed, so it is a tab stop in both directions rather than one that exists only when walked forward.
standing.breaks:
What the sharpened fix plausibly breaks, and what to re-measure:

1. Accessibility-tree exposure. `visibility: hidden` hides cardDots from screen readers; `opacity: 0` does not. After the change every card on the board — not just the roving stop — exposes a "Move this task" button to browse mode, where today only the coarse-pointer build does. Re-measure the SR reading order of one tray at 1440 and decide whether that is acceptable; it matches what a phone already announces, so it is defensible, but it is a real change and should be a deliberate call, not a side effect.

2. Invisible hit targets. `opacity: 0` alone leaves the 24px button and its `inset: -4px` ::before ring clickable. `pointer-events: none` at rest closes that; without it, a tap or click that lands in the card foot without a preceding hover (stylus, synthetic click, touch on a non-coarse device) would open the move menu instead of the note. Re-measure: press the card foot's empty right-hand slot with the mouse moved away first, and confirm the note opens, not the menu.

3. Menu placement. src/tasks.js:2697 positions the popup from the trigger's measured rect. Both `visibility: hidden` and `opacity: 0` preserve layout, so geometry should be identical — but re-run the card-menu placement check at 1280 and 390 to confirm `card-menu-renders-off-screen` (r3, closed) has not reopened.

4. Re-run both gates: audit.mjs (hit targets and contrast sample computed style; a 0-opacity control could read differently) and interaction-check.mjs. Then re-drive the full tab walk at 390 touch, 768, 1280, 1440, 1920 in both directions and confirm the walk is now symmetric: card → tick → who → cardDots → trayAdd forward, and the exact reverse backward, with the menu painted at every step where it holds focus.

rounds.notes: selfInflicted 0.86 — twenty-five of the twenty-nine standing problems are in work built between rounds 3 and 4, which is the honest reading of a round that followed the largest build of the engagement. seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
rounds.headline: Seven seats, 29 findings, 25 standing — 4 blocking, 6 misleading, 12 defect, 3 refinement — and the engagement's first sign-off, from the seat that scored it 9.0. Every one of the 25 is now closed. The round's whole shape was one class: a sentence that was TRUE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN and had been outlived by the thing it described. A closed door still apologising for a search that now filters as you type. Ctrl+K answering with that apology while the field it should focus sat 40px below. A completion screen printing “0 became tasks and the rest stayed here” and offering “See them in Tasks” as its only filled action. An index head reciting the workspace total over eight rows. None of it throws, none of it looks broken, and all of it reads as finished prose — findable only by asking the product a question you already know the answer to.

confirmed.element: More menu item data-door="home" (src/app.js:97, 108; src/tasks.js:542) against the project switcher's live All projects option (src/tasks.js:635)
confirmed.problem: Two different things are called "All projects", one of them works and the other says it does not exist, and they can be on screen together. With that board on screen, open More: the first item reads "All projects — Not here yet", tooltip "Every project in one list. Not here yet." confirmed.consequence: The one system in this product that exists to be believed — a door that says plainly it is not built — is caught saying it about a feature the person is using. Once a person catches an unavailable-message being false they stop reading all of them, which costs the product every other honest door at once.
confirmed.fix: In src/app.js restore the door's own name and its own destination: `MORE_DOORS` entry becomes `{ key: "home", label: "Home" }`, and `NOT_YET.home` becomes "Your starting screen for Signal Studio. Not here yet." Mirror the same string in src/tasks.js:542. Leave the project switcher's "All projects" and its "Everything you are running, on one board" exactly as they are — that one is true.

confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED — every claim reproduces verbatim, the code reads exactly as quoted, no gate covers it, and it is not a re-file. DRIVEN (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, at 1440x960, 768x1024 and 390x844). Press `[data-act="projects"]`, activate `.projItem[data-project="all"]`, then press `[data-rail="more"]`: - Tasks `h1` = "All projects"; `[data-act="projects"]` text "All projects", aria-label "All projects, switch project"; head "3 projects, day 11 of 356"; `.card` count = 40; `#say` "All projects. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it." - `.morePop` items at 1440/768 = `[{door:"home", text:"All projects" + "Not here yet", title:"Every project in one list. Not here yet."}, Inbox, Help]`; at 390 the same three plus Settings. - Co-visibility measured, not assumed: I enumerated every leaf node whose text is exactly "All projects" and is inside the viewport. **Two, at every width.** 1440: the switcher at (207,35) and the More item at (135,773). 768: (116,83) and (129,663). 390: (25,80) and (200,621). Screenshotted at 1440 — the board shows "All projects · 10 of 40 done · 3 projects, day 11 of 356" with 40 cards from three projects, and 700px below it a panel reading "ALSO IN SIGNAL STUDIO / All projects — Not here yet". That is the finding, exactly as filed, in one frame. THE ICON MAKES IT WORSE THAN FILED, and the seat missed it. `src/icons.js:24` — `home: ''` — is a literal house. So the row draws a house, is keyed `home`, and is labelled "All projects". The mark, the key and the label already disagree with each other before the board contradicts any of them. That is independent corroboration that the label is the thing that drifted. MECHANISM AND PROVENANCE. `src/app.js:107-111` `MORE_DOORS = [{key:"home", label:"All projects"}, inbox, help]`; `src/app.js:97` `NOT_YET.home = "Every project in one list. Not here yet."`. In round 4 the label was already "All projects" and a refutation of `more-menu-heading-contradicts-every-item-under-it` even cites it approvingly ("'All projects / Every project in one list' is unmistakably the workspace level"). What changed underneath it is that round 4 built the project architecture and shipped a live merged view whose own name is "All projects". The door's sentence was true when written and is now false; nobody re-read it after the switcher landed. That is a genuine round-4 regression of a round-1 constraint, not taste. NOT A RE-FILE, checked against the ledgers rather than asserted. `all-projects-speaks-a-placeholder` (r4, closed) is the switcher's live region saying "the project" — a different element, a different string, and its fix landed (`#say` now reads "All projects."). `more-menu-heading-contradicts-every-item-under-it` (r4, refuted) is the panel's `

` heading, not the item's label; its refutation turned on invisibility of the panel, which has since been fixed (`.morePop` now paints `rgb(17,17,17)` opaque with `inset 0 0 0 1px` and `--float-ink`, items at `rgb(255,255,255)`). `closed-doors-defer-to-closed-doors` (r4, refuted) is the "comes with X" grammar in Tasks. `two-account-tiles-*`, `account-tile-named-two-ways`, `closed-doors-two-treatments` — all a different door. None of them touch this collision. NOT A GATE RESTATEMENT. `interaction-check.mjs` has zero hits for `moreItem`, `data-door` or "All projects". `verify.mjs:661-684` asserts only that each of home/inbox/help/settings/me is `aria-disabled`, reachable, and carries a title matching `/not here yet/i` — it never reads the label. `tools/flow.mjs:143` counts `>= 3` doors. `tools/projects.mjs:253` asserts `all.head === "All projects"` on the BOARD head, and `:437` measures the panel's contrast. Not one of them can see this. SEVERITY — misleading, and I am confirming the class rather than correcting it. The error runs in the seat's favour, so it does not flip the conclusion (94% across, not 92%), but a UI-composition finding whose entire case is a pair of gap figures does not get to have three of them wrong.

2. THE PREMISE. "The gap it is supposed to divide" is the seat's assumption, not the artefact's claim. A 1px hairline sitting 6px in front of a right-aligned cluster is the standard toolbar segment-delimiter idiom — it heads the cluster, it does not float in the middle of the void. And across all eight states at 390/768/1280/1440/1920, no element that paints (non-zero box, not `.sr`, opacity > 0) computes a `font-size` below 11px.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE OBSERVATION — do not discard the observation, and do not ship this remedy as written. It is a defect, not more.

WHAT REPRODUCES, EXACTLY. Driven in chromium at 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`: `.rail .railAvatar` renders 'OR' at font-size 11px, letter-spacing 0.825px, text-indent 0.825px, line-height 14.08px on a 32px disc at (34,900), ink 17.73px. `[data-app="tasks"] .dockAvatar` renders the same two letters at 10px / 0.4px / text-indent 0px / line-height 13px on a 34px disc at (907,883), ink 15.42px. Both painted, both on screen, 873px apart. Every number the seat quotes is exact, including the 8.1px-vs-9.3px side clearance. Notes' `.dockAvatar` (:4025) is 11px/0.825px/0.825px/14.08px, ink 17.73px — so two of the three instances agree and Tasks' dock is the odd one. The COMPOSITION.md §5 quote is verbatim and the ruling genuinely landed only on `.railAvatar`.

WHY THE FIX FAILS — THE LOAD-BEARING ERROR. `--tr-cap` is defined in exactly one place in the file, line 3321, inside `[data-app="notes"] { … }`. It does not exist in the Tasks scope. I applied the seat's four declarations verbatim to the live page and read the result: `getPropertyValue('--tr-cap')` on the Tasks disc returns the empty string, so `letter-spacing: var(--tr-cap)` and `text-indent: var(--tr-cap)` are invalid at computed-value time and fall back to `normal` / `0px`. Measured after the fix: 11px / letter-spacing **normal** / text-indent **0px** / 14.08px, ink **16.08px** — not 17.73px, and not "byte-identical" to anything. The fix does not unify the monogram; it invents a third setting for it, which is the exact defect the finding was filed against.

THREE MORE FACTUAL ERRORS. (1) "`.railAvatar` (:366–369)" is `.railName`; `.railAvatar` is :426–439, and it writes raw literals — `11px`, `0.075em`, `1.28` — not tokens, deliberately, per its own comment at :424: "the numbers are written out rather than tokenised because the shell may not depend on a product." So "byte-identical to `.railAvatar`" is impossible with `var()`s. (2) "the dock's total width is unchanged at 385px" — `[data-app="tasks"] .dock` measures 369.89px at 1280, 1440 and 1920. The width is indeed unchanged; the number is wrong. (3) "`.dockAvatar` is a fixed-width grid item" — the dock is `display: flex`; the disc is a flex item that is itself `display: grid` internally. The conclusion survives (`width: 34px`, flex-grow 0), the stated mechanism does not.

THE typeRamp CLAUSE IS FALSE TO THE FILE. "10px is the only type below 11px anywhere in the application, in any of the eight states, at any of the five viewports" holds only for the eight *static* states — I swept every visible element with direct text across all eight states at 390/768/1280/1440/1920 and the disc was the sole hit. But this engagement asks you to drive it, and the moment you do, it breaks: focus a card, press Space, and `[data-app="tasks"] .carry kbd` paints ↑↓←→ / Space / Esc at **10px** (:2008–2011), 19px tall, on screen. `[data-app="tasks"] .ghost em.toolDot` (:3189) is a fourth 10px declaration. Deleting `10` from `typeRamp` would therefore not "make the ladder a law again" — it would leave three shipping 10px rules under a config that claims none exist, and it only stays green because the audit never visits a carry.

FOURTH CLAUSE IS A NO-OP. ":11300 `<span class="dockAvatar">`" is markup inside a template string, not a declaration. It already matches `[data-app="tasks"] .dockAvatar`, so the single CSS change covers the loading dock; there is nothing there to "apply the same to."

SEVERITY. Correctly a defect, no higher. Nothing is asserted untrue and nothing fails to work; it is one pixel of size and 0.4px of tracking on two letters, on discs of different diameter and different ground, 873px apart. It is real and worth fixing at this bar, but it is not misleading and not blocking.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Write literals, the way `.railAvatar` deliberately does, because `--tr-cap` does not exist outside `[data-app="notes"]`.

1. At :2041 replace `font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em;` with `font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.075em; text-indent: 0.075em;`. The `text-indent` is not optional — without it the trailing letter-space pushes two capitals off centre, which is why `.railAvatar` carries it at :437.

2. At :2786 delete `[data-app="tasks"] .dockAvatar { line-height: 13px; } /* 10px */` and instead add `[data-app="tasks"] .dockAvatar,` to the existing 11px leading group at :2787–2790 (`.trayName, .trayCount, .tag, .when { line-height: 14px; } /* 11px */`). This keeps Tasks' own stated rule — "a label of size N leads at round(1.3N)" — rather than importing Notes' 1.28 ratio into a product that does not own it. 14px against the rail disc's 14.08px is 0.08px, invisible, and it leaves Tasks' leading table internally consistent, which the seat's `var(--lh-tight)` would have broken.

3. Do NOT touch `elevate.config.json`. Removing `10` from `typeRamp` while :2008 and :3189 still declare 10px would make the config assert something the file contradicts the moment a card is picked up. If the ladder is to become a law, that is a separate, larger pass: lift `[data-app="tasks"] .dockField kbd`, `.carry kbd` and `.ghost em.toolDot` to 11px first, re-measure the carry HUD and the ⌘K keycap for overflow at 390 and 768, and only then drop the step. Short of that, record the ruling in COMPOSITION.md §5 directly under the `.railAvatar` entry — that is where the first half of this ruling is already written down, and it is what actually stops the step coming back.

4. Delete nothing at :11300. One class selector already covers the loading dock and the board dock, so the disc cannot resize between "Opening the board" and the board.

WHAT IT PLAUSIBLY BREAKS. Nothing geometric: I applied the size change live and the disc stays 34x34 (explicit width/height, flex-grow 0), the dock stays 369.89px at 1280/1440/1920, and the ink grows 15.42px to 17.73px inside 34px, leaving 8.135px a side. standing.element:
Tasks card meta glyph — span.grow[aria-label="Came from a note in Notes"] — and the task panel's ACTIVITY line, the bare
  • Came from a note in Notes
standing.problem: Driven at 1440 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.board. Six cards wear a small document glyph whose accessible name is "Came from a note in Notes". It is a SPAN, tabIndex −1, no role, sitting in a row between two real buttons (button.tick "Mark done" and button.cardDots "Move this task"). Open the card and the panel repeats the sentence as a bare LI, tabIndex −1, no role; the panel's only controls are aria-label "Close task" and "Mark done". Notes carries the whole return leg — N.taskOf(noteId) exists in fixture.js, and button.deskFactLink "Open in Tasks: …" mounts Tasks and reveals the card. Tasks carries nothing equivalent. The seam runs one way.
standing.consequence: Orla is standing at the board, which is where she stands most of the day. A card tells her it came from something she wrote, in a glyph that sits between two buttons and therefore looks like one. She presses it and nothing happens; she opens the card and reads the same sentence again, still inert. The one thing the suite exists to make possible — getting back to the words behind the task — is available only from the side she is not on. Notes says "Your note stays here", "still yours to edit", "every note stayed here"; Tasks names the note and then refuses to open it.
standing.fix: Invert the existing LINK map in src/fixture.js into N.noteOf(taskId), beside the N.taskOf that already ships. Render the card glyph as <button class="grow cardSrc" aria-label="Open the note this came from: {lede}"> at the same 44×44 hit target .cardDots beside it already uses, and render the panel's ACTIVITY line as that same button with its existing visible text. On activate: mount Notes, lift N.noteOf(id) onto the desk through the path an index-row click already uses, move focus into .readBody, and write "Opened the note this came from." to #say. No new surface, no new copy register, no new colour — one map inversion and one handler reusing the lift that exists.
standing.assertion: At 1440 on ?v=paper&state=tasks.board, the card "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" contains a focusable control whose accessible name matches /^Open the note this came from/; activating it leaves [data-app="notes"] as the only non-hidden .app, .readBody textContent contains "Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn", document.activeElement.closest(".readBody") is non-null, and #say reads "Opened the note this came from." The same assertion driven from the task panel's ACTIVITY row.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, AND ON THE CLASS. The asymmetry is real and I reproduced every DOM fact — but the fix is broken on its own map, on half its targets, and on the API it assumes exists, and the artifact already carries this as a named, deferred DECISION rather than a defect. WHAT REPRODUCES (driven, chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=tasks.board). Six `.card .grow` spans, each `aria-label="Came from a note in Notes"`, tabIndex −1, 13x13, on demo-t-01, demo-t-02, demo-t-06, demo_task_checkout, demo_task_linen, demo_task_registrar. Opening a card gives a panel whose only controls are "Close task", "Mark done" and the ``; ACTIVITY is a bare `
  • Came from a note in Notes
    • `, tabIndex −1. A census of `[data-app="tasks"] *` for anything naming a note returns those six spans and nothing else. The other leg works: lifting n01 and pressing `.deskFactLink` mounts Tasks, reveals the card, focuses it and says "Opened in Tasks. Your note stayed in Notes." Two of the seat's minor claims are off — the span carries `role="img"`, not "no role" — and one is exactly right: `.cardDots` measures 44.0x44.0 (the tick is 18x18 with a −7px `::before`, i.e. 32x32), so the seat's hit-target number is the correct one to copy. WHY THE FIX FAILS. (1) HALF THE INVERTED MAP POINTS AT NOTES THE PRODUCT CANNOT OPEN. `LINK` inverted gives s1/s2/s3 for demo_task_checkout / demo_task_linen / demo_task_registrar. Those ids are not in `N.notes` (n01–n14) and never appear as an index row in Notes' notebook scene — I enumerated `.idxRow` there and got exactly n01–n14, no s-row. They live only in `N.crossed`, rendered only in `?state=notes.seam`, where the three rows print the TASK wording, its lane and its age ("Clear Sunday 11am late checkout with housekeeping | Done | 20 ho…"). Driven: in notes.seam I clicked `.idxRow[data-id="s1"]` and `.readBody` did not change — it stayed on n14's heating note. There is no desk lift for these three and no `.readBody` to move focus into. The seat's load-bearing sentence, "lift N.noteOf(id) onto the desk through the path an index-row click already uses", describes a path that does not exist for three of the six cards. Shipping it turns three honest provenance glyphs into three buttons that promise a note and deliver nothing — which is the misleading class the finding is trying to close. (2) IT INVERTS THE WRONG MAP. Live crossings are held in `crossings` in app.js, not in fixture `LINK` — `openTask()` reads `crossings[noteId] || N.taskOf(noteId)` precisely for that reason. I drove a real send (n03 → peel → send), walked the spine to Tasks, and the board carried SEVEN glyph cards: the six fixture ones plus `seam_n03_1`. The inverted `LINK` returns null for `seam_n03_1`. Under this fix the newest card on the board — the one the operator just made, where "open the note this came from" matters most — gets a dead button. (3) THE HANDLER IT REUSES DOES NOT EXIST. Notes registers `{ show: paint, api: { paint, state } }` (notes.js:3904) — a repaint and a state getter, nothing that opens a note by id. `window.__SUITE` exposes go / cross / uncross / openTask / register / reproject / start / refresh; there is no `openNote`. `N.noteOf` is `undefined`. So this is a new public entry point on Notes plus a new suite-level mirror of `openTask()`, not "one map inversion and one handler". (4) IT IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD, AS A DECISION. BUILD-LIST.md §6 names it verbatim: "The seam only runs one way. A task on the board carries `fromNote` and cannot open the note it came from. The join in `src/fixture.js` already holds both ends, so the data is there; what is missing is a control on the card and a decision about whether Tasks is allowed to send you to Notes mid-board." The author found this, wrote it down, and identified the missing piece as a product decision. The seat re-files it as a wiring oversight. ON SEVERITY. Nothing here asserts something untrue and nothing advertised fails. "Came from a note in Notes" is a statement of provenance, correctly given `role="img"`; it never promises navigation, and Notes' own copy promises the opposite direction ("Your note stays here", "the one-way edge into Tasks", fixture.js:467). A one-way seam that says it is one-way is not misleading. Refinement.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Do not ship the card-foot button. The glyph is honest as a provenance mark and should stay a `role="img"` span. If the founder makes the decision BUILD-LIST.md §6 asks for — that Tasks may send you to Notes mid-board — the correct build has four parts, and it is a day's work, not a map inversion:

1. Make the three ledger-only crossings real notes. Move s1/s2/s3 into `N.notes` with `sent: true` and their existing `task`/`lane`/`crossedWhen`, so the notebook index carries them and the desk can lift them the way it lifts n01. Re-assert `N.counts.sent` and the `fromNote.length !== Object.keys(LINK).length` guard afterwards. Until this lands, half the seam has no note to return to and no back-link should be drawn at all.

2. Resolve through the live map first. Add `N.noteOf = function (taskId) { … }` as the inverse of `LINK`, and in app.js write `openNote(taskId)` as the exact mirror of `openTask`: `var noteId = Object.keys(crossings).find(k => crossings[k] === taskId) || (window.NOTES.noteOf && window.NOTES.noteOf(taskId));` — `crossings` first, fixture second, or the card the operator just sent gets a dead control.

3. Give Notes a real door. Extend its registration at notes.js:3904 to `api: { paint, state, open }`, where `open(noteId)` sets `openId`, sets `refocus = { kind: "read" }`, paints, and returns false for an unknown id. `openNote` must handle that false the way `openTask` handles a missing card: `go("notes")` and say "That note is not in this notebook."

4. Put the control in the PANEL only, not on the card. Turn the existing ACTIVITY line into `<button type="button" class="tpSrc" data-act="open-note" data-id="…">Came from a note in Notes</button>` with its existing visible text — a person in the panel has already committed to one task, so leaving the board costs them nothing, whereas six new 44x44 targets on the board cost every card a tab stop and a chunk of its drag region. On activate: `go("notes", { announce: false, focus: false })`, `open(noteId)`, focus `.readBody`, and say "Opened the note this came from. Your task stayed in Tasks." — mirroring, word for word, the sentence the other leg already speaks.

(c) Mounting Notes from mid-board is a product switch: the board's scroll position and the returned focus must be re-measured against r1 `product-switch-loses-place` and r2 `board-does-not-scroll-focus-into-view`. (d) `N.counts.sent` is asserted in fixture.js and would move if s1–s3 are promoted into `N.notes`. RE-MEASURE AFTER: the tab route at 390/768/1280/1440/1920; `.cardFoot` geometry and card drag hit region; board scroll+focus across a Tasks→Notes→Tasks round trip; `#say` on both legs; the ONE WORLD throws in fixture.js (the `fromNote.length !== Object.keys(LINK).length` assert) and `N.counts.sent`; both gates.

standing.element: .app / .sheet on a spine click — .rail [data-rail="notes|tasks|timeline"]
standing.problem: Sampled across requestAnimationFrame at 1440 while clicking .rail [data-rail="timeline"] from tasks.board: t+0ms reads tasks visible / timeline hidden, t+22ms reads tasks hidden / timeline visible, and every sampled frame carries opacity 1 and transform: none. getComputedStyle on both .app and .sheet returns transition-duration 0s. Meanwhile .railTile runs color, background-color 0.14s cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) — so the spine tile is still settling for 140ms after the sheet behind it has already been wholly replaced.
standing.consequence: The suite makes exactly one architectural claim — three products mounted at once, none ever torn down, one room with the walls taken out — and one gesture carries it. That gesture presents as three separate pages swapping in a single frame. Nothing breaks and nothing is lost (I confirmed a half-typed draft in .topField and a note lifted onto the desk both survive a round trip), but the person never feels the continuity the architecture actually delivers. It is the moment a discerning stranger decides whether this is one application or a shell around three, and right now the pixels answer wrongly while the code answers rightly.
standing.fix: On the incoming .app only, add an entrance of opacity 0→1 with translateY(2px→0) over var(--motion-fast) (140ms, already the token) on var(--curve), fired by the same attribute flip that unhides it. Leave the outgoing .app an instant hidden so no dead frame and no held-open scroller appears. Add [data-app] { animation: none } to the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in src/shell.css, which the codebase already branches on in eighteen places. No new token, no new duration, no change to the spine's own 140ms.
standing.assertion: Sampling getComputedStyle(incoming .app).opacity on successive requestAnimationFrames after a spine click yields at least three distinct values strictly between 0 and 1 under reducedMotion "no-preference", and exactly one value (1) under reducedMotion "reduce"; the outgoing .app is hidden on the first sampled frame in both cases; and the audit's motion check still passes with no duration above var(--motion-fast).
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE OBSERVATION. Every measurement in the observation reproduces exactly — do not discard the observation — but the proposed remedy is a no-op on two of the three products and actively destructive on the third.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, rAF-sampling `.app[data-app="tasks"]` and `.app[data-app="timeline"]` across a click on `.rail [data-rail="timeline"]`: the flip lands between the first and second sampled frame, and all 26 sampled frames out to 406ms read `opacity: 1, transform: none`. `getComputedStyle` on all three `.app` elements and on their `.sheet` children returns `transition-duration: 0s` and `animation-name: none`. `.railTile` reads `color 0.14s cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background-color 0.14s cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`. Every fact is right. The suite really does hard-cut the sheet while the spine tile is still settling.

WHY THE FIX IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL FOR NOTES AND TASKS. `src/shell.css:110` is `.app { display: contents; }`, and only `.app[data-app="timeline"]` (shell.css:114) overrides it to `display: block`. A `display: contents` element generates no principal box, so `opacity` and `transform` on it have nothing to apply to. I injected the fix verbatim (`@keyframes appIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(2px) } to { opacity: 1; transform: none } }` on `.app:not([hidden])`) and drove it. Chromium reports the animation running — `animation-name: appIn`, `opacity` ticking 0 → 0.46 → 0.90 → 1 — and reports `transform: none` in the same frame, which is the browser telling you the transform is not being applied. Screenshot proof, animation paused at the 0% keyframe, rail transitions disabled, 1340x960 crop: the tasks frame at `opacity: 0` is **132,700 bytes** — the board fully painted, unchanged. The Timeline frame at the same paused keyframe is **5,875 bytes** — blank. So the seat's own fix delivers an entrance to Timeline only and silently nothing to Notes and Tasks, which are the two products the seat sampled. The finding would ship, look correct in a code review, and leave two-thirds of the defect exactly where it is.

WHAT IT BREAKS ON THE THIRD. `[data-app="timeline"] .b-edit` is `position: fixed` (timeline.css:1154), and at 390 it stays fixed — measured `position: fixed`, rect top 294 / bottom 832 in an 844 viewport, correctly anchored to the bottom edge. A `transform` on `.app[data-app="timeline"]` makes it the containing block for that fixed panel: the same measurement with `transform: translateY(2px)` on the app reads **top -294 / bottom 244** — the moment editor is flung 588px off the top of the phone screen. So on a phone, leaving Timeline with an editor open and coming back would throw the editor off-screen for the whole 140ms entrance and snap it back. `[data-app="timeline"][data-undo="true"] .b-undoHome .b-undo` (timeline.css:1877) is fixed under the same rule and takes the same hit. The fix trades a clean cut for a 140ms glitch.

TWO SMALLER ERRORS. (1) The reduced-motion clause is redundant: `foundation.css:139-145` already zeroes `--motion-fast` to `0ms` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so an animation declared at `var(--motion-fast)` is already 0ms there; the extra `[data-app] { animation: none }` block adds a rule that changes nothing. The "eighteen places" count is right (18 matches across the CSS), but it is cited to justify a rule that is not needed. (2) `.app:not([hidden])` also fires on the product mounted at first paint, so the whole app would fade in on load — not fatal, but not what the finding describes and not what it budgeted for.

SEVERITY. Downgraded to refinement. Nothing is broken and nothing is untrue: three products are mounted at once and none is ever torn down, and an instant swap is a defensible — arguably the honest — expression of that. Linear switches views on a cut. This is a taste improvement with a real argument behind it, not a defect.

And it silently does nothing at all for Notes and Tasks, so anyone who ships it will believe the defect is closed when it is two-thirds open.

What the sharpened version could still touch, and what to re-measure after it lands: (1) `go()` in `src/app.js:263` calls `sheet.focus({ preventScroll: true })` on the arriving sheet — re-drive a spine switch by keyboard and confirm the focus ring is not invisible for the first frames and that focus still lands on the sheet, not the tile. standing.problem: The dictation demo and the notebook show one note in two different wordings, on one screen at the same time. standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, every observation reproduces verbatim, and it must NOT be discarded — it is the sharpest misleading-class defect I drove this round. The fix is refuted because its one guard is factually wrong about the code, and shipping it as written would replace a true sentence on the phone with a silent no-op and a false announcement.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, at 1920/1440/1280/768/390).

1. Tasks search works. `[data-app="tasks"] .dockInput` is a live `input[type=search]`, `aria-label`/`placeholder` both "Search tasks", visible at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 768. Typing "marquee" takes the board from 13 cards to 2 at every one of those widths. Typing "zzz" renders the designed `.emptyBoard`. Exact.
2. Ctrl+K denies it. Focus a `.card`, press Ctrl+K: `document.activeElement` stays on the card and `#say` reads "Search arrives with the other views." at 1920/1440/1280/768/390. Exact.
3. Notes answers the same chord properly — `.searchTop` mounts, focus lands on `INPUT#q`, `#say` reads "Search everything you wrote." Exact.
4. The justifying comment is stale and the pill is gone. I enumerated every `kbd` inside `[data-app="tasks"]` at all five widths: **zero**. Tasks' dock renders a bare input, no keycap, no `title`. (The "Ctrl K" keycap in the document belongs to Notes' `.dockField` — an unscoped `querySelector` catches it, which is worth knowing when re-measuring.) `src/tasks.js:2291` still reads "The pill prints this key, so the key has to answer — with the same sentence the pill's own tooltip carries", and `src/tasks.js:951` records the conversion that killed the pill: "A real field, not a door. It was the one control at the foot of the sheet that looked like an input and refused to be one." Exact.

NOT A RE-FILE, AND I CHECKED. `search-door-answered-three-ways` (r3) was refuted on the explicit premise "Tasks does NOT have search — it is a closed door", which was true then: `.dockField` was a disabled BUTTON carrying `title="Search comes with the other views."` That premise is now false. The ground moved and the denial did not move with it. Severity confirmed at **misleading**, not blocking: Tasks prints no keycap, so nothing the product displays fails to work — but it asserts, in a live region, that search does not exist, over a control the product itself names "Search tasks", to a suite user who learned the chord one product away in Notes where it IS printed on a keycap.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED — one hard error, measured.

The guard is "where `.dockInput` exists". Existence is not the discriminator. At 390 `[data-app="tasks"] .dock` computes `display: none` (`src/shell.css:367-370` — "Tasks folds the dock into the capsule and carries the add verb there"), so the input is **still in the DOM** — I measured `document.querySelectorAll(".dockInput").length === 1`, `exists: true` — while `getClientRects().length === 0` and `offsetParent === null`. I ran the proposed body verbatim at 390: `focus()` is a no-op and `document.activeElement` stays `BODY`. So the fix at ≤720 would `preventDefault`, move nothing, and announce "Search tasks." — a false statement replacing a currently true one. Today's phone behaviour is honest and would be regressed.

The finding's own prose gets the intent right ("keep a door sentence only where the field genuinely is not rendered (≤720)") — the code it wrote does not implement its own prose.

WHAT THE FINDING MISSED, WHICH MAKES THE REPAIR SMALLER THAN IT THINKS. `.headSearch` (`src/tasks.js:792`) is a ghost button, `aria-label="Search"`, `notYet(SEARCH)` → `title="Search comes with the other views."`, tabIndex 0. I measured its visibility: **hidden at 1440, visible at 390** — the exact inverse of the dock field. The layout is already correct: the desk shows the working field, the phone shows the honest door. Only the keyboard handler is stale. And the words the finding asks for already exist as the `SEARCH` constant at `src/tasks.js:536` — "Search comes with the other views." — which is a *different* sentence from the one the handler says, so the corrected fix also closes r3's one surviving observation for free.

1. **The rail, which is the real risk and the one decision the founder has to make.** Tasks' `onKey` fires from the spine — I confirmed it: focus `.rail [data-rail="tasks"]`, press Ctrl+K, and `#say` already reads the denial. The problem is real, reproduces verbatim, and must NOT be discarded — but the proposed remedy is wrong on three counts and the artifact already contains the correct pattern forty lines of source away, which the seat did not look for. WHAT I CONFIRMED.
