All 13 are hidden.\n\nShow all work". The code is quoted correctly: src/tasks.js:193 is `: "Nothing on the board is" + scope + ".") +`, and line 191-194 are as the seat prints them. The reachability analysis is right and I checked it exhaustively: the bare-copula string requires `!adj && !cond` (lateOnly and todayOnly both off) AND empty `scope` (clientOnly null), so `filtering()` can only be true via `queryText`. The query-only no-match case is the sole route to it, and it is the commonest way to empty this board. Neither gate covers it — interaction-check.mjs has no assertion on `.emptyBoard`, the dock field or filterSentence(), so this is genuinely outside automation. Class is `defect`, not more: the sentence is unfinished, not untrue; "All 13 are hidden" is correct and the board still works. WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. (1) It prints the same verb twice on consecutive lines. tasks.js:941 renders `Nothing matches.` and tasks.css:1935 makes that `b` a block with `margin-bottom: 6px`, so filterSentence() lands directly under it. The fix would ship "Nothing matches. / No task matches "zzz". All 13 are hidden." — "matches" twice in eleven words, 6px apart. Notes solves this identical problem and deliberately switches verb across the two lines: notes.js:2553 titles it "Nothing matched" and notes.js:2563 bodies it `No note says “${esc(query)}”.` The seat's own product proves the fix's word choice wrong. (2) Straight quotes introduce a second quotation grammar into the suite. notes.js:2563 and 2598 use curly “ ” for exactly this construction; the fix's ASCII `"` would be the only straight pair in the copy. At the Stripe/Linear bar that is a typographic defect, and it is the one-fact-two-treatments class this panel has already closed repeatedly (three-eyebrows-for-one-role, done-is-the-name-of-a-lane, cancelled-moment-stated-four-ways). (3) The literal drops a guard the existing line carries. The fix hardcodes `'. All ' + all + ' are hidden.'`, discarding `(all === 1 ? "is" : "are")` from line 194. A copy fix that regresses agreement is not the fix. (4) The fix is narrower than the seat's own complaint. Its guard — "when queryText.trim() is the only live filter" — leaves query+overdue printing "No overdue task is on the board. All 13 are hidden." and query+client printing "Nothing on the board is for Mara & Finn.", both of which still never name the query. That is the second half of the seat's stated problem ("never names the thing doing the hiding") and the fix does not touch it. (5) It stops one step short of the law this artifact wrote for itself. notes.js:2600 states it in the spec sheet on screen: "A search with no hits offers the nearest thing it does have. A dead end is a defect." Notes' no-hit state offers a nearest note and two moves. Tasks' offers one button. Naming the query is necessary but is not the whole gap.

standing.element: Filter menu "By tag" group (src/tasks.js filter toolPop) and the " for " scope clause in filterSentence()
standing.problem: The filter flattens a couple and a category into one thing, and the board's own drawing keeps them apart. On the card, Mara & Finn is `button.who` — sentence case, weight 600, underlined, title "Show only Mara & Finn" — and Venue, Enquiry, Bar are `span.tag` in uppercase mono. The Filter menu puts all four under one heading, "By tag", so the couple whose wedding the board exists for is filed as a tag. The single "for X" clause then runs the other way: pressing Venue announces and prints "Showing 4 tasks for Venue. 9 others are hidden." — a preposition written for a person applied to a category, so Venue reads as somebody being worked for. The code's own variable is called `clientOnly`, so the distinction exists everywhere except in the two places the person reads.

It is the one place the product's vocabulary stops matching the thing in front of her, and it makes a person-shaped fact and a category-shaped fact indistinguishable in the only menu that sorts by them.
standing.fix:
Split the group in the filter toolPop: keep `

By tag

` above Venue, Enquiry and Bar, and add `

By couple

` above the entries whose values appear on cards as .who. In filterSentence(), use " for " only when the filter value is one of those .who names and " tagged " otherwise, so Venue reads "Showing 4 tasks tagged Venue."
standing.assertion: At 1440, open Filter and assert Mara & Finn does not sit under the "By tag" heading; press Venue and assert the board sentence contains "tagged Venue" and not "for Venue".
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, every observation reproduces verbatim, and it must NOT be discarded. The remedy's second half introduces a garden-path sentence that is two clicks from the opening board, which at this bar is a regression, so the finding is refuted and the corrected fix is below.

DRIVEN, chromium 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`. Every claim checks out, and the seat actually understated its own case:

1. Filter pop innerText, verbatim: `"FILTER / Overdue / Past its day / Due today / Owed before tonight / BY TAG / Mara & Finn / Venue / Enquiry / Bar"`. Four entries, one heading. Confirmed.
2. Pressing Venue, live region and the strip both read, verbatim: `"Showing 4 tasks for Venue. 9 others are hidden."` Confirmed on both surfaces.
3. The board really does draw them apart, and not by accident. `src/tasks.js:91` holds `const CLIENTS = new Set(["Mara & Finn", "Nora & Cian", "Aisling & Tom"])`; line 342 branches on `CLIENTS.has(task.tag)` to emit `button.who` or `span.tag`. `tasks.css:835` gives `.who` 12px/600/`--ink-1` with `text-decoration: underline dotted` at rest (`:843`); `:829` gives `.tag` 11px mono 400 uppercase `--ink-3`. The comment above line 341 states the intent outright: "Which couple a task belongs to is the question a venue asks on a Saturday. Which area of the house it touches is background." So this is a shipped, deliberate distinction that the Filter menu simply never received — internal inconsistency, not taste.
4. The seat says "the two places the person reads". It is three. `src/tasks.js:1196` prints `fact("Tag", task.tag)` in the open-card detail panel, so the couple is labelled "Tag" there too. The fix as scoped leaves that one standing.
5. Not a gate restatement: `interaction-check.mjs` asserts nothing on this sentence or this menu (grepped, no hits).

SEVERITY. The seat named no class; I put it at **defect**. The counts are correct and every filter does what it says, so it is not blocking; "tag" is the literal field name, so nothing untrue is asserted and it is not misleading. It is a copy and grouping defect that the board's own ink contradicts — visibly wrong, passable.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. Half (a), splitting the group, is right and `CLIENTS` is the exact test for it — but it is silent on ordering, and `allTags()` returns first-encounter order, which on this board is `[Mara & Finn, Venue, Enquiry, Bar]`, i.e. the couple comes FIRST. "Keep By tag above Venue, Enquiry and Bar, and add By couple above the .who entries" cannot be done without partitioning and reordering the list, which the fix does not say.

Half (b) is wrong where it lands. `scope` is appended at the END of the sentence, after the noun, and there are two other branches at `src/tasks.js:186-193` besides the "Showing" one. Swapping " for " to " tagged " in that trailing slot produces, in the empty branch, `"No overdue task is on the board tagged Enquiry. All 13 are hidden."` — the participle attaches to "board", not to "task". That is reachable in two clicks: I drove Overdue + Enquiry on the opening fixture and got the live string `"No overdue task is on the board for Enquiry. All 13 are hidden."` today. " for " has the seat's problem; " tagged " in that same slot has a worse one. The fix is right in exactly one of the three branches.

By couple

' + couples.map(row…)` followed by `'

By tag

' + areas.map(row…)`, each heading guarded by its own group being non-empty (a board with no couples, or none but couples, must not print a bare heading). Couples first, matching the card's own rank. Keep all entries in one `role="menuitemradio"` set — it is still one selection, `clientOnly`, and turning it into two radio groups would lie about that. (2) `filterSentence()`, `src/tasks.js:179-193`. Do not swap the preposition in the trailing slot. standing.element: Tasks · Ctrl/⌘K, .dockInput, .headSearch
standing.problem: Driven at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 768 on ?state=tasks.board: .dockInput is a live <input type="search" aria-label="Search tasks">, visible and tabbable, and typing "marquee" filters the board from 13 cards to 2 with a strip reading "Showing 2 tasks. 11 others are hidden." At every one of those widths Ctrl+K announces "Search arrives with the other views." — the honest-door sentence for a feature that does not exist (src/tasks.js:2294). The head magnifier carries a third string, "Search comes with the other views." (SEARCH, src/tasks.js:536), though that one is only visible at ≤720 where .dockInput is genuinely hidden, so the phone is honest and the desk is not. The r3 refutation of `search-door-answered-three-ways` turned on the premise "Notes HAS search — a real, working overlay. Tasks does NOT — it is a closed door." That premise is now false: the source comment above .dockInput reads "A real field, not a door… It expands on focus, filters as you type." The field was built and the two closed-door sentences were never retired — lessons L-03, a fix manufacturing a defect elsewhere.
standing.consequence: Ctrl+K is the chord this suite itself teaches — it opens Notes' search overlay one rail-tile away. Orla presses it in Tasks and the product tells her, in its own live region, that search is not built yet, while search is running two inches below her hands. She stops looking for it. An honest-door programme that says "not here yet" about a feature that is here spends the credibility of every other not-here-yet sentence in the app.
standing.fix: In src/tasks.js:2288–2295, replace the say() branch with the real thing: when .dockInput is visible (>720), preventDefault, focus .dockInput, select its contents, and say("Search tasks."); when it is not visible (≤720), keep the existing not-yet sentence and make it the SAME string the head magnifier uses, so one door has one sentence. Delete the second wording so "arrives with the other views" and "comes with the other views" are not both in the product.
standing.assertion: On tasks.board at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, pressing Ctrl+K moves document.activeElement to .dockInput and no live region contains the substring "with the other views"; at 390, Ctrl+K and .headSearch produce the same single not-yet sentence and .dockInput is not visible.
standing.verdict: REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, every observation reproduces exactly, and it must NOT be discarded. It is misleading-class and it is not a re-file: the premise really did change under the round-3 refutation. WHAT I DROVE (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, at 1920x1000 / 1440x960 / 1280x900 / 768x1024 / 720x900 / 390x844): - 1920, 1440, 1280, 768: `.dockInput` is ``, 144x38, `offsetParent` non-null, `tabIndex 0`. Typing "marquee" takes the board from 13 `.card[data-id]` to 2 and the strip reads exactly "Showing 2 tasks. 11 others are hidden." Verbatim correct. - At all four of those widths Ctrl+K puts "Search arrives with the other views." in the live region (`src/tasks.js:2294`). Verbatim correct. - 720 and 390: `[data-app="tasks"] .dock` computes `display:none`, `.dockInput` is 0x0 with `offsetParent` null, and `.headSearch` becomes 37x34 (`src/tasks.css:365` + `:2016`) carrying `aria-disabled="true" title="Search comes with the other views."` (SEARCH, `src/tasks.js:536`). Verbatim correct. - Line cite is accurate: the branch is `src/tasks.js:2290–2296` with the `say()` at 2294, inside a handler gated on `window.__SUITE.active("tasks")` (`src/tasks.js:3665`), so there is no collision with Notes' real Ctrl+K overlay (`src/notes.js:3524`). THE PREMISE REVERSAL IS DOCUMENTED, NOT ASSERTED. `panel/round-3.json` records the refuted finding's driven DOM as `` — a closed door. It is now an input, and `src/tasks.js:955` says why in its own comment: "A real field, not a door. It was the one control at the foot of the sheet that looked like an input and refused to be one." The r3 refutation's "WHAT SURVIVES" paragraph is explicit that the copy mismatch was only refinement because "both sentences are honest… nothing is asserted untruly to anyone." That sentence is what died. At every desk width the product now denies, by keyboard, a feature that is on screen and working two inches below the cards — and it says it from the spine too (measured: `.rail [data-rail="tasks"]` focused, Ctrl+K, live region "Search arrives with the other views."). Misleading is the right class. WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. 1. Half B is factually wrong and would spread the lie rather than retire it. "Keep the existing not-yet sentence at ≤720 and make it the SAME string the head magnifier uses" standardises on "Search comes with the other views." — a sentence that is now false in its own right. "The other views" is this board's fixed idiom for the unbuilt view switcher (`SOON` = "Board is the only view for now.", `TOOLS` = "Filter, Sort and Display come with the other views."), so it tells a phone user the feature is unbuilt. It is built. It is withheld at ≤720 because the dock is `display:none`, which is a width fact, not a roadmap fact. The finding's own load-bearing claim that "the phone is honest and the desk is not" is therefore wrong, and its fix would copy the false string to a second site — the exact class it is prosecuting. 2. It hands the keyboard into a room whose only exit is ``. Measured at 1440: focus `.dockInput`, press Escape on an empty field, `document.activeElement` is BODY (the `search.blur()` branch, `src/tasks.js:3579`); with text it takes two presses and still lands on BODY. Today almost nobody arrives there by keyboard; the fix makes the chord the front door, so shipping it as written re-opens `undo-drops-focus-to-body (r1)` / `undo-drops-focus-on-body (r1)` at a new site. 3. It leaves the one context where the key is already silent. Measured: with a draft composer open, Ctrl+K does nothing at all — no announcement, focus stays on `.cardTitle` — because the draft branch returns at `src/tasks.js:2286` before the board-wide keys. 1. `src/tasks.js:2290–2296` — replace the `say()` with the real thing, gated on the field actually being on screen rather than on a width number: `const f = document.querySelector(".dockInput"); if (f && f.offsetParent !== null) { event.preventDefault(); f.focus(); f.select(); say("Search tasks. Type to filter the board."); return; }`. `offsetParent` tracks the same CSS that hides the dock (measured null at 720/390, non-null at 768/1280/1440/1920), so the branch can never drift from the breakpoint. Do not say bare "Search tasks." — that is verbatim the input's `aria-label`, so a reader hears it twice.

2. Return the keyboard where it came from. Record the element focused when Ctrl+K fired and restore it on the empty-field Escape branch (`src/tasks.js:3576–3580`) instead of `search.blur()`, falling back to the first card — the same treatment `task-close` and `search-clear` already give (`src/tasks.js:2643`, `:2651`).

standing.element: Tasks · .trayAdd draft commit, the undo strip, Ctrl/⌘Z
standing.problem: Driven at 1440. Focus .trayAdd, Enter, type "Confirm the cake delivery window", Enter. The polite region reads "Confirm the cake delivery window added to the to do column. Press Ctrl Z to undo." and the visible strip reads "Cake delivery window added to To do — Undo · Ctrl Z". Commit leaves focus in the next empty draft (p.cardTitle inside .card[data-draft]) for rapid entry, which is right. Pressing Ctrl+Z there does nothing: the To do lane still holds ["Confirm marquee sides…","Reprint the faded…","Send midweek rate…","Confirm the cake delivery window",""], and the polite region does not change — not even to "Nothing left to undo." Press Escape first ("Discarded.") and the same Ctrl+Z works immediately: "Confirm the cake delivery window removed again." Cause: onKey returns early for every key inside .card[data-draft] .cardTitle (src/tasks.js ~2280) before the board-wide Ctrl+Z branch below it can run. Notes proves this is not a platform constraint — Ctrl+Z inside .topField undoes a save and says "Put back. Your note is in the field again."
standing.consequence: The one moment the product prints the undo chord in two places at once is the one moment the chord is dead. Orla mistypes a task, presses Ctrl Z exactly as instructed, watches nothing happen, and now believes undo does not work in Tasks — so she stops reaching for it on the ticks, drags and carries where it does work. A reversibility surface is worth nothing once a person has seen it lie once.
standing.fix: In src/tasks.js, inside the `if (field)` early-return block that owns the draft field, add before the return: `if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && (key === "z" || key === "Z")) { event.preventDefault(); if (!draftText.trim()) discardDraft(); undoLast(); return; }` — so an empty rapid-entry draft is dropped and the last committed action is reversed. A draft with typed text keeps native text undo.
standing.assertion: On tasks.board, after committing a new task with Enter (focus left in the next draft), pressing Ctrl+Z removes the just-added task from the To do lane and the polite region reads "<title> removed again."
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces verbatim, and must NOT be discarded. Ship the corrected remedy in sharpenedFix instead.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, 1440x960, file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board). Focus the first `.trayAdd`, Enter, type "Confirm the cake delivery window", Enter. The polite `.sr` region reads exactly "Confirm the cake delivery window added to the to do column. Press Ctrl Z to undo." and the strip reads "Undo · Ctrl Z". Focus lands in `.card[data-draft] .cardTitle` (activeElement `cardTitle`, aria-label "What has to happen?"). Ctrl+Z there: the board still holds `new-1` "Confirm the cake delivery window", the polite region text is byte-identical to before the press — not even "Nothing left to undo." Escape → "Discarded.", focus to `.trayAdd`; Ctrl+Z now → "Confirm the cake delivery window removed again." and `new-1` is gone. The seat's cause is exact: `src/tasks.js:2282-2287`, the `if (field)` block answers only Enter and Escape and then `return`s, above the board-wide Ctrl+Z branch at 2297. The Notes counter-example is also exact and stronger than the seat states — `src/notes.js:3481-3491` does not merely handle Ctrl+Z in a field, it implements precisely the empty-vs-typed split this finding wants: `if (typing && e.target.closest(".topField, .phoneField") && draft.length) return;` then `doUndo()`. Notes therefore proves both that this is not a platform constraint and that the split is the house rule. The gate asserts nothing about the draft field (`interaction-check.mjs` mentions undo only in a comment), so this is not a restatement. Severity is blocking on the stated definition: the product speaks an instruction into the live region and prints it on the strip, and the key is dead at the one focus location the product itself chose.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED.

1. The code contradicts its own prose, destructively. The note says "A draft with typed text keeps native text undo." The snippet does the opposite: `event.preventDefault()` is unconditional and `undoLast()` is unconditional — only `discardDraft()` sits behind the `!draftText.trim()` guard. So a person mid-sentence in the composer who presses Ctrl+Z to take back a typo gets no character back (native undo is preventDefault'd away) and instead has the previously committed card silently spliced off the board, with "… removed again." spoken over them. I measured today's behaviour for that exact case: type "Chase the florist" into the fresh draft, Ctrl+Z → the field returns to empty, the board is untouched, nothing is announced. The fix replaces a harmless browser-owned undo with undo destroying a committed task while somebody is typing — the failure Notes wrote a five-line comment about and guarded against. That alone is fatal.

2. It regresses the empty-history case. Empty draft, nothing on `undoHistory`: the fix calls `discardDraft()` (which closes the composer, says "Discarded.", mounts and runs `leaveDraft()` to `.trayAdd`) and then `undoLast()` says "Nothing left to undo." So a keystroke that undoes nothing tears down the open composer and moves focus out of it. Ctrl+Z must never be the key that closes your composer.

3. Two `say()` calls and two `mount()`s for one keystroke. `discardDraft()` speaks "Discarded." into the same polite `.sr` node that `runUndo` then overwrites with "… removed again." in the same tick, so the first sentence is clobbered before any AT reads it — and "Discarded." is the wrong receipt anyway, since the branch is defined by the draft being empty and the same word is Escape's receipt for deliberately abandoning typed words.

The numbers and file references in the observation are right; `draftText` is genuinely live (`src/tasks.js:3500-3502` sets it on `input`, and `commitDraft` zeroes it at 2228 before opening the next composer), so the guard variable choice is sound even though the branch built on it is not.
standing.breaks:
Plausible breakage and what to re-measure after it lands:

1. Typed-text undo in the composer. Type into `.card[data-draft] .cardTitle`, press Ctrl/⌘Z: a character or the last input batch must come back, the polite region must not change, and no card may leave any lane. Today one press clears the whole typed string (one input batch = one native undo entry) — that behaviour must be unchanged, since the sharpened fix returns before `preventDefault`.

2. Focus after undo-from-draft. `document.activeElement` must be `.card[data-draft] .cardTitle`, never `<body>` and never a detached node. This is the twice-closed class (r1 `undo-drops-focus-on-body`, r1 `undo-drops-focus-to-body`), and `runUndo`'s `add` branch does not set `focusId`, so this is the single most likely regression.

3. The blur-to-nothing commit path, `src/tasks.js:3646-3661`. `undoLast()`'s `mount()` detaches the focused field, which fires `focusout` with a null `relatedTarget`. The `!field.isConnected` guard should swallow it, but a double-add is exactly what that guard exists to prevent — re-drive Ctrl+Z-in-draft and assert the lane count drops by exactly one and no duplicate title appears.

4. Undo under the overdue filter and inside the planning drawer. `commitDraft` has a branch that turns `lateOnly` off on add (2242-2245); undoing that add from the draft field must not leave the filter chip and the board disagreeing, and `leaveDraft`'s collapsed-column fallback (2202-2207) must still find a visible `.trayAdd` when the lane empties.

5. Touch build. At ≤720 the draft renders Add/Discard buttons instead of the "Enter adds it. Esc discards it." hint; re-drive at 390x844 to confirm the new branch does not intercept anything the on-screen buttons own, and that the undo strip at that width still reads whole.

6. Re-run both gates: `audit.mjs --lab=...` (should be untouched — no visual change) and `interaction-check.mjs` (green today, and worth growing an assertion here: commit from `.trayAdd`, Ctrl+Z in the fresh draft, assert the card is gone, the region says "… removed again.", and activeElement is still the draft field).

standing.element: Tasks · .dockInput input handler
standing.problem: Driven at 1440. Typing into .dockInput steps the board 13 → 11 → 9 → 8 → 2 → 0 cards, and the polite live region emits nothing at any step; at zero results it still emits nothing. The visible strip does update ("Showing 8 tasks. 5 others are hidden."), so a sighted user is served and a screen-reader user is not. Every other filter in the same product does announce through say(): the overdue chip gives "Showing 1 overdue task. 12 others are hidden.", the who chip gives "Showing 7 tasks for Mara & Finn. 6 others are hidden." The search path (src/tasks.js:3503–3517) calls mount() and restores the caret but never calls say(). Notes' search, in the same application, announces the count, the matched excerpt and the near-miss. Neither the strip nor any announcement ever repeats the query text back.
standing.consequence: The one control that can empty the entire board is the one control that never says what it did. A screen-reader user types four letters, eleven of thirteen cards disappear, and the product is silent — the dead-end filter the paid-for library names by name. Inside one suite, the same gesture is exemplary in Notes and mute in Tasks, so the person cannot form one expectation of what searching feels like here.
standing.fix: In the .dockInput input handler in src/tasks.js, after mount() and the caret restore, call say(filterSentence()) debounced ~300ms so keystrokes do not stack, and include the query in the sentence — extend filterSentence() to append `for “<queryText>”` when queryText is set, matching the `scope` clause it already builds for clientOnly.
standing.assertion: On tasks.board, typing "marquee" into .dockInput leaves the polite live region reading a sentence containing both "2" and "marquee"; clearing the field leaves it reading "Showing all work."
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, reproduces exactly, and must NOT be discarded. Do not drop the observation; drop the remedy as written.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, 1440x960, _gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board, a MutationObserver on #say installed before the first keystroke):
- Typing "confirm marquee" one character at a time steps the board 13 → 12 → 6 → 3 → 2 → 1 cards. The MutationObserver log is `[]` at every step and #say.textContent is `""` after a 1.2s settle. The seat's exact card sequence (13→11→9→8→2→0) is query-dependent and it never names its query, but the mechanism is verbatim right.
- At zero results ("zzzz"): 0 cards, the centred block reads "Nothing matches. Nothing on the board is. All 13 are hidden." and the live-region log is still `[]`. Silent at the one moment silence costs most.
- The peer controls do announce, exactly as claimed. Pressing the who chip logged "Showing 7 tasks for Mara & Finn. 6 others are hidden."; Escape in the field logged "Search cleared." So the search path is the one filter in Tasks that is mute.
- The code is as described: src/tasks.js:3500–3517 sets `queryText`, calls `mount()`, restores the caret, and never calls `say()`. Notes does the opposite in the same application — src/notes.js:2997–3011 clears `searchSaid` and speaks the head count, the cursor row and the no-hit panel's title/body/moves on a 350ms debounce.
- `filtering()` (src/tasks.js:167) does include `queryText`, so the drawn strip at src/tasks.js:1073 does update while the ear gets nothing. The asymmetry is exactly as stated.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. Half of it is right; the half that touches `filterSentence()` is wrong, and it is wrong in drawn copy, not only spoken copy.

1. It collides with the very clause it cites. `filterSentence()` already builds `scope = " for " + clientOnly`. Appending `for “<queryText>”` stacks a second identical preposition: with the who chip on and "cake" typed you get "Showing 3 tasks for Mara & Finn for “cake”. 10 others are hidden." I confirmed both filters compose (who chip + "cake" → 0 cards, both live, `Filter2` on the button face), so this is reachable by the ordinary route, not a corner.

2. It edits two pieces of visible copy the finding does not mention. `filterSentence()` is not a spoken string — it is rendered into the `.carry` strip (src/tasks.js:1073) and into the "Nothing matches." block (src/tasks.js:942). Measured at 768: with the appended query the pill grows 442 → 632px and `.carryName` clips (scrollWidth 568 vs width 502, `white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis`) — the ellipsis eats the tail, so the drawn strip loses "…10 others are hidden." in order to echo the query. The fix trades a spoken count for a drawn one. At 1440 it grows to 698px unclipped, so the two widths disagree about what the strip says.

3. On the empty branch the naive append makes an already-broken sentence worse rather than repairing it. The branch is `"Nothing on the board is" + scope + "."`, which with a query alone already prints the complementless "Nothing on the board is." Appending `for “cake”` gives "Nothing on the board is for “cake”." and, with the chip, "Nothing on the board is for Mara & Finn for “cake”." The query needs its own grammatical slot, not the tail of a sentence that has no complement.

4. It leaves the debounce timer unfenced. `search-clear` (src/tasks.js:2646–2652) and Escape (src/tasks.js:3563–3575) both say "Search cleared." — a keystroke's pending 300ms timer lands after that and speaks a second, contradicting sentence.

SEVERITY: I am raising it, not lowering it. This is blocking, not a defect. The field's accessible name is "Search tasks" and it filters as you type; for a person working by ear the control produces no perceivable result at any keystroke, including the one that empties the board. Every sibling filter in the same head answers. That is the control failing to do what it says for that user, and it is the last round.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Keep the first half, replace the second.

(a) ANNOUNCE. In the `.dockInput` branch of the delegated `input` listener (src/tasks.js:3502–3516), after `mount()` and the caret restore, add a module-level `let searchSaid = null;` beside `queryText` (src/tasks.js:71) and do `clearTimeout(searchSaid); searchSaid = setTimeout(() => say(filterSentence()), 300);`. Add `clearTimeout(searchSaid)` to the `search-clear` branch (src/tasks.js:2646) and to the Escape branch (src/tasks.js:3567) so a pending sentence can never land on top of "Search cleared."

REFUTED ON THE FIX, THE COMPARATOR AND THE CLASS — but two-thirds of the observation is real and must NOT be discarded.

DRIVEN, chromium 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`. The repro reproduces verbatim. Real click on `.b-grab`, append " TWO" to `#b-edit-title`, Tab to commit, real click on `.b-step[data-delta="1"]` (aria-label "Move a day later"):
- after rename — strip: "Renamed to Menu tasting at The Orchard TWO. Undo Ctrl Z"; row data-date 2026-08-01, away=16
- after +1 — strip: "Menu tasting at The Orchard TWO moved 1 day later. Undo Ctrl Z"; row 2026-08-02, away=17
- after Ctrl+Z — row 2026-08-01, `.b-stepRead` "Saturday 1 August 2026 / in 16 days", strip: "Renamed to Menu tasting at The Orchard TWO. Undo Ctrl Z"
- after 2nd Ctrl+Z — title back to "Menu tasting at The Orchard", strip data-empty="true", text ""
- after 3rd Ctrl+Z — nothing changes, nothing said; `.b-live` is "" for the whole session.
(Note for the record: Ctrl+Z is deliberately ignored while focus is in an INPUT/TEXTAREA — src/timeline.js:2049 — so the repro only works if the stepper is clicked, not scripted.)

So: no depth marker, real. Silent exhausted stack, real. What is refuted is the diagnosis, the comparator, the fix, and the class.

1. THE COMPARATOR IS FALSE, AND IT IS THE FINDING'S ONLY ARGUMENT. I drove Tasks the same way (tick two cards, then Ctrl+Z): tick1 → "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company done Undo Ctrl Z"; tick2 → "…walk-in couple done Undo 1 more Ctrl Z"; after one Ctrl+Z → "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company done Undo Ctrl Z". Tasks prints the identical past-tense receipt for a tick that did not just happen (src/tasks.js:2069 sets `undone = undoHistory[undoHistory.length-1]` on undo, and every `what` string at 1044–1054 is past tense). Tasks does NOT distinguish an offer from a receipt. It adds a count and nothing else. The finding cites Tasks as having solved the register problem; it has not. The offer/receipt split is a new invention being imported under a false flag of consistency.

2. THE STRIP ASSERTS NOTHING UNTRUE, so "misleading" is one class too high. "Renamed to Menu tasting at The Orchard TWO." is true at the frame it is shown: the moment IS so named, and that rename is the standing top of the stack the button will reverse. The source's own contract says so — "silent until it has something true to say, and every entry carries the closure that reverses it" (src/timeline.js:1207). Timeline's bar is also permanent, unlike Tasks' 6-second transient, which makes the standing-offer reading stronger here, not weaker. Class is defect.

3. THE FIX DOES NOT FIX THE ONE THING THAT ACTUALLY HARMS. `.b-undo` is `role="status"` (src/timeline.js:1226) and is the only feedback undo produces — `undo()` at 1287–1320 speaks nothing, and `.b-live` stayed empty across every press. A screen-reader owner presses Ctrl+Z on a date move and hears a sentence about a rename; they are never told the moment went back to Saturday 1 August. Rewriting that sentence as "Undo: renamed to X" still never announces the reversal. The diagnosed harm survives the fix intact.

4. THE FIX MANUFACTURES THE DEFECT CLASS THIS ENGAGEMENT KEEPS CLOSING. Ship it and the suite's one shared undo strip speaks two grammars: Tasks "…done", Timeline "Undo: renamed to…". That is one-move-two-verbs / three-unavailability-grammars again, self-inflicted. And "Undo: renamed to X" sits beside a button labelled Undo and a keycap Ctrl Z — the word Undo three times in a three-element strip. Worse copy.

5. Minor: paintUndo is 1234–1263, not 1235–1250.

standing.element: Notes capture field and index rover across the 720px layout boundary — src/notes.js:187 (`PHONE_AT = 720`), the ResizeObserver at :3857 and the resize listener at :3868, against `paint()` at :2754
standing.problem: Both breakpoint handlers call `paint()` with `refocus` unset. `paint()` captures the index scroll, the read-body scroll and the caret, but restores focus for anything that is not a TEXTAREA/INPUT only when `refocus` is set, and restores the caret only by re-finding the field through `caret.sel` — the active element's first class name. Across 720 that class name changes (`.topField` at ≥721 becomes `.phoneField` at ≤720), so the selector matches nothing and focus lands on `<body>`. Driven, chromium: at 768 with `.idxRow` focused, stepping the viewport 760→740→730→725→721 keeps focus; 720 drops it to BODY, and it drops again going back up from 700 to 1440. Tasks (`.card`) and Timeline (`.b-grab`) both survive the identical crossing, so this is Notes alone. Reproduced on a real touch context: viewport 844x390 isMobile+hasTouch, typed "Ask the marquee company about the side pan" into `.topField`, rotated to 390x844 — activeElement becomes BODY, `.phoneField` still holds the text, and the next nine characters typed ("els today") are discarded; `p.sr` says nothing. notes.js line 6 states the contract this breaks in its own words: "same caret — because a capture product that loses your place is a capture product that has failed", and `paint()`'s header comment says "Nothing here may cost the operator their place." Both are false across this boundary.
standing.consequence: Orla turns her phone from landscape to portrait mid-note. The words already typed survive, but the caret is gone, nothing on screen or in the live region says so, and every further character she types is silently thrown away until she notices the text has stopped growing and taps the field again. Silent destruction of typed input in the one product whose entire premise is capture.
standing.fix: In both breakpoint handlers, before calling `paint()`, set `refocus` from the current active element: if it is `.topField`/`.phoneField`, `refocus = { kind: "field", sel: next ? ".phoneField" : ".topField", end: true }`; if it is an `.idxRow`, `refocus = { kind: "row", id: active.dataset.id }`; otherwise `refocus = { kind: "act", sel: "." + active.classList[0] }`. Separately, make `paint()`'s caret fallback survive a renamed field: capture `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` before the repaint and, when `refocus.kind === "field"`, re-apply those offsets to the field found by the new selector instead of dropping them.
standing.assertion: In a touch context at 844x390, focus the capture field, type 43 characters, resize to 390x844, and assert (a) `document.activeElement` is the capture field, (b) its `selectionStart` equals the pre-resize offset, and (c) three further keystrokes appear in its `value`. Assert the same for 390x844 → 844x390, and for `.idxRow` focus stepped across 721→720 and 720→721 at both orientations.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, reproduces verbatim on every claim, and must NOT be discarded — it is blocking and it is a paid-for class creeping back (lessons.md:238, "Repaints that annihilate place ... the exact element that held focus"). Wire the sharpened fix, not this one.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`)
1. Index rover, 768x1024, `.idxRow` focused, stepping the viewport: 760/740/730/725/721 all report activeElement `BUTTON.idxRow`; at 720 it is `BODY` (`.topField` gone, `.phoneField` present); 700 still BODY; back up to 1440 still BODY. Exactly as stated.
2. Touch repro, 844x390 isMobile+hasTouch: typed "Ask the marquee company about the side pan" into `.topField` (selectionStart 42), rotated to 390x844 — activeElement BODY, `.phoneField` holds the 41 characters, the next nine ("els today") land nowhere, `.phoneField` still reads "...side pan", and the live region text is unchanged. Silent loss of typed words in a capture product whose own line 6 says the opposite.
3. Notes alone: `.card` (tasks.board) and `.b-grab` (timeline.owner-flight) hold focus through 721→720→700→1440.
4. Mechanism is as described: `paint()` (notes.js:2765) captures `sel = active.id ? "#id" : "." + active.classList[0]`; neither textarea carries an id (:1652, :1768), so the desk caret is stored as `.topField` and re-found after a repaint that only rendered `.phoneField`. Non-text elements get no capture at all unless `refocus` is set, and neither breakpoint handler (:3861 ResizeObserver, :3869 resize) sets it. Not covered by interaction-check.mjs — no resize assertion exists there.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG
(a) The catch-all `refocus = { kind: "act", sel: "." + active.classList[0] }` is the exact anti-pattern `paint()` already documents as a bug it paid for once, and it fails two ways at this boundary. I enumerated every focusable in the Notes mount at 768 and at 700 and resolved each desk class against the phone tree: `.act` (Save it), `.filingBtn`, `.verb` (Dictate, Read a photo) and `.dockField` (Search) all resolve to NULL — five of thirteen desk controls still drop to BODY, so the fix leaves most of the room broken while claiming the room. Worse, first-class-name silently mis-targets where it does resolve: `.dockGlyph[data-act="voice"]` → `.dockGlyph[data-act="search"]`, `.headAct[data-act="options"]` → `.headAct[data-act="privacy"]`, `.groupBtn[data-act="group-day"]` → `group-about`. Focus the microphone, rotate, press Enter, and search opens. Landing on a different control is worse than landing on body, and it is the failure mode this programme has already bought.
(b) The two halves contradict each other. Part A sets `end: true`; part B asks for `selectionStart/End` to be re-applied. In the existing branch (:2919) `if (refocus.end && field.setSelectionRange) setSelectionRange(value.length, value.length)` runs unconditionally, so part B is dead on arrival and a caret parked mid-note is still thrown to the end. The seat's repro never saw it because its caret was already at 42 of 42.
(c) One risk it does NOT carry, in its favour: an inactive product's mount is `display:none` + `hidden` + `inert`, so a Notes repaint firing while the operator is on Tasks cannot steal focus out of Tasks. That half of the objection does not apply.

SEVERITY: blocking, and correctly so — typed characters are destroyed with no announcement.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Fix it once, generically, inside `paint()` — not in two hand-written breakpoint branches — so every control in the room survives the crossing rather than the two the seat happened to test.

1. Widen the caret capture to the pair selector the file already uses elsewhere (:3518, :3894). In `paint()`, when the active element is the capture field, store `sel: ".topField, .phoneField"` instead of `"." + classList[0]`, and keep `start`/`end` as it already does. The existing fallback branch then re-finds the field under either name and re-applies the real offsets. That alone closes the rotation-loses-your-words case with no new state and no `refocus` plumbing.
2. For everything else, capture a stable identity rather than a class. Every focusable in the Notes mount carries one: `.idxRow` has `data-id`, and all thirteen other controls carry `data-act` — including the two that rename across the boundary (`[data-act="keep"]` is `.act` at desk and `.dockGlyph` at phone; `[data-act="search"]` is `.dockField` at desk and `.dockGlyph` at phone). So in `paint()`, before the `innerHTML` write, if `refocus` is unset and the active element is inside `mount`, synthesise one: a `[data-id]` row → `{ kind: "row", id }`; otherwise `{ kind: "act", act }` from `data-act`. Restore with `mount.querySelector('.' + cls + '[data-act="' + act + '"]') || mount.querySelector('[data-act="' + act + '"]')` so the class is a preference and never a requirement — that keeps `.verb[data-act="voice"]` on the verb going phone→desk while still finding the dock glyph when the verb is gone.
3. Drop `end: true` from the field path when captured offsets exist, or gate it (`if (refocus.end && refocus.start == null)`), so the two halves stop contradicting each other.
4. Say it. This repaint currently announces nothing; if the crossing genuinely cannot restore a control (a control that exists at one width only), `say()` where the keyboard has landed rather than leaving a person on `<body>` in silence.
Then delete the need for the breakpoint handlers to know anything: they keep calling bare `paint()`, and `paint()` keeps its own promise.

standing.element: Tasks sheet head at ≤720 — `button.ghost` aria-label "Search", `aria-disabled="true"`, `title="Search comes with the other views."`
standing.problem: Driven across the declared widths: at 390 and 720 Tasks' search is a closed door whose sentence — spoken to `p.sr` on Enter and shown as a tooltip — is "Search comes with the other views." At 721, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920 the same product renders a live `input.dockInput` that filters the whole board (typing "linen" collapses it to one card and prints "Showing 1 task. 12 others are hidden. [Show all work]"). So search does not come with the other views; it is in this view, and simply is not built at this width. Worse, the three "other views" it names are themselves closed doors carrying "Board is the only view for now.", so the sentence routes Orla to three dead ends for a feature she already has. Notes answers the same question honestly on the same phone: its dock search is live at 390. This is a door sentence that is wrong, which the brief places explicitly in scope; it is not the r4 census finding, which was killed on method rather than on any width-dependent claim.
standing.consequence: On her phone Orla is told that searching her tasks is a feature of List, Schedule or Calendar. She stops looking for it, and the three places she is pointed at are all shut. The honest-doors doctrine is the founder's designed answer to an unfinished product; one door that states a falsehood about the product's own capability spends the credibility of all eleven of them.
standing.fix: Replace the title and the spoken sentence on that control with one that is true of the width and defers to nothing: "Search is on the wider screen for now." Leave the control focusable, `aria-disabled`, and announcing, as it is. Do not name List, Schedule or Calendar.
standing.assertion: At 390 and 720, the Tasks search control's `title` and the string written to `p.sr` on Enter both match "Search is on the wider screen for now." and contain none of "List", "Schedule", "Calendar" or "other views"; and for every closed door in the suite, assert no door's sentence names a capability that a control with the same accessible name performs at another declared viewport.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY — the problem is real, every observation reproduces verbatim, and it must NOT be discarded. The fix as written repairs one of the two sentences that say this and leaves the falser one running, at every width.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven, chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, at 390x844 (touch), 720, 721, 768, 1280, 1440, 1920.
- `.headSearch` is `display:flex` at 390 and 720, `display:none` from 721 up. `aria-label="Search"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `title="Search comes with the other views."`, `tabIndex 0`, at every width. Source: `master.html:10410` (const), `:10666` (the only use); mirror `src/tasks.js:536`. The ≤720 reveal is `master.html:2729` inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`; `.dock { display:none }` at `:2750`.
- Pressing it — force-click and Enter with focus on it — both put exactly `Search comes with the other views.` into `p.sr`. Confirmed both routes.
- `.dockInput` (`aria-label="Search tasks"`, `master.html:10831`) is hidden at 390/720 and live at 721/768/1280/1440/1920. Typing `linen` at 768 and at 1440 collapses the board to one card, "Chase linen order, now shipping Tuesday", and the strip reads `Showing 1 task. 12 others are hidden.` with a `.carryDo` "Show all work". Verbatim as filed.
- List, Schedule and Calendar are all `aria-disabled="true"` `title="Board is the only view for now."` at all seven widths. So the sentence does route to three shut doors.
- Notes at 390 does carry a live `.dockGlyph[aria-label="Search everything you wrote"]`; Ctrl+K there mounts `.searchTop`, focuses the input and says "Search everything you wrote." Confirmed.
So the sentence is false in the ordinary reading — search is in this view, at this state, and is simply not drawn at this width — and it is false in a way the operator can catch by opening the same board on a laptop. `misleading` is the right class; the seat did not overstate it.

NOT A RE-FILE. r3's `search-door-answered-three-ways` was refuted on the premise "Notes HAS search … Tasks does NOT — it is a closed door", and it prosecuted an `aria-label` on `.dockField` that never existed. That premise is now stale: `.dockField` has since been rebuilt into a real `input.dockInput` (its own comment at `master.html:10824` says "It was the one control at the foot of the sheet that looked like an input and refused to be one"). r4's `closed-doors-defer-to-closed-doors` was killed on a miscounted census and on register, not on width-dependent truth. This is a different claim about a surface that did not exist when those were adjudicated.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. `SEARCH` is not the only place Tasks answers this question. `master.html:12168` / `src/tasks.js:2294` binds board-wide Ctrl/⌘K to `say("Search arrives with the other views.")` — a second, differently-worded sentence, and it fires at EVERY width. Driven: at 390 it says it, at 768 it says it, at 1440 it says it, with the live `.dockInput` sitting in the dock two inches below. Land the fix as written and you get (a) a phone where the button says "Search is on the wider screen for now." and the chord says "Search arrives with the other views." — one door, two sentences, the exact class this codebase has already paid for three times — and (b) the false sentence still shipping at 1280/1440/1920, where it is not merely imprecise but flatly contradicted by a working search field on the same screen. Fixing the weaker half and leaving the stronger half is not an improvement at the declared bar.

One more thing the fix does not know: the Ctrl+K branch justifies itself with "The pill prints this key, so the key has to answer". Tasks prints no such key any more. I enumerated every `kbd` in the Tasks surface at 390, 768 and 1440 — the only Tasks keycaps are Ctrl ↓ and Ctrl Z; the "Ctrl K" caps I found belong to Notes' mounted-but-hidden dock. The comment is stale and so is the string it defends.

The copy itself I do not object to. "Search is on the wider screen for now." is true at 390/720, it defers to nothing, and its "… for now" cadence sits correctly beside "Board is the only view for now." on the same head. Keeping the control focusable, `aria-disabled` and announcing is right and matches `notYet()` at `master.html:10406`. The finding is refuted on completeness, not on wording.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Change both sentences in one edit, in `src/tasks.js` (then rebuild `master.html` / `console.html`; nothing in `interaction-check.mjs`, `gate.mjs`, `verify.mjs` or `gates/` asserts either string, so both gates stay green).

1. `src/tasks.js:536` — `const SEARCH = "Search is on the wider screen for now.";` Leave `notYet()` and the `.headSearch` markup exactly as they are: focusable, `aria-disabled="true"`, `aria-label="Search"`, sentence in `title` and spoken to `p.sr` on press. Do not name List, Schedule or Calendar. (This half is the seat's, unchanged.)

2. `src/tasks.js:2294` — stop the Ctrl/⌘K branch saying anything false. Make it width-aware against the same 720 boundary the CSS uses: if `document.querySelector(".dockInput")` is visible (≥721), `preventDefault()`, focus it, and let the field announce itself — no `say()` at all, because there is nothing to apologise for. If it is not visible (≤720), `say(SEARCH)` so the chord and the button in the head speak one sentence. Delete the stale comment above it ("The pill prints this key…") — Tasks prints no ⌘K keycap at any width.

RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS: (a) at 1280/1440/1920, Ctrl+K focuses `.dockInput` without scrolling the board or moving `.tray` scrollLeft, and does not steal the chord while a card is carried or the draft composer is open — the branch sits after the draft's Enter/Escape guard at `:12156`, keep it there; (b) at 390/720, force-click and keyboard-Enter on `.headSearch` and Ctrl+K all put the identical new string into `p.sr`; (c) re-run both gates; (d) grep for any surviving occurrence of "the other views" in Tasks — `TOOLS` at `master.html:10409` ("Filter, Sort and Display come with the other views.") is a separate door on `.viewTools`, which is `display:none` at ≤720, and it is not in this finding's scope, but confirm the edit did not touch it.
