standing.element: Tasks dock search — `[data-app="tasks"] .dockInput:focus { outline: none; }` at src/tasks.css:1259, against `[data-app="tasks"] .dockField:focus-within, [data-app="tasks"] .dockField.is-live { ... }` at src/tasks.css:1232-1233
standing.problem: The input's own ring is removed with the comment "The ring belongs to the pill, not to the input inside it", but the pill is never given one: `.dockField:focus-within` shares its entire declaration block with `.dockField.is-live`, so focus and "there is a query in the box" are drawn identically. Measured at 1440 (computed style, four states in sequence): at rest 196px wide, `rgba(17,17,17,0.04)` fill, `inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0)`; focused 392px, white, `inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(17,17,17,0.16)`; typed "linen" — identical; focus moved to `.dockPrimary` with the query still present — **byte-identical to the focused state**. The whole focus signal is therefore a 1px inset of `rgba(17,17,17,0.16)`, which composites to #d8d8d8 on the white pill and on the white dock behind it: **1.43:1**, against the 3:1 floor for a non-text indicator. Every other control in the suite gets `outline: 2px solid var(--indigo)` — I measured 55 of 56 focusable controls across tasks.board, notes.notebook, notes.seam and timeline.owner-flight at ratios of 3.00 to 18.88. This one is the only exception, and the panel already closed the same class once on the spine (`spine-focus-ring-below-non-text-contrast`, r3) — the dock search was not brought with it.
standing.consequence: A keyboard user who has typed a query, tabbed onto the board, and tabbed back has no way to see whether the search field holds focus: the field looks the same either way. On the one control that governs what the whole board shows, the person cannot tell where they are — and if they do notice a change, it is a grey hairline at an eighth of the contrast the rest of the product uses to say the same thing.
standing.fix: Split the shared block. Keep `width`, `padding`, `background` and `box-shadow` on `[data-app="tasks"] .dockField:focus-within, [data-app="tasks"] .dockField.is-live`, and add a focus-only rule after it: `[data-app="tasks"] .dockField:focus-within { outline: 2px solid var(--indigo); outline-offset: 2px; }`. Declare it after the interaction rules, per the existing convention at tasks.css:143, so the state system is not overridden.
standing.assertion: With `.dockInput` focused, `getComputedStyle(.dockField).outlineStyle === "solid"`, `outlineWidth === "2px"`, `outlineColor === "rgb(79, 70, 229)"`, and its contrast against the composited dock backdrop is ≥3:1; then type a query, move focus to `.dockPrimary`, and assert `getComputedStyle(.dockField).outlineStyle === "none"` — i.e. focused and unfocused-with-a-query render differently.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX AND ON THE CENSUS, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do not discard the observation; the remedy as written reintroduces the exact defect its own cited comment exists to prevent, and I proved that by applying it.

WHAT REPRODUCES EXACTLY. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 against `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, four states in sequence, computed style on `[data-app="tasks"] .dockField`:
- rest: 196px, `rgba(17,17,17,0.04)`, `rgba(0,0,0,0) 0 0 0 1px inset`
- focused (settled past the 220ms): 392px, `rgb(255,255,255)`, `rgba(17,17,17,0.16) 0 0 0 1px inset`
- typed "linen": identical, class becomes `dockField is-live`
- focus moved to `.dockAvatar`/`.dockPrimary`, query still present: **byte-identical**
The shared block at src/tasks.css:1232-1233 is verbatim as quoted, `.dockInput:focus { outline: none }` at 1259 is verbatim, and `--line-strong: rgba(17,17,17,0.16)` (src/tasks.css:52) over white gives 1.43:1. All correct.

WHERE THE CENSUS IS WRONG. "Every other control in the suite gets `outline: 2px solid var(--indigo)` — 55 of 56 ... this one is the only exception" is false. I tabbed all four states the seat names and read the computed outline at each stop. Three fields carry no outline, not one: `.dockInput`, notes `.topField` (src/notes.css:407 `outline: none`), and notes `.peelField`. The suite has a deliberate, documented house pattern for text fields — suppress the input's outline, light the **container's ring in solid indigo**: src/notes.css:406 `.top:has(.topField:focus-visible) { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--indigo), ... }` (I measured it firing: `rgb(79,70,229) 0 0 0 1px`), src/notes.css:408 the same for `.phoneField`, and `.peelField` carries `rgb(79,70,229) 0 0 0 1px inset` on itself. So Tasks is not the lone outline-less control; it is the lone field whose container ring is drawn in **ink instead of indigo**. That correction matters because it is what the fix should have been built from and was not.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG — measured, with the seat's rule injected verbatim via addStyleTag:
1. **It paints a keyboard ring on a mouse click.** `:focus-within` is not `:focus-visible`. A plain pointer click on the field yielded `outline: 2px solid rgb(79,70,229)`. Nothing else in the suite does this; notes.css:406 uses `:has(.topField:focus-visible)` precisely to avoid it.
2. **It puts two indigo rings on one composed control.** With a query typed, `.dockClear` renders and is the next tabstop. At that stop I read `.dockClear` outline `2px solid rgb(79,70,229)` (from the generic rule at src/tasks.css:143) **and simultaneously** `.dockField` outline `2px solid rgb(79,70,229)` from the new rule. That is verbatim "two rings on one object is the classic composed-control tell" — the comment at src/tasks.css:1257-1258 that the finding quotes as evidence of the bug is in fact the reason the current code is shaped as it is, and the fix walks straight into it.
3. **The geometry is wrong on the numbers.** `2px` width + `2px` offset extends 4px. Measured: gap from pill to `.dockPrimary` is exactly **4px**, and pill-left to dock-left is **5px** (`.dock` has `gap: 4px; padding: 5px`, src/tasks.css:1191-1192). The ring would fill the entire gap and butt against the Add-task button, and sit 1px inside the dock's own edge.
4. Minor: the enumeration "keep width, padding, background and box-shadow" silently drops `color: var(--ink-1)` from the same block.

SEVERITY, corrected. Not blocking and not misleading — defect. A keyboard user is not actually stranded: the pill jumps 196→392px, the ground goes wash→white, `.dockField:focus-within svg` darkens to `--ink-2`, and a caret is drawn. And in the one state the seat calls byte-identical, focus is on another control that is showing its own indigo ring, so nobody is lost. What is genuinely below the bar is that this is the suite's only focus indicator drawn in ink, at 1.43:1 against the 3:1 floor, and the only one that reads the same as a content state.
standing.breaks:
What the sharpened fix could plausibly break, and what to re-measure:
- The `box-shadow` transition on `.dockField` (tasks.css:1148-ish) now animates a colour swap between two states rather than transparent→ink. Re-drive rest → click → type → Tab-away and confirm the ring does not flash a mid-transition mauve, and that `prefers-reduced-motion` still lands on the right terminal colour (the reduce block at tasks.css:1274 kills the transition entirely, so verify the ring is correct there too).
- Specificity: `:has(.dockInput:focus-visible)` (0,3,0) beats the shared `:focus-within` block (0,2,0) only because it is declared later as well — confirm no later rule in the ≤720 block at tasks.css:1279-1282 re-declares `box-shadow` on `.dockField` and clobbers it. That block only sets `width`, so it should be clean, but re-read it after the edit.
- Phone: at 390 the field is `width: 100%` and the expansion is carried by ground + ring alone, so the ring is doing proportionally more work. Re-shoot `paper-tasks.board--390x844.png` and confirm the indigo reads against the white dock and is not clipped by the dock's 5px padding.
- Gates: re-run `audit.mjs --lab=...` — `var(--indigo)` is one of the locked 11 so the palette lock should stay green, but the non-text contrast check will now see a new ring colour on this element and should be confirmed reporting 6.31:1 rather than 1.43:1. Re-run `interaction-check.mjs` unchanged; this touches no behaviour it asserts.
- The one thing genuinely lost: `is-live` and focus are no longer distinguishable by *geometry*, only by ring colour. If the panel wants them separable at a glance in a screenshot, that is a second decision, not this fix.
- Re-tab tasks.board end to end and confirm the tabstop count is unchanged (18 at 1440) and that `.dockClear`, when a query is present, shows exactly one `2px solid rgb(79,70,229)` outline and the pill shows only its inset ring.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .trayBody — the column scroller's bottom edge, and the .tray::after hairline drawn at it
standing.problem: The column scroller rests at scrollTop 0 with its height set by the board row, so its bottom edge falls at an arbitrary y inside whatever card happens to be there — and it lands inside a line box, not between them. Measured with a Range/getClientRects sweep against the live page: tasks.dense cuts a line of type in two or three lanes simultaneously at EVERY declared viewport. 1920x1000 (the committed frame): To do cuts "Enquiry" 7.5px into a 14px line, In progress cuts "Aisling & Tom" 8.9px into 16px, Done cuts "Deposit invoice settled, Mara & Finn" 13.2px into an 18px line — the second line reads "& Finn" with its lower third sliced off by the hairline. 1440x960: three lanes, one showing only 3.1px of an 18px line. 1280x900: three lanes. 768x1024: two lanes. 390x844: three lanes. tasks.board is clean at 1280/1440/1920 but cuts at 768 (Done, "Mara & Finn", 6.4 of 16) and 390 (two lanes). The same mechanism produces a 5.5px sliver of a 98px card in Done at 1120x820 — a five-pixel ghost of a card above the rule. The source comment at the .tray::after rule states the design's own goal — "A rule says the same thing and never touches a glyph" — and the rule keeps that promise while the clip it marks does not: scroll-snap governs where the scroller RESTS after a scroll, and nothing governs where it starts. NOTE: I am aware `dense-board-cuts-a-word-in-half` (r3) was refuted on its fix. I am filing this deliberately, with per-viewport measurements it did not carry and a different remedy, because the surface still bisects type in a frame this panel is being shown.
standing.consequence: Orla opens her real board — the dense one, thirty-two tasks — and the first thing her eye lands on at the foot of three columns is half a line of letters. A half-drawn word is not read as "there is more below"; it is read as the app failing to paint. It is the loudest thing on a surface whose entire argument is calm, and it is in the screenshot.
standing.fix: In the same post-layout pass that sets `--body-bottom`, for each overflowing `.trayBody` compute the offset of the last card that fits entirely — `[...body.querySelectorAll('.card')].filter(c => c.offsetTop + c.offsetHeight <= body.clientHeight).pop()` — and set `body.style.blockSize` to that card's bottom offset (clearing the inline size when the body no longer overflows). The scroller then always ends in the 8px gutter between cards, the existing hairline lands in that gutter, and the leftover pixels fall to the tray's bottom padding above the Add row. No new colour, no mask, no change to the snap model.
standing.assertion: For `tasks.board` and `tasks.dense` at 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, walk every text node inside every `.trayBody` and assert that no client rect straddles the scroller's bottom edge (never `rect.top < body.bottom - 0.5 && rect.bottom > body.bottom + 0.5`); and assert that every partially-visible `.card` shows either 0px or its full height.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE OBSERVATION — and the fix is not merely wrong, it makes every number in the finding worse. Do not discard the observation; do not ship this remedy.

THE OBSERVATION REPRODUCES, ALMOST EXACTLY. Chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.dense`, Range/getClientRects sweep against each `.trayBody`'s bottom edge at rest. 1920x1000: To do cuts "Enquiry" 7.5 into a 14px line, In progress cuts "Aisling & Tom" 8.9 into 16px, Done cuts "Deposit invoice settled, Mara & Finn" 13.2 into 18px — all three verbatim. 1440x960: three lanes, "Nora & Cian deposit received" showing 3.1 of 18 — verbatim. 1280x900: three lanes. 1120x820: Done is a 5.5px sliver of a 98px card — verbatim. tasks.board clean at 1280/1440/1920, cuts at 768 (Done, "Mara & Finn", 6.4 of 16 — verbatim) and 390 (two lanes). Only one number is off: dense at 390 cuts two lanes, not three (Done there is a 10.9px sliver carrying no line box). The mechanism is stated correctly too — snap governs rest-after-scroll, nothing governs the start.

THE FIX IS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG BECAUSE IT MEASURES IN THE WRONG COORDINATE SPACE. `.trayBody` declares no `position`; `.tray` declares `position: relative` (line 1279). I confirmed at runtime that every card's `offsetParent` is `.tray`, not `.trayBody` — card `offsetTop` values in To do at 1920 are 66, 210, 316, 459…, where 66 is the head's own height. So `c.offsetTop + c.offsetHeight <= body.clientHeight` compares tray-relative tops against the body's height, and `body.style.blockSize = <that card's bottom offset>` assigns a tray-relative number as a block-size. The file's own `measureEdges` gets this right two lines away — `last.offsetTop - body.offsetTop + last.offsetHeight` — and the fix drops the `- body.offsetTop`.

I RAN THE FIX AS WRITTEN. 1920x1000, tasks.dense, three consecutive passes:
1. It does not fix the cut — it doubles it. Before: three of five lanes cut type. After: FIVE of five, each ~9-10px into a 21px line ("Enquiry." 9.3/21, "Aisling & Tom." 9.7/21, "Bar. High priority." 9.4/21, "Held 21 days, since 25 Jun" 10/21, "Nora & Cian" 9/16), each ending ~55px into a card. The 66px error lands the new edge mid-card every time.
2. It breaks two lanes that were clean. Waiting and Under review do not overflow at 1920 (`data-more` absent, all content visible, no cut). The filter still returns a "last fitting card" there and clamps them: review 464→413, waiting 233→183. Content that was fully on screen is now hidden and cut mid-line. The finding's guard — "clearing the inline size when the body no longer overflows" — never fires, because the clamp is what creates the overflow. Passes 2 and 3 confirm it latches.
3. Its claim about where the leftover pixels go is false about the code, and this is the seat's own subject. `.tray` is `padding: 14px 12px 0` — no bottom padding — and `.trayAdd` is `flex: none; margin-top: 4px` with no auto margin. Today all five "Add here" rows sit flush at the tray foot (top 862, tray bottom 898 at 1920). After the fix: 843, 843, 612, 382, 787 — five Add rows at five heights, up to 461px apart, each floating over 55-516px of empty white above an unchanged tray foot. The shared `.tray::after` hairline, which is drawn at `--body-bottom`, goes ragged with them. A UI-composition finding that trades one straight rule across the board for five staggered rules and five staggered Add rows is a net loss.

SEVERITY. The seat declares none; the class is defect, not more, which is exactly where `dense-board-cuts-a-word-in-half` (r3) left it. A scroll container clipping its content is the universal behaviour of every list in Linear, Stripe and Vercel, and the partial card is itself the overflow cue the hairline seconds. This is the third filing of this surface (`tray-clips-cards-mid-line` r1, `dense-board-cuts-a-word-in-half` r3); filing it again with a new remedy was legitimate, and the remedy is worse than the disease.
standing.breaks:
The fix as filed breaks three things I measured: it cuts type in five lanes instead of three; it clamps and clips two lanes (Waiting, Under review at 1920) that do not overflow at all, hiding visible content; and it lifts the five "Add here" rows to five different heights (843/843/612/382/787 against an unchanged tray foot at 898), taking the `.tray::after` hairline ragged with them. It also latches — `measureEdges` runs on every scroll (13283) and every repaint (13137), the clamp keeps the body overflowing, so the "clear when it no longer overflows" release never fires.

If the sharpened version lands, re-measure: (a) the Range sweep at 390/768/1120/1280/1440/1920 across `tasks.dense`, `tasks.board` and the filtered board — zero cut line boxes is the pass, and any lane whose `data-more` state flips is a regression; (b) the five `.trayAdd` rect tops per viewport — they must stay equal in overflowing lanes and equal to trayBottom − 36; (c) the spread of `--body-bottom` across the five trays, which is the new composition cost and the reason to reconsider shipping it; (d) three consecutive `measureEdges` passes at one viewport, asserting `clientHeight` is identical on passes 2 and 3, since the ratchet is the failure mode; (e) the compact-density and stacked-header paths, where the head is a different height and the dropped `- body.offsetTop` term would have had a different magnitude; (f) keyboard carry and the completion FLIP, which scroll the body and re-enter `measureEdges` mid-animation — the existing comment at `extent` warns that `scrollHeight` lies during the settle, and a height clamp that fires there will pump the layout; (g) `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs`, both currently green.

standing.element: [data-app="notes"] .desk / .deskAside / .index — Notes, reading a note
standing.problem: The desk's height is set entirely by the metadata rail, not by the note. `.readBody` renders at a fixed 496px measure and 55–83px tall for every one of the 14 fixture notes (scrollHeight == clientHeight throughout; the 425px max-height is never reached), while `.deskAside` renders at 155, 224 or 275px depending on how many labelled facts that note carries. So `.desk` takes exactly three heights — 291, 360 and 411px — and the index below it takes exactly three tops — 426, 495 and 546px — identical at 1280, 1440 and 1920. Driven by clicking rows in order, the row you just clicked moves under your own pointer: row2 +99px, row3 +69px, row4 −158px, row9 −200px, row10 −122px. Nothing scrolls to compensate (index scrollTop stays 0); focus is correctly moved to `.readBody`, so the keyboard survives and the eye does not.
standing.consequence: Reading down her notebook is the thing Orla does most, and every note she opens throws the rest of the list up or down by as much as 200px. The next note she meant to read is no longer where she left it, so a second click lands on a different note than the one she was looking at. The list under her hand is not stable, and it is unstable for a reason she can never see: the length of the machine's metadata column.
standing.fix: Reserve the reading desk at one height. Give `.deskAside` a `min-block-size` equal to its tallest configuration (275px at desk widths, measured), so `.desk` renders 411px for every note and `.index` keeps one top. The already-empty lower half of the note column absorbs the reserve — it is the writing area "Write on it" opens into, so the space is not wasted. Leave the ≤720 branch alone, where the desk is `display: none`.
standing.assertion: At 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, lift each of the 14 `.idxItem` rows in turn and assert `.desk` height is identical for all 14 (±1px) and `.index` top is identical for all 14 (±1px); and assert that clicking any `.idxItem` moves that element's own bounding-box top by 0px (±1px).
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, AND ON ONE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF THE OBSERVATION. Do not discard the geometry — the core measurement reproduces exactly — but do not ship this remedy.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, clicking each of the 14 index rows at 1280x900, 1440x960, 1920x1000): `.deskAside` renders at exactly 155 / 224 / 275px on a 3 / 4 / 5-fact note; `.desk` at exactly 291 / 360 / 411px; `.index` top at exactly 426 / 495 / 546px — identical at all three widths. `.readBody` is 496px wide and 55 or 83px tall for every fixture note, scrollHeight == clientHeight throughout, and its computed max-height is 365px at 1280, 425px at 1440, 465px at 1920 (the seat quoted the 1440 value as if it were the constant — minor, but it is one of three). Focus does land on `.readBody`. So the diagnosis "the desk's height is set by the metadata rail" is correct.

WHAT DOES NOT. "Nothing scrolls to compensate (index scrollTop stays 0)" is false, and it is the sentence the severity rests on. Driven clean at 1440x960 — click rows 0..13 in order, no synthetic scrolling — `.index` scrollTop goes 0, 0, 0, 0, 158, 158, 158, 187, 318, 319, 432, 432, 432, 502. The index scrolls the cursor row toward the top of its own viewport on click (it carries `scroll-padding-top: 66px` and `scroll-padding-bottom: var(--walk-reserve, 160px)`), so a large share of the displacement the seat attributes to the desk resize is in fact a deliberate scroll-into-view of the row you clicked. And the five quoted displacements do not reproduce under the seat's own stated protocol: I measured, in click order, +220, 0, −121, +69, −158, 0, 0, −29, −131, +50, −234, 0, +69, −70. Neither 0- nor 1-indexing maps "row2 +99 / row9 −200 / row10 −122" onto that. The phenomenon is real; the evidence offered for it is not the evidence that was measured.

THE FIX IS WRONG ON ITS NUMBER, ITS BOUNDARY, AND ITS JUSTIFICATION.

1. 275px is not the tallest configuration "at desk widths". The two-column desk starts at 1081px, not 1280. Measured on the 5-fact note: 1081 → aside 294px, desk 430, index top 565; 1100 → 294 / 430 / 565; 1160 and up → 275 / 411 / 546. Between 1081 and ~1150 the margin column is narrow enough that a fact wraps. A 275px `min-block-size` therefore leaves the desk taking TWO heights (411 and 430) across that band and the index still moving 19px — the finding does not fix its own problem where its own layout branch begins.

2. The named exemption is at the wrong breakpoint. The finding says "leave the ≤720 branch alone, where the desk is `display: none`". But the branch that matters is `@media (max-width: 1080px)`, where `.deskAside` becomes `grid-auto-flow: column` — a horizontal strip under the writing. Measured on the 5-fact note: 768 → aside 73px, desk 320; 900 → 73 / 320; 1024 → 73 / 328; 1080 → 73 / 328. An unqualified `min-block-size: 275px` injects 202px of dead white into the desk across the entire 721–1080 tablet band and pushes the index down by that much — on the widths where the index is already the more cramped of the two locked planes. As written, the fix ships that regression.

3. The justification is factually false. "The already-empty lower half of the note column absorbs the reserve — it is the writing area 'Write on it' opens into." It is not. Driven at 1440 on note 0: read mode desk 411, index top 546; press `[data-act="edit"]` and the desk becomes 347 with the index top at 482 — the textarea renders 116px and the foot moves out of the spanning row, so "Write on it" SHRINKS the desk by 64px. The aside is 275px in both states, so pinning the aside does not stabilise the desk across the note's own states either: after the fix the index would still jump 64px the moment you write on a note, and the reserved band would still be dead white in read mode, which is exactly the `notes-desk-half-empty` class this programme already adjudicated once.

SEVERITY. The seat implies more than this is worth. The product does nothing it does not say and asserts nothing untrue; the index does scroll the clicked row into view, and the row you clicked stays on screen in all 14 cases (`visBefore` true throughout). This is a defect — visibly wrong, passable — not blocking or misleading.
standing.sharpenedFix: Reserve, but scope it and use the measured number. (a) Put the reserve inside the two-column branch only — `@media (min-width: 1081px) { [data-app="notes"] .top[data-two] > .deskAside { min-block-size: 294px; } }` — so the 721–1080 band, where the aside is a 73px horizontal strip, is untouched. 294px is the measured tallest configuration (5 facts at 1081–1150, where the margin column wraps); 275px is only the tallest at ≥1160 and leaves the desk taking two heights below that. With 294 the desk renders 430px and `.index` keeps one top at 565px for every fixture note at every width ≥1081. (b) Either accept that "Write on it" still shortens the desk by 64px, or close that separately by keeping `.topFoot` spanning `1 / -1` in the edit template as it is in read, which is where the 64px goes. (c) If the dead band reads as empty rather than as desk, prefer holding the height on `.desk` rather than on the aside — the paper then stays honest to its content and the reserve is ground, not white paper — but re-check that the paper's own moving bottom edge is the lesser evil before choosing it.
standing.breaks:
The fix AS WRITTEN breaks the 721–1080 band: `.deskAside` there is a 73px horizontal strip, so a 275px floor adds 202px of dead paper and drives `.index` down from a 320–328px desk to ~522px, on the widths where the index has least room. It also fails to stabilise 1081–1160 (aside 294 > 275, two desk heights remain) and does nothing about the 64px the desk loses when the edit template renders.

AFTER THE SHARPENED FIX LANDS, RE-MEASURE: (1) `.readBody`'s height sum — it computes `max(120px, 100vh - var(--desk-chrome,311px) - var(--index-floor,224px) - var(--peel-h,0px))`, and `--desk-chrome: 311px` is commented as "measured at 1280, its widest". A permanent 294px aside makes the desk taller than that constant assumes, so re-derive 311 and re-check the note window at 1280x800 and 1440x900, not just at 1000px tall. (2) The index floor: confirm at least the five rows `--index-floor` is written to buy still render at 1281x800 with the taller desk. (3) The seam: `notes.seam` at 1440 measures aside 155 / desk 475 with the peel panel under the paper; a 294px floor pushes that desk to ~514, so re-check that `--peel-h` yielding still leaves the index reachable at 1280x800. (4) The three shipped 1920 frames (`shots/paper-notes.notebook`, `paper-notes.seam`) move — regenerate. (5) Re-run both gates: `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs` (the audit's hit-target and index-row rows sit below the desk and will shift).

rounds.notes: Every blocking, misleading, defect and refinement finding is closed and each carries an assertion written against it: tools/truth.mjs grew two sections (11c, 11d) and tools/round5.mjs is new. The gate went 379 → 439. Three assertions had to be repaired before they measured anything, and all three failed the same way this lab has now met seven times — the rule was not reading what it thought it was reading. The index-head rule looked for the count inside #index, where it is not, read NaN and passed every state without measuring one. The couple's filter sentence was guarded behind “if the menu offered it”, was never offered, and was never reported. The breakpoint-caret rule read document.activeElement, which answers BODY for a document that does not hold window focus — so it reported a lost caret three separate ways on a product that had put it back 35ms in. Two product defects were found by fixing those rules: Tasks' dock monogram was reaching across a scope boundary for Notes' --tr-cap and silently computing `normal`, and the desk-height reserve exposed a control the craft rule was measuring against the fold rather than against the product.

seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
rounds.headline: The first round on a frozen surface, and the first whose worst finding was a live crash. Seven seats drove one page NARROWED across 720 — something no loop in either gate had ever done, because every one of them opens a fresh page per width — and three of them independently hit the same ReferenceError: the media-query listeners the 2 September ledger added had never executed at all, so the timeline kept the desk composition on a phone and Tasks kept a five-lane board in a 372px viewport. Four green gates had frozen that build hours earlier. The round also proved a second blind spot of the same shape: every no-sideways-scroll assertion had only ever run on a coarse pointer, so the dictation floor overflowed the document by 145px at 320 — WCAG 1.4.10 — on exactly the narrowed desktop window the guideline describes. Refutation rose from 14% to 29%: three seats sighted the Timeline wordmark and all three were killed, one by driving rather than reading. 24 confirmed, 7 closed, 17 standing.

confirmed.element: title="Reading a photo happens on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1675, 1698, 1800) and title="Notes options are on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1633) against the ratified NOT_YET grammar at src/app.js:96-105; ELSEWHERE at src/notes.js:3462-3469
confirmed.problem: The honest doors were settled in one grammar and Notes' own two closed doors did not get it. src/app.js:96-105 holds five noun phrases naming a destination — "Every project in one list. Not here yet.", "Guides and support. Not here yet." — with the reason recorded in the code (a door's job is to name what is behind it). Notes' photo and options doors instead say the work "happens on another screen", which names a place this product does not have and tells Orla her photo-reading is somewhere else rather than not built. Driven, the same voice reaches the screen reader five more times (src/notes.js:3462-3469). One of those five is broken English: ELSEWHERE.privacy at src/notes.js:3465 concatenates N.copy.privacyLong, which has no terminal period, so pressing "Private to you" announces "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — two sentences fused with no punctuation. The same token is concatenated correctly, with the period, at src/notes.js:2656.
confirmed.fix: Correct two errors in the proposed fix first. (a) ELSEWHERE.photo and ELSEWHERE.options are DEAD code: src/notes.js:3220 intercepts any aria-disabled control whose title matches /Not here yet/ and announces the TITLE — driven, [data-act="options"] and [data-act="photo"] speak their titles verbatim and never reach the table. So rewrite the titles at 1633/1675/1698/1800 and delete those two table entries rather than rewriting them. (b) ELSEWHERE.more is reached ONLY by the note-level button at src/notes.js:1951/2200, whose own aria-label is "More actions for this note" — the suite door is handled separately at src/notes.js:3243 — so it must become "More for this note. Not here yet.", NOT "The rest of Signal Studio. Not here yet." as proposed, which would keep the exact mismatch that makes it a defect. Then: titles 1633 -> "More for this note. Not here yet."; 1675/1698/1800 -> "A photo, read into words. Not here yet."; ELSEWHERE.privacy -> `${N.copy.privacyLong}. Your privacy settings. Not here yet.` (the period is the bug); retry -> "Sending again. Not here yet. Your note is still here."; destroy -> "Deleting for good. Not here yet. Nothing here is deleted.". Gate it: assert every string a closed door speaks ends in "Not here yet." (optionally plus one reassurance sentence) and that no string in src/ contains "another screen".
confirmed.verdict: Driven at 1440 on notes.notebook, two of these are objectively broken, not taste: pressing the head's "Private to you" announces into the live region, verbatim, "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — two sentences fused, because N.copy.privacyLong (src/fixture.js:617) has no terminal period and src/notes.js:3465 omits the one that lines 1632 and 2656 both add; and pressing the note's "More actions for this note" announces "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen.", the wrong destination and with no "Not here yet." at all. src/notes.js is the only file in src/ containing "another screen" (11 occurrences) against the ratified noun-phrase grammar at src/app.js:96-105, and the door titles contradict themselves in one breath — "happens on another screen. Not here yet." cannot both be true.

confirmed.element: .b-layout [data-layout-to] / [data-app="timeline"][data-layout] — src/timeline.js:176-178 `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { if (C.rootEl()... ) go("owner-flight"); })`, in the core IIFE that opens at src/timeline.js:26; `C` is only declared at src/timeline.js:331, inside the renderer's separate closure
confirmed.problem: `C` is not in scope at line 177, so every crossing of 720px throws `ReferenceError: C is not defined` (measured: Chromium pageerror at MediaQueryList.<anonymous>, on 768→721→700 and again on 700→900) and the re-mount never runs. The file's own header comment at src/timeline.js:4-8 states the contract this handler exists to keep — "the across composition is withheld on it, and crossing it re-mounts the owner's surface so the bar is never stale" — and it is not kept. Driven: load timeline.owner-flight at 1024 (data-layout="across", the Across/Down group present), resize to 700 → data-layout stays "across" and the Across/Down buttons are still on screen at phone width, against the locked decision "Across is never offered on a phone". `acrossAllowed()` (src/timeline.js:620) reads `!PHONE_T.matches` correctly, but only at render time, and nothing re-renders. The reverse is as bad: load at 700 (down, no toggle), widen to 1024 → still down, toggle still absent, so a desk user who narrowed the window once can never get the across composition back. The gates cannot see any of this because both open a fresh page per viewport and never cross the boundary.
confirmed.fix: Replace the body of the handler at src/timeline.js:177 with a plain re-mount in the scope it actually lives in — `mount();` — and nothing else. Do NOT call `go()`: `go()` (src/timeline.js:2318-2326) moves focus to `.b-pressTitle`/`.b-who`, and stealing focus to a heading because somebody dragged a window edge is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Add the same one-line remount to the tasks/notes pattern already in use (`PHONE.addEventListener("change", () => mount())`, src/tasks.js:4203) so all three products cross 720 the same way, and add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs that resizes an open page across 720 in both directions and requires zero pageerrors plus `[data-layout-to]` absent below 721.
confirmed.verdict: confirmed by reproduction — the failing gate log is panel/round-6/confirmed-by-reproduction/

confirmed.element: [data-app="notes"] .darkActs / .darkAct — src/notes.css:1889 `.darkActs { display: flex; ... flex: 0 0 auto; margin-left: auto; }`, src/notes.css:1007 `.darkAct { ... height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; }`, and src/notes.css:1787 `.darkAct kbd { display: none; }` which lives inside `@media (pointer: coarse)` opened at src/notes.css:1770
confirmed.problem: In notes.voice the dictation overlay's action pair cannot shrink or wrap, so it forces the whole DOCUMENT to scroll sideways. Measured: `.darkActs` renders 440px wide at left:32, needing 472px of viewport; `.darkAct` ("Stop and read it back" + a 63px `<kbd>Ctrl Enter</kbd>`) is 296px with no min-width:0. Driven at height 844: without mobile emulation documentElement overflow is 152px @320, 82px @390, 42px @430, 12px @460, 0 from ~472; WITH the gate's own isMobile/hasTouch emulation it is still 28px @320. The only rule that relieves it hides the keycap under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, so a narrowed desktop window — which is exactly how WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow is tested, and what a 1280px desktop at 400% zoom becomes — never gets it, and neither does a 320px phone. 1.4.10 (AA) requires no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px; this state fails it in both pointer modes. The gate cannot see it because config.viewports starts at 390 and marks it isMobile, and `@media (max-width: 900px)` at src/notes.css:1893 only lets `.darkFoot` wrap — it never touches `.darkActs`. This is the same class the 2 September ledger already closed once for notes.review ("the one state in the suite that scrolled sideways at 390 was the one the gate never walked"); it is back, one state over.
confirmed.fix: Ship only the first TWO of the three proposed rules, appended after src/notes.css:1899: `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkActs { flex: 1 1 100%; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-left: 0; min-width: 0; } }` and `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkAct { flex: 1 1 100%; min-width: 0; justify-content: center; padding: 0 12px; } }`. Verified with the rules injected at the DOCUMENT TAIL (injecting into <head> loses the same-specificity cascade to the page's own <style> at line 10 and leaves a spurious 26px residual — that, not a second cause, is what the cut-off run saw): overflow is 0px at 320/360/390/430/460/719 in BOTH pointer modes, pills stay 44px tall at 256px @320 and 326px @390, nothing clips, and 768/1440 are unchanged (131/290 fine, 86/215 coarse). Do NOT add the third rule and do NOT delete the coarse keycap hide: without them the keycap still fits unclipped inside the 256px pill at 320 and overflow is still 0, so the Ctrl+Enter hint survives for exactly the keyboard user who narrows a desktop window. Then add { "name": "320x844", "width": 320, "height": 844 } with no isMobile to elevate.config.json so the reflow width is gated on a fine pointer.
confirmed.verdict: Driven and reproduced: on a fine pointer at height 844, notes.voice makes documentElement.scrollWidth exceed clientWidth by 145px @320, 75px @390, 35px @430, 5px @460, 0 from 472, and window.scrollX really moves (scrolled to 60 at 390) — and it is user-reached, not URL-only: at 390 fine-pointer the single visible [data-act="voice"] glyph in the dock takes overflow from 0 to 75px on one click. The only relief is `.darkAct kbd { display: none }` inside `@media (pointer: coarse)` (src/notes.css:1787), so a narrowed desktop window — the exact WCAG 1.4.10 reflow test — never gets it; the gate misses it because interaction-check.mjs open() sets isTouch from vp.isMobile and config.viewports starts at 390 with isMobile:true.

confirmed.element:
[data-app="notes"] h1.headName / li.idxSection > h3.idxDay — src/notes.js:1628 `

All your notes

`, killed by src/notes.css:1595 `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`; the day groups at src/notes.js:2128 `

`
confirmed.problem: Notes is the only product of the three whose heading outline is wrong, and it is wrong two different ways. At a desk the accessibility tree reads heading[1] "All your notes" followed straight by five heading[3] day groups — level 2 does not exist anywhere in the product, so the outline skips a level on the surface a person spends most of their time on. At ≤720 `display: none` removes the h1 from the tree entirely (display:none prunes, it does not merely hide), so on a phone notes.notebook offers five level-3 headings under nothing, and notes.review offers a lone level-2 "Worth doing something about?" under nothing. Measured with page.accessibility.snapshot at 390 and 1440 across all four Notes states. Tasks keeps h1 "The Orchard, events" (plus five h2 lane names at a desk) at both widths and Timeline keeps h1 "Mara & Finn" plus two h2s at both widths, so this is Notes' defect alone, not a suite decision. The gate cannot see it: interaction-check.mjs never inspects heading levels, and the audit does not model the accessibility tree.
confirmed.fix: Both edits verified inert. (1) In the ≤720 block replace `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` with the sheet's existing `.sr` treatment from src/shell.css:89 AND add `min-width: 0` — the base rule at src/notes.css:287 sets `min-width: 5ch`, which would otherwise fight `width: 1px`. Driven at 390 in all four Notes states, before vs after: .head stays 100px tall and 372px wide, its bottom stays at y=109, .idx top is unchanged (224/194/142/224), documentElement X-overflow stays 0 and scrollHeight is unchanged — the only delta is the tree gaining its root. (2) Emit `<h2 class="idxDay">` at src/notes.js:2128 and drop role/aria-level: notes.css contains NO tag-based heading selector at all, and a live h3→h2 swap at 1440 left all five .idxDay boxes byte-identical in x/y/width/height/font-size/weight/colour/tracking/padding/position, with the outline becoming 1,2,2,2,2,2. Add one gate assertion per state per width: an h1 is present in the tree and no level is skipped.
confirmed.verdict: Enumerated the live outline in all four Notes states at 1440 and 390: at 1440 notes.notebook/notes.voice read h1 "All your notes" then five h3.idxDay with no h2 anywhere, and at 390 src/notes.css:1595 `display:none` prunes h1.headName from the tree entirely, leaving notes.notebook/voice as five orphan h3s, notes.review as a lone h2, and notes.seam with ZERO headings in the accessibility tree. Tasks keeps h1 at both widths and Timeline keeps h1+two h2s at both widths, so this is Notes alone; interaction-check.mjs never inspects heading levels.

confirmed.element: PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", …) — _gate-suite.html:20190-20192, `C.rootEl()` inside the IIFE that spans _gate-suite.html:20040-20319, where `C` is never declared (`var C = window.__TLCORE` is at _gate-suite.html:20345, inside the NEXT IIFE)
confirmed.problem: Every crossing of the 720px phone query throws `Uncaught ReferenceError: C is not defined` at _gate-suite.html:20191, in all three products (reproduced by resizing tasks.board, notes.notebook and timeline.owner-flight from 1440 to 720 — one throw each, in both directions). The handler's whole job is to re-render the timeline for the new layout, so it does nothing at all. The consequence is measured: timeline.owner-flight loaded fresh at 390 gives data-layout="down", zero layout toggles and the action bar folded to "Add a moment · ···". The SAME state narrowed from 1440 to 390 gives data-layout="across", TWO visible [data-layout-to] buttons and the full desk bar "Add a moment / Preview / Get the link" — so the phone gets the across composition and the layout toggle that the 2 September ledger decided is never offered on a phone, plus a three-button desk bar at 390. Enlarging back does not repair it either; the state is stuck at whatever the first paint chose. The behaviour gate cannot see this: it opens each state fresh at a fixed viewport and never resizes, and document overflow stays 0 so the sideways-scroll assertions stay green. A person rotating a phone, a tablet entering split view, or anyone dragging a browser window narrower gets this surface.
confirmed.fix: Two lines. In the IIFE at _gate-suite.html:20040, add `var C = window.__TLCORE;` beside the other module handles at the top of that IIFE (or replace the reference at :20191 with `window.__TLCORE.rootEl()`), so the handler runs instead of throwing. Then, because the handler currently re-renders only when the state is owner-flight, widen it to re-render whatever is mounted: `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { var st = window.__TLCORE.rootEl().getAttribute("data-state"); if (st) go(st); });`. Add to interaction-check.mjs a resize assertion for every state and every crossing: open at 1440, setViewportSize to 390 and back, and require (a) pageErrors unchanged, and (b) that the post-resize DOM matches a fresh load at that width on data-layout, the count of visible [data-layout-to], and the visible .b-act labels.
confirmed.verdict: confirmed by reproduction — the failing gate log is panel/round-6/confirmed-by-reproduction/

confirmed.element: `let view = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)").matches ? "list" : "board";` — _gate-suite.html:11496, read once at script parse and never given a `change` listener (compare the 720 query at _gate-suite.html:11507-11509, which does get one)
confirmed.problem: The board/list rule is evaluated exactly once, at load. tasks.board loaded fresh at 390 correctly opens the List (segmented control reads "Board, List*", zero lanes rendered, board scrollWidth 372 = clientWidth). The same state narrowed from 1440 to 390 stays on the Board: five lanes visible and a board whose scrollWidth is 1520px inside a 372px viewport — a five-lane kanban paging sideways on a phone, which is the surface the 2 September ledger decided against ("below 1100 the board is a LIST"). It never repairs: enlarging and re-narrowing leaves it wherever the first paint put it. Document overflow stays 0 because the board is its own scroller, so every sideways-scroll assertion stays green, and the gate never resizes, so 129 assertions cannot see it.
confirmed.fix: Promote the query to a live one, matching what the 720 query already does. Replace the one-shot read with `const LIST_Q = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)"); let view = LIST_Q.matches ? "list" : "board"; let viewChosen = false;` — set `viewChosen = true` in the segmented control's handler at _gate-suite.html:14575 so an explicit human choice is never overridden — then `LIST_Q.addEventListener("change", (e) => { if (viewChosen) return; const next = e.matches ? "list" : "board"; if (next === view) return; view = next; mount(); });`. mount() already restores scroll and focus, so no place-keeping work is needed. standing.element: [data-act="open-task"].deskFactLink → openTask() at _gate-suite.html:11007-11019, against Notes' offerUndo/doUndo at _gate-suite.html:16137-16200 and the three per-product Ctrl+Z handlers at _gate-suite.html:14197 (tasks), :19509 (notes), :22171-22190 (timeline), each guarded on window.__SUITE.active(<product>)
standing.problem: Driven at 1440 on notes.seam, the suite's own primary journey: press Send to Tasks ("Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here. In The house.", card seam_n14_1 lands in To do, the strip reads "Undo · Ctrl Z · for 30 seconds"). The seam hands focus to "Open in Tasks"; press Enter; you arrive in Tasks with focus on the card that just landed. Press Ctrl+Z — the binding the strip you were reading a second ago advertised — and the suite answers "Nothing left to undo." while the seam's 30-second window is still counting down and the card is still under your hand. Nothing is undone. Arriving via the rail behaves the same. Walk back to Notes and the identical keystroke works ("Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.") and removes the card from both products. There are three independent undo stacks, each answering only for its own product, so the ONE act that by definition crosses products is the one act whose reversal the surface actively denies. "Nothing left to undo." is not a missing feature here; it is a false statement about the suite's state, spoken into the live region at the moment a person is least sure, on the gesture the whole suite exists to argue for.
standing.fix: Right mechanism, wrong file: the line numbers cited are in _gate-suite.html, which .gitignore lists and tools/wrap.mjs regenerates every gate run, so the edits must land in src/. Put armCross/takeCross on the suite api beside the cross/uncross it already exposes (src/app.js:1133); arm it from Notes' offerUndo (src/notes.js:268) when the label is the seam's and clear it in the expiry timeout at src/notes.js:307; consult it before the three bare denials at src/tasks.js:2483, src/notes.js (doUndo path, :309) and src/timeline.js:2170. Keep the single-consumption and expiry check as written, and run Notes' own doUndo so no revert logic is duplicated. Add one thing the fix omits: the cross-undo run from inside Tasks removes the card that is under the keyboard, so name the focus destination (the lane the card left, falling back to the rail's Notes tile) and make sure Tasks' refocus chain is not left on a removed node — that is the round-1 class the comment at src/notes.js:335 already records on the Notes side.
standing.verdict: Reproduced at 1440 on both arrival paths: after Send to Tasks the Notes strip reads 'Sent to Tasks. Undo Ctrl Z for 30 seconds' and card seam_n14_1 is on the board; press Open in Tasks (or the rail) and Ctrl+Z answers 'Nothing left to undo.' into the live region with the card still present and no undo affordance of any kind rendered in Tasks, while walking back to Notes shows the strip still counting ('for 27 seconds') and the same keystroke there says 'Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.' and removes the card from both. Three per-product stacks each guarded on __SUITE.active() mean the one act that by definition crosses products is the only act whose reversal is denied where the surface just sent you, and the denial is a false statement about suite state. No gate asserts this and it is a distinct defect from the four seam-copy findings — it is behaviour, not wording.

standing.element: .card[data-id] Space-to-drop branch of onKey() — _gate-suite.html:14304-14324 (compare the pointer drop at _gate-suite.html:15114 and the move menu at _gate-suite.html:14887, which both call arm({kind:"move"}))
standing.problem: Driven at 1440 on tasks.board: focus a card, Space ("Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."), ArrowRight ArrowRight, Space. The board says "...dropped in the review column." Ctrl+Z then answers "Nothing left to undo." and the card stays in Review. The identical move by mouse drag answers "...is back in the to do column.", and the same move through the card's Move menu is undoable too. Only the keyboard-carry drop fails to arm, because the Space branch of onKey mutates the lane and never calls arm(). Escape covers the card only while it is still in hand; once Space commits, the keyboard route is the one route to the board's most frequent structural act with no way back. The card advertises aria-roledescription="Movable task" and aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight", so this is precisely the promise the surface makes to the operator who cannot drag. A keyboard drop into Done IS undoable, because completed() arms — which is why the gap survives anyone who only tests the completion.
standing.fix: Do not capture heldSince/completedAt at the drop as proposed — moveTo() calls applyLaneFacts() unconditionally on every preview move, so the arrow walk has already nulled them by the time Space commits (this is the very failure the comment at src/tasks.js:3684-3686 records). Capture at PICKUP instead: in the else branch of the Space handler write carriedFrom = { lane: laneIds()[at.x], index: at.y, wasHeldSince: t.heldSince, wasCompletedAt: t.completedAt }, then in the drop branch pass those through to arm({kind:"move", id, title, lane: carriedFrom.lane, index: carriedFrom.index, toLane: lane, wasHeldSince: carriedFrom.wasHeldSince, wasCompletedAt: carriedFrom.wasCompletedAt}). Also mirror the pointer path's two other laws at src/tasks.js:3663-3667 and :3691-3694: skip arming (and the sentence) when the drop lands on the pickup lane+index, since a pick-up-and-put-back is a non-event, and do not announce an index in a sorted lane.
standing.verdict: Reproduced verbatim at 1440 on tasks.board: focus card, Space ("Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."), ArrowRight x2, Space -> "...dropped in the review column.", then Ctrl+Z -> "Nothing left to undo." and the card stays in Review; the same move by drag and by the card's Move menu both answer "...is back in the to do column.", and a keyboard drop into Done is undoable because completed() arms. Cause is exactly as stated at src/tasks.js:2884-2889 (the non-Done branch only calls say()), while the pointer path at :3687 and the menu path at :3460 both arm({kind:"move"}); interaction-check.mjs asserts nothing about carry undo, so no gate covers it, and the card advertises aria-roledescription="Movable task" plus aria-keyshortcuts for exactly this gesture.

standing.element: .b-editHost inside .b-stick — src/timeline.js:2429 (h("div.b-stick", …, [horizon({}), h("div.b-editHost"), …])) with the across-layout collapse at src/across.css:311-314 ([data-layout="across"][data-medium="full"] .b-two { display: block })
standing.problem: Timeline is Direction B, The Approach: the organising object is a distance. Placing a moment on that distance is the one act the direction exists for, and it is the one act performed blind. In the default desk layout (layout=across, medium=full) at 1440x960, pressing Add a moment inserts the 554px editor at y=497 — between the horizon band and the track — and pushes every one of the eight .b-grab handles to y=1179 and below. Measured: 0 of 8 moments on screen with the editor open, at 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000 alike. Pressing +7 does move the new moment's dot along the measure (its grab travels x=196 to 230 to 329 as the date goes 17 to 24 to 31 July, and the neighbouring moments re-stack to make room) — the mechanism is built and correct, and nothing scrolls it into view: the .app.sheet scroller (scrollHeight 1680, clientHeight 924) stays at scrollTop 0 through the open and through every stepper press. So the pin slides 133px along the ruler and the person pressing the button sees only a mono line reading "in 8 days". The same flow at layout=down keeps 3 of 8 moments on screen throughout, because .b-two is a real two-pane grid there — the comment at src/timeline.js:2431-2438 says that pane exists precisely so "the moment being moved" does not "walk off the bottom of the screen after two presses while the owner kept pressing". (1) Relocate the host: the across desk editor must not sit between the horizon band and the track, because scrolling the sheet to follow the dot would then carry the steppers out from under the hand - the exact failure keepInBand's own comment forbids. Render the second host after the plan and select it only when data-layout=across and data-medium!=phone, mirroring src/timeline.css:1187's :empty { display: none }. (2) Only then teach keepInBand a third band: the real scroller here is the .app.sheet element (overflow-y:auto), not .b-plan or the window, so add a branch that takes the nearest scrollable ancestor when neither `fixed` nor `paneScrolls` holds, and apply the existing minimum-correction arithmetic to it unchanged. Do not re-centre and do not touch the down layout, which already passes.
standing.verdict: Reproduced exactly by driving state=timeline.owner-flight&layout=across: pressing Add a moment inserts .b-edit at y=497, height 554, into the .b-editHost between the horizon band and the plan, and every .b-grab lands at y>=1157 - 0 of 8 moments in view at 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000. Two +7 presses walk the new dot x=196 to 230 to 329 while the only scroller (.app.sheet, scrollHeight 1680/1776 vs clientHeight 924/864) stays at scrollTop 0, because keepInBand at src/timeline.js:1536 returns early unless the panel is position:fixed or .b-plan scrolls, and across desk .b-plan computes overflow-y:visible. The same flow at layout=down keeps 3 of 8 in view (there .b-plan is overflow-y:auto), so the protection its own comment at src/timeline.js:2431-2438 describes is given up in the layout whose premise (src/across.css:308-310, 'the whole approach is in frame') is false the instant anyone edits.

standing.problem: The last thing you see after clearing the review queue counts the same notes twice. The builder is right for a mixed run ("8 notes went through. 3 became tasks and 5 stayed here.") and only stutters when every decision was the same kind — which is the common case, because most notes just get kept. Also worth recording in the finding: Keep is the only one-press outcome in review (d-task opens the peel, and d-delete is a closed door), so the stuttering branch is the flow's default ending rather than an edge case.

The code path is exactly as described — src/notes.js:1601 returns `went + parts[0]` whenever only one outcome occurred, so the same tally is printed twice in adjacent sentences. Tasks fixed that inside Tasks; the suite has re-created it threefold. Measured live at 1440 by picking a card up, opening the review actions and opening a moment's editor — three states no frame in shots/ contains, and the carry HUD is not one of the nine gated states, so neither gate can see it. Notes: Geist SANS 11px/600, radius 4px, padding 1px 5px, 18px tall, and its letter-spacing is INHERITED rather than declared (`font: inherit` with only size and weight overridden), so the same keycap renders at -0.0142em in .act and .dockField and -0.0164em in .darkAct — two letterfits on one object, which the audit gate also reports and does not pass. Timeline: Geist Mono 11px/400, +0.04em, radius 0, padding 0 — no box at all, just tinted mono text. So one object carries two families, two sizes, two weights, four letterfits, three radii and three paddings, and in one product it is not a key-shaped thing at all. standing.fix: Consolidate as proposed - 11px mono at +0.04em, the one spec that sits on an existing ramp step and does not fight the curve - but scope and finish it properly. (2) Unify the RING mechanism too, not just colour: Tasks uses `border: 1px solid` while Notes uses `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px`, which is why the two caps measure 19px and 17.9px tall even before the size change - declare the inset ring once and leave each product only its ring colour and fill. (3) The three Notes letterfits are all inherited: replace `font: inherit` with an explicit `letter-spacing: var(--cap-track)` at all five sites (notes.css 513, 542, 867, 908, 1032) rather than relying on the shared rule to win. (4) Re-measure the arrows exception (tasks.css:1578) after the 10 to 11px change before choosing 0.18em, and re-check .undoAct, which currently has no box and will gain one.

Notes' `font: inherit` gives it not two but THREE letterfits on one object (-0.0142em in .act/.dockField, -0.0164em in .darkAct at notes.voice, -0.0071em in .undoAct after a seam send), all tighter than Notes' own declared 11px tracking (--tr-11: 0em) and tighter than its 15px body at --tr-14 (-0.012em), so the curve inverts at the smallest size. A font-size census of every visible text node across all nine gated states at 1920 returns 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20, 27, 30, 96 and 148 and no 10, and no kbd is visible in tasks.board or tasks.dense at rest - so the 10px cap is a ramp step that exists only in ungated states neither gate can see, and this is exactly the residue tools/exclusions.mjs hands to the panel rather than proves.

standing.element: .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick — the one accent-filled mark on the horizontal measure. Broken by [data-app="timeline"][data-medium="sheet"|"full"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: -28px } at _gate-suite.html:7785-7786, which outranks [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) } at :8297
standing.problem: Direction B's whole claim is that position on the measure is daysFromToday x pixels-per-day computed from real dates. On the ACROSS axis the one mark the design accents as "this one, next" is the only mark plotted at the wrong distance. Measured at 1920x1000 (?layout=across): the .b-item for 'Menu tasting at The Orchard / Sat 1 Aug / 16' anchors at x=524.5, and its title, its date, its '16' and its own stem (.b-item::after, left:0) all sit at 524.5 — but its .b-tick centre is at 496.5, exactly 28.0px left. Every other tick is dead on (dx=0.0 at days 23, 37, 44, 51, 65, 79), so the filled dot visibly detaches from the stem that points at it. Cause is specificity: the desk-medium lead override is (0,5,0) and beats the across-axis rule at (0,4,0), so `left: 0` reaches all six ordinary marks and never the lead one. 28px is not a fixed error in days, because the rail rescales: 1602px/79d at 1920 reads 1.4 days early, 1.97 early at 1440, 2.30 at 1280, and 4.73 days early at 768 (rail 468px/79d), where the mark for Sat 1 August lands where Monday 27 July belongs. Identical on paper and on ink. The DOWN axis is correct (every tick dx=-23.5), so the error appears only on the axis whose entire job is horizontal distance — and both gates pass because neither compares a tick's centre with its item's anchor.
standing.fix: Add one rule after _gate-suite.html:8300 so the across axis governs the lead mark as it already governs the other six: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; }` — (0,5,0) and later in the file, so it beats :7786. If you would rather not stack a counter-rule, scope both desk overrides to the vertical axis instead by inserting `.b-measure:not([data-across="true"])` after the [data-medium] compound at :7781-7782 and :7785-7786, which leaves the down axis byte-identical. Then close the hole in the gate: for every .b-item on the across measure assert |tick centre x - item anchor x| <= 0.5px.
standing.verdict: Every measurement checks out: at 1920&layout=across the lead .b-item anchors at x=524.45 and its tick centre at 496.45 (dx=-28.00, computed left:-28px), the other six ticks are dead on (dx=0.00), and the down axis is uniformly consistent (every tick centre at dx=-23.50, lead included) so the error exists only on the axis whose job is horizontal distance. Cause is the specificity stated — the (0,5,0) [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] lead override outranks the (0,4,0) across-axis rule; medium resolves to "full" at every desk width, so it reproduces at 1440/1280/1024 and at 768-across, on paper and on ink, and the filled dot is visibly off its own leader stem in a crop. The proposed one-rule fix, applied in-page, takes dx to 0.00 and moves nothing else. Same defect as lead-tick-off-its-own-date-in-across, sighted independently by a second seat — one defect, one fix, two sightings.

standing.element: [data-app="notes"] .deskFactLink[data-act="open-task"] and .peelSent + .act[data-act="open-task"] — notes.seam after pressing [data-act="send"]; src/notes.js (desk meta + peel receipt), src/notes.css (.deskFactLink, .peelSent)
standing.problem: At the one moment that justifies the suite existing, the surface answers once-asked four times. Measured at 1440x960 with no scrolling (document scroll 0), after Send to Tasks the string 'Switch on before guests arrive, not when' is printed three times: .deskFactLink at (815,294) 13px/400 under the eyebrow IN TASKS AS, .peelSent at (272,445) 17px/600 under the eyebrow TASKS HAS IT, and a <b> at (264,667) 15px/400 in the ALREADY IN TASKS row. Two eyebrows name one fact two ways. Two separate controls both carry data-act="open-task" to the same destination, 233px apart — .deskFactLink at y=294 (accessible name 'Open in Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when. Your note stays here.') and .act at y=527 ('Open in Tasks'). The reassurance is doubled too: .peelSent's 'Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit.' repeats the meta link's own 'Your note stays here.' Meanwhile the loudest rendering (17px/600) is the transient receipt and the durable record is the 13px/400 one, so prominence runs backwards. The same flow on a phone renders 2 occurrences and 1 control, which is the right shape — the duplication is desk-only, created by the meta column.
standing.fix: Do it with one guard, not three edits: at src/notes.js:1894 render the 'In Tasks as' .deskFact on `note.sent && !sentTask`, so while the receipt is up the margin row stands down entirely and returns the moment [data-act="close-peel"] clears sentTask — that removes the second printing, the second open-task control and the second reassurance together, and matches the shape the phone already has. Reject parts (a) and (c) of the proposed fix: keep the title in .peelSent (the receipt is where the eye is, and 'Tasks has it' alone names no object), and do not delete a visible sentence on the grounds that an accessible name carries it — that is moving truth out of the visible layer. Companion edit required: the send path deliberately focuses .deskFactLink (documented at src/notes.js:335), so retarget it to the receipt's own [data-act="open-task"] and keep the undo-revert refocus chain working.
standing.verdict: Every measurement checks out at 1280/1440/1920 with document scroll 0: after Send to Tasks the sentence prints at .deskFactLink (815,294) 13px/400 under eyebrow 'In Tasks as', .peelSent (272,445) 17px/600 under 'Tasks has it', and idxText b (264,667) 15px/400 under 'Already in Tasks'; two visible [data-act="open-task"] controls sit 233px apart with different accessible names to the same destination; and the phone renders the correct shape (one report, one control), so the desk meta column creates it. Driving it also shows focus after send landing on the quiet 13px margin link, not on the receipt's own 'Open in Tasks' 543px away — the duplication has a real cost, not just a tidiness one. This is the DISTINCT desk-duplication defect; seam-receipt-over-explains names the same pair from the copy side and adds nothing checkable, and it is a different defect from the card-note stutter that seam-card-repeats-its-own-title/seam-payoff-card-stutters name on the Tasks side.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .card .cardNote in the board view between 1100 and 1279px — the board/list crossing at 1100 (src/tasks.js) and the tray floor (src/tasks.css .tray min/max width)
standing.problem: There is a 180px-wide band where the board is kept and its cards stop saying what to do. Measured on tasks.dense: at 1280 zero of eight card notes are trimmed; at 1279 all eight are, and at 1100 the notes render 18-45 per cent of their text in 196px lanes. 'Add Northlight (photography) and County Marquee. Drop the lapsed DJ.' renders as 'Add Northlight (photography)…' at every width from 1100 to 1279 — the instruction is the part that is gone. 'Top table moved away from the speakers, check sightlines to the arch.' renders 23 per cent at 1180. At 1100 one card title is trimmed as well. The list view that solves it already exists and is switched on 1px lower, at 1099, where the same notes are read whole. Lane width at 1279 is 226px and the note measure 149px — identical to 1280 — so the entire cliff is the `@media (min-width: 1280px)` max-height override at src/tasks.css:946-949, not the lane. standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .tray[data-lane] .trayBody[data-more] and the .tray::after fold rule — src/tasks.css:812-827, set by measureEdges() at src/tasks.js:3761
standing.problem: In the state built to test density, 10 of 32 tasks are hidden and nothing on the sheet says so in words. At 1920x1000 on tasks.dense the To Do scroller runs 195-775 and its fifth card ends at exactly 775, so no card peeks; '+ Add here' sits at 779, four pixels below the cut, in the position that conventionally terminates a list. Five tasks — 'Price the extra hour on the bar for Nora & Cian', 'Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet', 'Pencil the autumn date in the diary', 'Service the terrace heaters before October', 'Replace the two broken chairs in the barn' — are entirely below it. In Progress hides 2 of 7 and Done 3 of 9. The scrollbar gutter is 0px, there is no mask. The two cues are a 1px rule at rgba(17,17,17,0.08) — the identical --line token every card border is drawn in — and the numeral 10 at 11px/400/62 per cent ink, 630px away at the far right of the lane head, which requires Orla to count the visible cards and subtract. The fold rule was chosen over a gradient for a good rendering reason recorded in the CSS; the gap it leaves is that the cue carries no word.

(1) Fix the cue as well as the word: a hairline drawn in the same --line value as every card border cannot read as a cue whatever it says beside it — step the fold to --ink-4, the value the card's own open ring already uses, so it is a different line from the thirty it sits among. (2) Do not add a button. Three lanes gaining a second tab stop in their foot, and 'Add here' pushed a row further down, costs more than it buys; render the residue as quiet non-interactive text in the trayAdd row's own line ('5 more below', 13px/400/62% ink, right-aligned) and let the existing lane scroller and card rover do the moving. Derive the number as lane count minus fully-visible cards from the same accessor the head count uses, and assert it in interaction-check.mjs at 1920 and 1440.
